body.text: āha: kena kāraṇenāyuṣman subhūte evaṃ vadasi? yo rūpasya vyayo na tad rūpaṃ, yo vedanāyā vyayo na sā vedanā, yaḥ saṃjñāyā vyayo na sā saṃjñā, yaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vyayo na te saṃskārāḥ, yo vijñānasya vyayo na tad vijñānam.
body.translated_text: He said: For what reason, O venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do you speak thus? The destruction (<s>vyaya</s>) of form is not that form; the destruction of feeling is not that feeling; the destruction of perception is not that perception; the destruction of formations is not those formations; the destruction of consciousness is not that consciousness.

body.text: yaś cakṣuṣo vyayo na tac cakṣuḥ, yaḥ śrotrasya vyayo na tac chrotraṃ, yo ghrāṇasya vyayo na tad ghrāṇaṃ, yo jihvāyā vyayo na sā jihvā, yaḥ kāyasya vyayo na sa kāyaḥ, yo manaso vyayo na tan manaḥ.
body.translated_text: The destruction of the eye is not that eye; the destruction of the ear is not that ear; the destruction of the nose is not that nose; the destruction of the tongue is not that tongue; the destruction of the body is not that body; the destruction of the mind is not that mind.

body.text: yo rūpasya vyayo na tad rūpaṃ, yaḥ śabdasya vyayo na sa śabdaḥ, yo gandhasya vyayo na sa gandhaḥ, yo rasasya vyayo na sa rasaḥ, yaḥ sparśasya vyayo na sa sparśaḥ, yo dharmāṇāṃ vyayo na te dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: The destruction of visible form is not that visible form; the destruction of sound is not that sound; the destruction of smell is not that smell; the destruction of taste is not that taste; the destruction of tangible objects is not that tangible object; the destruction of mental objects (<s>dharma</s>s) is not those mental objects.

body.text: yaś cakṣurvijñānasya vyayo na tac cakṣurvijñānaṃ, yaḥ śrotravijñānasya vyayo na tac chrotravijñānaṃ, yo ghrāṇavijñanasya vyayo na tad ghrāṇavijñānaṃ, yo jihvāvijñanasya vyayo na taj jihvāvijñānaṃ, yaḥ kāyavijñanasya vyayo na tat kāyavijñānaṃ, yo manovijñānasya vyayo na tan manovijñānam.
body.translated_text: The destruction of eye-consciousness is not that eye-consciousness; the destruction of ear-consciousness is not that ear-consciousness; the destruction of nose-consciousness is not that nose-consciousness; the destruction of tongue-consciousness is not that tongue-consciousness; the destruction of body-consciousness is not that body-consciousness; the destruction of mind-consciousness is not that mind-consciousness.

body.text: yaś cakṣuḥsaṃsparśasya vyayo na sa cakṣuḥsaṃsparśaḥ, yaḥ śrotrasaṃsparśasya vyayo na sa chrotrasaṃsparśaḥ, yo ghrāṇasaṃsparśasya vyayo na sa ghrāṇasaṃsparśaḥ, yo jihvāsaṃsparśasya vyayo na sa jihvāsaṃsparśaḥ, yaḥ kāyasaṃsparśasya vyayo na sa kāyasaṃsparśaḥ, yo manaḥsaṃsparśasya vyayo na sa manaḥsaṃsparśaḥ.
body.translated_text: The destruction of eye-contact is not that eye-contact; the destruction of ear-contact is not that ear-contact; the destruction of nose-contact is not that nose-contact; the destruction of tongue-contact is not that tongue-contact; the destruction of body-contact is not that body-contact; the destruction of mind-contact is not that mind-contact.

body.text: yaś cakṣuḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā vyayo na sā cakṣuḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanā, yaḥ śrotrasaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā vyayo na sā śrotrasaṃsparśapratyayavedanā, yo ghrāṇasaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā vyayo na sā ghrāṇasaṃsparśapratyayavedanā, yo jihvāsaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā vyayo na sā jihvāsaṃsparśapratyayavedanā, yaḥ kāyasaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā vyayo na sā kāyasaṃsparśapratyayavedanā, yo manaḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā vyayo na sā manaḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanā.
body.translated_text: The destruction of feeling conditioned by eye-contact is not that feeling conditioned by eye-contact; the destruction of feeling conditioned by ear-contact is not that feeling conditioned by ear-contact; the destruction of feeling conditioned by nose-contact is not that feeling conditioned by nose-contact; the destruction of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is not that feeling conditioned by tongue-contact; the destruction of feeling conditioned by body-contact is not that feeling conditioned by body-contact; the destruction of feeling conditioned by mind-contact is not that feeling conditioned by mind-contact.

body.text: yaḥ pṛthivīdhātor vyayo na sa pṛthivīdhātuḥ, yo 'bdhātor vyayo na so 'bdhātuḥ, yas tejodhātor vyayo na sa tejodhātuḥ, yo vāyudhātor vyayo na sa vāyudhātuḥ, ya ākāśadhātor vyayo na sa ākāśadhātuḥ, yo vijñānadhātor vyayo na sa vijñānadhātuḥ.
body.translated_text: The destruction of the earth element is not that earth element; the destruction of the water element is not that water element; the destruction of the fire element is not that fire element; the destruction of the wind element is not that wind element; the destruction of the space element is not that space element; the destruction of the consciousness element is not that consciousness element.

body.text: yo 'vidyāyā vyayo na sāvidyā, yaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vyayo na te saṃskārāḥ, yo vijñānasya vyayo na tad vijñānaṃ, yo nāmarūpasya vyayo na tan nāmarūpaṃ, yaḥ ṣaḍāyatanasya vyayo na tat ṣaḍāyatanaṃ, yaḥ sparśasya vyayo na sa sparśaḥ, yo vedanāyā vyayo na sā vedanā, yas tṛṣṇāyā vyayo na sā tṛṣṇā, ya upādānasya vyayo na tad upādānaṃ, yo bhavasya vyayo na sa bhavaḥ, yo jāter vyayo na sā jātiḥ, yo jarāmaraṇasya vyayo na taj jarāmaraṇam.
body.translated_text: The destruction of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is not that ignorance; the destruction of formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is not those formations; the destruction of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is not that consciousness; the destruction of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) is not that name-and-form; the destruction of the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>) is not those six sense-bases; the destruction of contact (<s>sparśa</s>) is not that contact; the destruction of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) is not that feeling; the destruction of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is not that craving; the destruction of clinging (<s>upādāna</s>) is not that clinging; the destruction of existence (<s>bhava</s>) is not that existence; the destruction of birth (<s>jāti</s>) is not that birth; the destruction of aging-and-death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>) is not that aging-and-death.

body.text: yo dānapāramitāyā vyayo na sā dānapāramitā, yaḥ śīlapāramitāyā vyayo na sā śīlapāramitā, yaḥ kṣāntipāramitāyā vyayo na sā kṣāntipāramitā, yo vīryapāramitāyā vyayo na sā vīryapāramitā, yo dhyānapāramitāyā vyayo na sā dhyānapāramitā, yaḥ prajñāpāramitāyā vyayo na sā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: The destruction of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) is not that perfection of giving; the destruction of the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) is not that perfection of morality; the destruction of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) is not that perfection of patience; the destruction of the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) is not that perfection of vigor; the destruction of the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) is not that perfection of meditation; the destruction of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) is not that perfection of wisdom.

body.text: yo 'dhyātmaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sādhyātmaśūnyatā, yo bahirdhāśūnyatāyā vyayo na sā bahirdhāśūnyatā, yo 'dhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatāyā vyayo na sādhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā, yaḥ śūnyatāśūnyatāyā vyayo na sā śūnyatāśūnyatā, yo mahāśūnyatāyā vyayo na sā mahāśūnyatā, yaḥ paramārthaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sā paramārthaśūnyatā, yaḥ saṃskṛtaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sā saṃskṛtaśūnyatā, yo 'saṃskṛtaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sāsaṃskṛtaśūnyatā, yo 'tyantaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sātyantaśūnyatā, yo 'navarāgraśūnyatāyā vyayo na sānavarāgraśūnyatā, yo 'navakāraśūnyatāyā vyayo na sānavakāraśūnyatā, yaḥ prakṛtiśūnyatāyā vyayo na sā prakṛtiśūnyatā, yaḥ sarvadharmaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sā sarvadharmaśūnyatā, yaḥ svalakṣaṇaśūnyatāya vyayo na sā svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā, yo 'nupalambhaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sānupalambhaśūnyatā, yo 'bhāvaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sābhāvaśūnyatā, yaḥ svabhāvaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sā svabhāvaśūnyatā, yo 'bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāyā vyayo na sābhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: The perishing of internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>) is not that internal emptiness; the perishing of external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) is not that external emptiness; the perishing of internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) is not that internal-and-external emptiness; the perishing of the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of emptiness; the perishing of great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>) is not that great emptiness; the perishing of ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>) is not that ultimate emptiness; the perishing of the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of the conditioned; the perishing of the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of the unconditioned; the perishing of the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of the ultimate limit; the perishing of the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of the beginningless and endless; the perishing of the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of non-rejection; the perishing of natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) is not that natural emptiness; the perishing of the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of all dharmas; the perishing of the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of own-characteristics; the perishing of the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of non-apprehension; the perishing of the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of non-existence; the perishing of the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of inherent nature; the perishing of the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) is not that emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature.

body.text: anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yo rūpasya vyayo na tad rūpaṃ, yo vedanāyā vyayo na sā vedanā, yaḥ saṃjñāyā vyayo na sā saṃjñā, yaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vyayo na te saṃskārāḥ, yo vijñānasya vyayo na tad vijñānam.

children.translated_text: ) For indeed, the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) are not other than non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>), non-arising is itself the immeasurables, the immeasurables are themselves non-arising; by this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called 'the immeasurables' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual (<s>advaya</s>). body.text: anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa ya imā ucyante āveṇikabuddhadharmā ity advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā.
body.translated_text: By this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called 'the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual.

body.text: tathā hi nānyat srotaāpattiphalam anyo 'nutpādaḥ, anutpāda eva srotaāpattiphalaṃ srotaāpattiphalam evānutpādaḥ, anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yad etad ucyate śrotraāpattiphalam ity advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā, tathā hi nānyat sakṛdāgāmiphalam anyo 'nutpādaḥ, anutpāda eva sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalam evānutpādaḥ, anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yad etad ucyate sakṛdāgāmiphalam ity advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā, tathā hi nānyad anāgāmiphalam anyo 'nutpādaḥ, anutpāda evānāgāmiphalam anāgāmiphalam evānutpādaḥ, anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yad etad ucyate 'nāgāmiphalam ity advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā, tathā hi nānyad arhattvam anyo 'nutpādaḥ, anutpāda evārhattvam arhattvam evānutpādaḥ, anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yad etad ucyate 'rhattvam ity advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā, tathā hi nānyā pratyekabodhir anyo 'nutpādaḥ, anutpāda eva pratyekabodhiḥ pratyekabodhir evānutpādaḥ, anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yo 'yam ucyate pratyekabodhir ity advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā, tathā hi nānyā sarvajñatānyo 'nutpādaḥ, anutpāda eva sarvajñatā sarvajñataivānutpādaḥ, anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yeyam ucyate sarvajñatety advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā, tathā hi nānyā mārgākārajñatānyo 'nutpādaḥ, anutpāda eva mārgākārajñatā mārgākārajñataivānutpādaḥ, anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yeyam ucyate mārgākārajñatety advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā, tathā hi nānyā sarvākārajñatānyo 'nutpādaḥ, anutpāda eva sarvākārajñatā sarvākārajñataivānutpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: For indeed, the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>) is not other than non-arising, non-arising is itself the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry is itself non-arising; by this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called 'the fruit of stream-entry' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual. For indeed, the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>) is not other than non-arising, non-arising is itself the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning is itself non-arising; by this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called 'the fruit of once-returning' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual. For indeed, the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) is not other than non-arising, non-arising is itself the fruit of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning is itself non-arising; by this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called 'the fruit of non-returning' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual. For indeed, <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhatva</s>) is not other than non-arising, non-arising is itself <s>arhat</s>ship, <s>arhat</s>ship is itself non-arising; by this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called '<s>arhat</s>ship' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual. For indeed, <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>) is not other than non-arising, non-arising is itself <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening, <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening is itself non-arising; by this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called '<s>pratyeka</s>-awakening' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual. For indeed, omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) is not other than non-arising, non-arising is itself omniscience, omniscience is itself non-arising; by this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called 'omniscience' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual. For indeed, the knowledge of path-aspects (<s>mārgākārajñatā</s>) is not other than non-arising, non-arising is itself the knowledge of path-aspects, the knowledge of path-aspects is itself non-arising; by this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called 'the knowledge of path-aspects' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual. For indeed, the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) is not other than non-arising, non-arising is itself the knowledge of all aspects, the knowledge of all aspects is itself non-arising.

body.text: anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa yeyam ucyate sarvākārajñatety advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā.
body.translated_text: By this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called 'the knowledge of all aspects' — this is an enumeration made of the non-dual.

body.text: athāyuṣman subhūtir bhagavantam etad avocat: yasmin samaye bhagavan bodhisattvo mahasattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carann imān dharmān evam upaparīkṣate, tasmin samaye bhagavan rūpasyānutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, vedanāyā anutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, saṃjñāyā anutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, saṃskārāṇām anutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, vijñānasyānutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya.
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: At the time when, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) examines these <s>dharma</s>s in this way, at that time, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, he sees the non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>) of form on account of its ultimate purity (<s>atyantaviśuddhi</s>); he sees the non-arising of feeling on account of its ultimate purity; he sees the non-arising of perception on account of its ultimate purity; he sees the non-arising of formations on account of their ultimate purity; he sees the non-arising of consciousness on account of its ultimate purity.

body.text: cakṣuṣo 'nutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, śrotrasyānutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, ghrāṇasyānutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, jihvāyā anutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, kāyasyānutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya, manaso 'nutpādaṃ paśyaty atyantaviśuddhitām upādāya.
body.translated_text: He sees the non-arising of the eye on account of its ultimate purity; he sees the non-arising of the ear on account of its ultimate purity; he sees the non-arising of the nose on account of its ultimate purity; he sees the non-arising of the tongue on account of its ultimate purity; he sees the non-arising of the body on account of its ultimate purity; he sees the non-arising of the mind on account of its ultimate purity.

A <s>Buddha</s> too is non-arising; the dharmas of a <s>Buddha</s> too are non-arising. Yet it is attained: by those of the <s>śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and <s>arhat</s>ship are indeed attained; by those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening is indeed attained; by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the knowledge of all aspects — there will be no division of the five destinies — the fivefold awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is indeed attained by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: yady āyuṣman subhūte sarvadharmā anutpādaḥ, kiṃ kāraṇaṃ srotaāpannena trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāya mārgo bhāvitaḥ, sakṛdāgāminā rāgadveṣamohānāṃ tanutvāya mārgo bhāvitaḥ, anāgāminā pañcānām avarabhāgīyāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāya mārgo bhāvitaḥ, arhatā pañcānāṃ mūrdhabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāya mārgo bhāvitaḥ, pratyekabuddhayānikaiḥ pratyekabodhaye mārgo bhāvitaḥ? kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo duṣkaracaryāñ carati yad duḥkhāni sattvānāṃ kṛtane pratyanubhavati? kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tathāgatenānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddhā, kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tathāgatena dharmacakraṃ pravartitam?
body.translated_text: If, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, all dharmas are non-arising, for what reason has the path been cultivated by the stream-enterer for the abandonment of the three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>)? For what reason has the path been cultivated by the once-returner for the attenuation of passion, hatred, and delusion? For what reason has the path been cultivated by the non-returner for the abandonment of the five lower fetters? For what reason has the path been cultivated by the <s>arhat</s> for the abandonment of the five higher fetters? For what reason has the path been cultivated by those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle for <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening? For what reason does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practice difficult austerities, enduring sufferings for the sake of beings? For what reason has the <s>Tathāgata</s> fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)? For what reason has the <s>Tathāgata</s> turned the wheel of the Dharma (<s>dharmacakra</s>)?

body.text: evam ukte āyuṣmān subhūtir āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputram etad avocat: nāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpādasya dharmasya prāptim icchāmi na samayaṃ cānutpādasya srotaāpattitvam icchāmi, srotaāpattiphalaṃ nānutpādasya sakṛdāgāmitvam icchāmi, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ nānutpādasyānāgāmitvam icchāmi nānāgāmiphalaṃ nānutpādasyārhattvam icchāmi nārhattvasākṣātkriyāṃ, nānutpādasya pratyekabuddhatvam icchāmi na pratyekabodhir nāpy aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrecchāmi yo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo duṣkaracaryāṃ caran nāpi bodhisattvo mahāsattvo duṣkarasaṃjñayā carati. tat kasya hetoḥ? na hy āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra duḥkhasaṃjñāṃ janayitvāśakyam aprameyāṇām asaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānām arthaṃ kartum api tv āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra sarvattveyumātṛsaṃjñā janayitvā pitṛsaṃjñāṃ janayitvā putrasaṃjñā janayitvāsakyam aprameyāṇām asaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānām arthakartun tac cānupalambhayogena evaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena cittam utpādayitavyaṃ, yathātmātmeti cocyate sa ca sarveṇa sarvathā sarvaṃ na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate.
body.translated_text: When this was said, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wish for the attainment of a non-arising dharma, nor do I wish for the occasion of stream-entry of the non-arising, nor for the fruit of stream-entry, nor do I wish for the state of once-returning of the non-arising, nor the fruit of once-returning, nor do I wish for the state of non-returning of the non-arising, nor the fruit of non-returning, nor do I wish for <s>arhat</s>ship of the non-arising, nor the direct realization of <s>arhat</s>ship, nor do I wish for <s>pratyekabuddha</s>hood of the non-arising, nor <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening. Nor, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, do I wish that the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should practice difficult austerities, nor does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practice with the notion of difficulty. For what reason? For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, having generated the notion of suffering, one is unable to benefit immeasurable, innumerable beings. But rather, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, having generated the notion that all beings are one's mother, having generated the notion that they are one's father, having generated the notion that they are one's children — one is able to benefit immeasurable, innumerable beings. And this should be done through the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>). Thus the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should generate the mind, for that which is called 'self' — that in every way and in all respects is entirely not found, not apprehended.

body.text: evam adhyātmikabāhyeṣu dharmeṣu saṃjñotpādayitavyā, saced evaṃ saṃjñām utpādayitavyeti duṣkarasaṃjñām utpadayiṣyati. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi na sa kaccit tad dharmam utpādayati nopalabhyate nāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpāde tathāgatam icchāmi nānuttarā saṃyaksaṃbodhir yathā tathāgatena dharmacakraṃ pravartitaṃ na hy anutpannena dharmeṇa prāptiḥ prāpyate.
body.translated_text: Thus should the notion be generated regarding internal and external dharmas. If one should generate such a notion, one will not generate the notion of difficulty. For what reason? For indeed, no one at all produces that dharma — it is not found, not apprehended. Nor do I, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wish for the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the non-arising, nor for unsurpassed perfect awakening, nor for the turning of the wheel of the Dharma by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; for indeed, by a non-arising dharma, attainment is not attained.

body.text: āha: kim punas tvam āyuṣman subhūte utpannena dharmeṇa prāptim icchasi? athānutpannena dharmeṇa prāpyamāṇam?
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: But do you, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, wish for attainment through an arisen dharma? Or is it being attained through a non-arisen dharma?

body.text: subhūtir āha: nāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrotpānnena dharmeṇa prāptim icchāmi nāpy anutpannena dharmeṇa prāpyamāṇām.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wish for attainment through an arisen dharma, nor for what is being attained through a non-arisen dharma.

body.text: āha: kiṃ punar āyuṣman subhūte nāsti prāptir nāsty abhisamayaḥ.
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is there no attainment and no realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>)?

body.text: subhūtir āha: asty āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra prāptir asty abhisamayo na punaḥ paramārthena dharmeṇa.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: There is, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, attainment, and there is realization — but not in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārtha</s>).

body.text: api tu khalu punar āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra lokavyavahāreṇa prāptir abhisamayo vā prajñāpyate lokavyavahāreṇa srotaāpanno vā sakṛdāgāmī vā nāgāmī vārhattvaṃ vā pratyekabuddho vā bodhisattvo vā prajñayate. na punaḥ paramārthena prāptir vābhisamayo vā srotaāpanno vā (

children.text: ) sakṛdāgāmī vānāgāmī vārhattvaṃ vā pratyekabuddho vā bodhisattvo vā buddho vā prajñapyate.
children.translated_text: a once-returner, nor a non-returner, nor <s>arhat</s>ship, nor a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, nor a <s>bodhisattva</s>, nor a <s>Buddha</s> is designated.

body.translated_text: Rather, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is through worldly convention (<s>lokavyavahāra</s>) that attainment or realization is designated; through worldly convention a stream-enterer, or a once-returner, or a non-returner, or <s>arhat</s>ship, or a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, or a <s>bodhisattva</s> is designated. But in the ultimate sense, neither attainment nor realization, neither a stream-enterer nor

body.text: āha: kiṃ punar āyuṣman subhūte yathaiva lokavyavahāreṇa prāptiś cābhisamayaś ca tathaiva pañcānāṃ gatīnāṃ lokavyavahāreṇa bhedo na punaḥ paramārthena?
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, just as attainment and realization exist through worldly convention, is the division of the five destinies (<s>gati</s>) likewise through worldly convention and not in the ultimate sense?

body.text: āha: evam etad āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra yathaiva lokavyavahāreṇa prāptiś cābhisamayaś ca tathaiva pañcānāṃ gatīnāṃ lokavyavahāreṇa bhedo na punaḥ paramārthena. tat kasya hetoḥ? na hy āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paramārtheṇa karmaṇaḥ karamavipākaḥ, notpādo na nirodho na saṃkleśo na vyavadānaḥ.
body.translated_text: He (<s>Subhūti</s>) said: Just so, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>. Just as attainment and realization exist through worldly convention, likewise the division of the five destinies is through worldly convention and not in the ultimate sense. For what reason? For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, in the ultimate sense there is no ripening of action (<s>karmavipāka</s>), no arising, no cessation, no defilement, and no purification.

body.text: āha: kiṃ punar āyuṣman subhūte 'nutpanno dharma utpadyate, atha votpanno dharma utpadyate?
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does a non-arisen dharma arise, or does an arisen dharma arise?

body.text: subhūtir āha: nāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya dharmasyotpādam icchāmi.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wish for the arising of a non-arisen dharma.

body.text: āha: katamasyāyuṣman subhūte anutpannasya dharmasyotpādaṃ necchasi?
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: Of which non-arisen dharma, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do you not wish for the arising?

body.text: subhūtir āha: rūpasyāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, vedanāyā āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, saṃjñāyā āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, saṃskārāṇām āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, vijñānasyāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wish for the arising of form, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnya</s>). I do not wish for the arising of feeling, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of perception, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of formations, which are non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of consciousness, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature.

body.text: cakṣuṣo 'ham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, śrotrasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, ghrāṇasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, jihvāyā aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, kāyasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, manaso 'ham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi.
body.translated_text: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wish for the arising of the eye, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of the ear, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of the nose, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of the tongue, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of the body, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of the mind, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature.

body.text: rūpasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, śabdasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, gandhasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya (

children.text: ) svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, rasasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, sparśasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, dharmānām aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi.
children.translated_text: — I do not wish for the arising of taste, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of tangible objects, which are non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of <s>dharma</s>s (mental objects), which are non-arisen and empty of inherent nature.

body.translated_text: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wish for the arising of visible form, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of sound, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of smell, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature —

body.text: cakṣurvijñānasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, śrotravijñānasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, ghrāṇavijñānasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, jihvāvijñānasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, kāyavijñānasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, manovijñānasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi.
body.translated_text: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wish for the arising of eye-consciousness, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of ear-consciousness, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of body-consciousness, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature. I do not wish for the arising of mind-consciousness, which is non-arisen and empty of inherent nature.

body.text: cakṣuḥsaṃsparśasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, śrotrasaṃsparśasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, ghrāṇasaṃsparśasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, jihvāsaṃsparśasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, kāyasaṃsparśasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, manaḥsaṃsparśasyāham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi.
body.translated_text: I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of eye-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnya</s>); I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of ear-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of nose-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of tongue-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of body-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of mind-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature.

body.text: cakṣuḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, śrotrasaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, ghrāṇasaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, jihvāsaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, kāyasaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, manaḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanāyā aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi.
body.translated_text: I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of feeling conditioned by eye-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of feeling conditioned by ear-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of feeling conditioned by nose-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of feeling conditioned by body-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature; I do not wish, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the arising of feeling conditioned by mind-contact which is unarisen and empty of inherent nature.

body.text: pṛthivīdhātor aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, abdhātor aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya (

children.text: ) svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, tejodhātor aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, vāyudhātor aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, ākāśadhātor aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi, vijñānadhātor aham āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrānutpannasya svabhāvaśūnyasyotpādaṃ necchāmi.

body.text: śāradvatīputra āha: kiṃ punar āyuṣman subhūte utpāda utpadyate? athānutpāda utpadyate?
body.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does arising (<s>utpāda</s>) arise? Or does non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>) arise?

body.text: āha: na hy āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrotpāda utpadyate, nānutpāda utpadyate. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra yaś cotpādo yaś cānutpāda ubhāv etau dharmau na saṃyuktau na visaṃyuktāv arūpiṇāv anidarśanāv apratighāv ekalakṣaṇo yad utālakṣaṇaḥ. tad anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa notpāda utpadyate, nānutpāda utpadyate.
body.translated_text: He replied: Indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, arising does not arise, nor does non-arising arise. For what reason? For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is arising and that which is non-arising — both these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, undemonstrable, non-resistant, of one characteristic, namely characteristiclessness. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, arising does not arise, nor does non-arising arise.

body.text: śāradvatīputra āha: anutpanno dharmo 'nutpanno dharma ity āyuṣman subhūte pratibhāti te mantrayitum, anutpannānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādo hy āyuṣman subhūte pratibhāti mantrayitum.
body.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: 'An unarisen dharma, an unarisen dharma' — Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does it occur to you to speak thus? Does it occur to you, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, to speak of the non-arising of unarisen dharmas?

children.text: ) chāradvatīputra yac ca pratibhāti te mantrayitum iti, anutpanno dharmo 'nutpanno dharma ity āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra na me pratibhāti mantrayitum, anutpannānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādo 'pi me āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra na pratibhāti mantrayitum. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra yaś cānutpanno dharmo yaś cānutpādo yac ca pratibhānaṃ ye ca mantrā yā cānutpattiḥ sarvadharmā ete na saṃyuktā na visaṃyuktā arūpiṇo 'nidarśanā apratighā avijñaptikā ekalakṣaṇā yad utālakṣaṇāḥ.
children.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which you say 'does it occur to you to speak thus' — 'an unarisen dharma, an unarisen dharma,' Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it does not occur to me to speak thus; nor does the non-arising of unarisen dharmas, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, occur to me to speak of. For what reason? For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is an unarisen dharma, that which is non-arising, that which is eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>), that which is speech (<s>mantra</s>), and that which is non-production — all these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, undemonstrable, non-resistant, inexpressible, of one characteristic, namely characteristiclessness.

body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'An unarisen dharma, an unarisen dharma' — Venerable

body.text: āha: anutpāda ity āyuṣman subhūte mantraḥ, anutpādaṃ pratibhānaṃ, anutpādo dharmaḥ, te 'pi dharmā anutpādā yāṃs tān ārabhya pratibhāti mantrayitum.
body.translated_text: He said: 'Non-arising' — Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, this is speech (<s>mantra</s>); non-arising is eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>); non-arising is a dharma; and those dharmas too are non-arising, concerning which it occurs to you to speak.

body.text: subhūtir āha: evam etad āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra anutpādo mantro 'nutpādaḥ pratibhāno 'nutpādo dharmaḥ, te 'pi dharmā anutpādā yāṃs tān ārabhya pratibhāti mantrayitum. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra rūpam anutpādo vedanānutpādaḥ saṃjñānutpādaḥ saṃskārānutpādo vijñānam anutpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: So it is, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>; non-arising is speech, non-arising is eloquence, non-arising is a dharma, and those dharmas too are non-arising concerning which it occurs to one to speak. For what reason? For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, form is non-arising; feeling is non-arising; perception is non-arising; formations are non-arising; consciousness is non-arising.

body.text: cakṣur anutpādaḥ śrotram anutpādo ghrāṇam anutpādo jihvānutpādaḥ kāyo 'nutpādo mano 'nutpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: The eye is non-arising; the ear is non-arising; the nose is non-arising; the tongue is non-arising; the body is non-arising; the mind is non-arising.

body.text: rūpam anutpādaḥ śabdo 'nutpādo gandho 'nutpādo raso 'nutpādaḥ sparśo 'nutpādo dharmā anutpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: Visible form is non-arising; sound is non-arising; smell is non-arising; taste is non-arising; tangible objects are non-arising; mental objects (<s>dharma</s>) are non-arising.

body.text: cakṣurvijñānam anutpādaḥ, śrotravijñānam anutpādo ghrāṇavijñānam anutpādo jihvāvijñānam anutpādaḥ kāyavijñānam anutpādo manovijñānam anutpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: Eye-consciousness is non-arising; ear-consciousness is non-arising; nose-consciousness is non-arising; tongue-consciousness is non-arising; body-consciousness is non-arising; mind-consciousness is non-arising.

body.text: cakṣuḥsaṃsparśo 'nutpādaḥ śrotrasaṃsparśo 'nutpādo ghrāṇasaṃsparśo 'nutpādo jihvāsaṃsparśo 'nutpādaḥ kāyasaṃsparśo 'nutpādo manaḥsaṃsparśo 'nutpādaḥ.

body.text: cakṣuḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanānutpādaḥ śrotrasaṃsparśapratyayavedanānutpādo ghrāṇasaṃsparśapratyayavedanānutpādo jihvāsaṃsparśapratyayavedanānutpādaḥ kāyasaṃsparśapratyayavedanānutpādo manaḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanānutpādaḥ.

body.text: pṛthivīdhātur anutpādo 'bdhātur anutpādaḥ tejodhātur anutpādo vāyudhātur anutpāda ākāśadhātur anutpādo vijñānadhātur anutpādaḥ.

body.text: avidyānutpādaḥ saṃskārā anutpādo vijñānam anutpādo nāmarūpam anutpādaḥ ṣaḍāyatanam anutpādaḥ sparśo 'nutpādo vedanānutpādaḥ tṛṣṇānutpāda upādānam anutpādo bhavo 'nutpādo jātir anutpādo jarāmaraṇam anutpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is non-arising; formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are non-arising; consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is non-arising; name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) is non-arising; the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>) are non-arising; contact (<s>sparśa</s>) is non-arising; feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) is non-arising; craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is non-arising; clinging (<s>upādāna</s>) is non-arising; existence (<s>bhava</s>) is non-arising; birth (<s>jāti</s>) is non-arising; aging-and-death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>) is non-arising.

body.text: dānapāramitānutpādaḥ śīlapāramitānutpādaḥ kṣāntipāramitānutpādo vīryapāramitānutpādo dhyānapāramitānutpādaḥ prajñāpāramitānutpādaḥ.

body.text: adhyātmaśūnyatānutpādo bahirdhāśūnyatānutpādo 'dhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatānutpādaḥ śūnyatāśūnyatānutpādo mahāśūnyatānutpādaḥ paramārthaśūnyatānutpādaḥ saṃskṛtaśūnyatānutpādo 'saṃskṛtaśūnyatānutpādo 'tyantaśūnyatānutpādo 'navarāgraśūnyatānutpādo 'navakāraśūnyatānutpādaḥ prakṛtiśūnyatānutpādaḥ sarvadharmaśūnyatānutpādaḥ svalakṣaṇaśūnyatānutpādo 'nupalambhaśūnyatānutpādo 'bhāvaśūnyatānutpādaḥ svabhāvaśūnyatānutpādo 'bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatānutpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: Internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising; the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) is non-arising.

body.text: smṛtyupasthānāny anutpādaḥ samyakprahāṇāny anutpāda ṛddhipādā anutpādaḥ indriyāṇy anutpādo balāny anutpādo bodhyaṅgāny anutpāda āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgo 'nutpāda āryasatyāny anutpādo dhyānāny anutpādo 'pramāṇāny anutpāda ārūpyasamāpattayo 'nutpādo vimokṣānutpādo 'nupūrvavihārasamāpattayo 'nutpādaḥ,
body.translated_text: The foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) are non-arising; the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) are non-arising; the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) are non-arising; the faculties (<s>indriya</s>) are non-arising; the powers (<s>bala</s>) are non-arising; the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) are non-arising; the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>) is non-arising; the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>) are non-arising; the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>) are non-arising; the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) are non-arising; the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) are non-arising; the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) are non-arising; the successive meditative attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>) are non-arising;

body.text: śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāny anutpādo 'bhijñānutpādaḥ, samādhayo 'nutpādo dhāraṇīmukhāny anutpādaḥ tathāgatabalāny anutpādo vaiśāradyāny anutpādaḥ pratisaṃvido 'nutpādo mahāmaitry anutpādo mahākaruṇānutpāda āveṇikabuddhadharmā anutpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>) — are non-arising; the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) are non-arising; the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>) are non-arising; the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>) are non-arising; the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>) are non-arising; the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) are non-arising; the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) are non-arising; great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) is non-arising; great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) is non-arising; the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>) are non-arising.

body.text: srotaāpattiphalam anutpādaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalam anutpādo 'nāgāmiphalam anutpādo 'rhattvam anutpādaḥ pratyekabodhir anutpādaḥ, sarvajñatānutpādo mārgākārajñatānutpādaḥ sarvākārajñatānutpādaḥ,
body.translated_text: The fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>) is non-arising; the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>) is non-arising; the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) is non-arising; <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhatva</s>) is non-arising; <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>) is non-arising; omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) is non-arising; the knowledge of path-aspects (<s>mārgākārajñatā</s>) is non-arising; the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) is non-arising.

body.text: anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇānutpādo mantro 'nutpādaṃ pratibhānam anutpādo dharmaḥ, te 'pi dharmā anutpādā yāṃs tān ārabhya pratibhāti mantrayitum.
body.translated_text: By this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, non-arising is speech, non-arising is eloquence, non-arising is a dharma, and those dharmas too are non-arising concerning which it occurs to one to speak.

body.text: āha: dharmakathikānām agratāyām ayam āyuṣman subhūtiḥ sthāpayitavyaḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi subhūtiḥ sthaviro yato yata eva paripṛcchyate tatas tata eva niḥsarati.
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: This Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> should be placed foremost among the expounders of the <s>Dharma</s>. For what reason? For indeed, the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, from wherever he is questioned, from there he emerges.

body.text: subhūtir āha: dharmataiṣāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bhagavataḥ śrāvakānām aniśritānāṃ sarvadharmeṣu te yato yata eva paripṛcchyante (

children.text: ) tatas tata eva niḥsaranti. tat kasya hetoḥ? yathāpi tad aniśritatvāt sarvadharmāṇām.
children.translated_text: from there they emerge. For what reason? Because indeed all dharmas are unattached.

body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: This is the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for the disciples (<s>śrāvaka</s>) of the <s>Bhagavat</s> who are unattached to all dharmas — from wherever they are questioned,

body.text: āha: katham āyuṣman subhūte 'niśritāḥ sarvadharmāḥ?
body.translated_text: He said: How, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are all dharmas unattached?

body.text: subhūtir āha: rūpam āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra prakṛtiśūnyaṃ tan nādhyātmaniśritaṃ na bahirdhāniśritaṃ nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate, vedanāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra prakṛtiśūnyā sā nādhyātmaniśritā na bahirdhāniśritā nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate, saṃjñāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra prakṛtiśūnyā sā nādhyātmaniśritā na bahirdhāniśritā nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate, saṃskārā āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra prakṛtiśūnyās te nādhyātmaniśritā na bahirdhāniśritā nobhayam antreṇopalabhyate, vijñānam āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra prakṛtiśūnyaṃ taṃ nādhyātmaniśritaṃ na bahirdhāniśritaṃ nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate.

Consciousness, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is empty by nature; it is not attached internally, not attached externally, and is not apprehended in between either.

body.text: anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa sarvadharmā aniśritāḥ prakṛtiśūnyām upādāya.

body.translated_text: Internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified; the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) should be purified.

body.text: smṛtyupasthānāni pariśodhayitavyāni, samyakprahāṇāni pariśodhayitavyāni, ṛddhipādāḥ pariśodhayitavyāḥ, indriyāṇi pariśodhayitavyāni, balāni pariśodhayitavyāni, bodhyaṅgāni pariśodhayitavyāni, āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ pariśodhayitavyaḥ, āryasatyāni pariśodhayitavyāni, dhyānāni pariśodhayitavyāni, apramāṇāni pariśodhayitavyāni, ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ pariśodhayitavyāḥ, vimokṣāḥ pariśodhayitavāḥ, navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ, śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāni pariśodhayitavyāni, abhijñāḥ pariśodhayitavāḥ, samādhayaḥ pariśodhayitavāḥ, dhāraṇīmukhāni pariśodhayitavyāni, tathāgatabalāni pariśodhayitavyāni, vaiśāradyāni pariśodhayitavyāni, pratisaṃvidaḥ pariśodhayitavyaḥ, mahāmaitrī pariśodhayitavyā, mahākaruṇā pariśodhayitavyā, āveṇikabuddhadharmāḥ pariśodhayitavyāḥ, sarvajñatā pariśodhayitavyā, mārgākārajñatā pariśodhayitavyā, sarvākārajñatā pariśodhayitavyā.
body.translated_text: The foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) should be purified; the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) should be purified; the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) should be purified; the faculties (<s>indriya</s>) should be purified; the powers (<s>bala</s>) should be purified; the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) should be purified; the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>) should be purified; the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>) should be purified; the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>) should be purified; the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) should be purified; the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) should be purified; the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) should be purified; the nine successive meditative attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>) should be purified; the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>) — should be purified; the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) should be purified; the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>) should be purified; the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>) should be purified; the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>) should be purified; the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) should be purified; the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) should be purified; great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) should be purified; great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) should be purified; the exclusive qualities of a Buddha (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>) should be purified; omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) should be purified; the knowledge of the path-aspects (<s>mārgākārajñatā</s>) should be purified; the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) should be purified.

body.text: athāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra punar āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtim etad avocat: katham āyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu caran bodhimārgaṃ pariśodhayati?
body.translated_text: Then Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> again said to Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: How, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, practicing the six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), purify the path to awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>)?

body.text: subhūtir āha: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra dānapāramitā laukiky asti (

children.text: ) lokottarāsti, śīlapāramitā laukiky asti lokottarāsti, kṣāntipāramitā laukiky asti lokottarāsti, vīryapāramitā laukiky asti lokottarāsti, dhyānapāramitā laukiky asti lokottarāsti, prajñāpāramitā laukiky asti lokottarāsti.
children.translated_text: and supramundane (<s>lokottarā</s>). The perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) is worldly and supramundane. The perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) is worldly and supramundane. The perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) is worldly and supramundane. The perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) is worldly and supramundane. The perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) is worldly and supramundane.

body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) is twofold: worldly (<s>laukikī</s>)

body.text: āha: katamāyuṣman subhūte dānapāramitā laukikī katamā lokottarā?
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: Which, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is the worldly perfection of giving, and which is the supramundane?

body.text: subhūtir āha: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dātā bhavati dānapatiḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakāyācanakebhyaḥ, annam annārthikebhyaḥ pānaṃ pānārthikebhyo yānaṃ yānārthikebhyo vastraṃ vastrārthikebhyaḥ puṣpaṃ puṣpārthikebhyo mālyaṃ mālyārthikebhyo gandhaṃ gandhārthikebhyo vilepanaṃ vilepanārthikebhya upāśrayam upāśrayārthikebhya śayyāsanaṃ śayyāsanārthikebhya upakaraṇam upakaraṇārthikebhyo bhaiṣajyaṃ bhaiṣajyārthikebhyaḥ, yāvad anyatarānyatarā mānuṣyakāpariṣkārān dadāti putrārthikebhyaḥ putraṃ dadāti duhitṛkārthikebhyo duhitṛn dadāti bhāryārthikebhyo bhāryāṃ dadāti rājyārthikebhyo rājyaṃ dadāti, śiro'rthikebhyaḥ śiro dadāti, nayanārthikebhyo nayanaṃ dadāti, aṅgapratyaṅgārthikebhyo 'ṅgaṃ dadāti, māṃsaśoṇitamajjārthikebhyo māṃsaśoṇitamajjān dadāti, tac ca saṃniśritaḥ parityajati tasyaivaṃ bhavati, ahaṃ dadāmy eṣa pratigrhṇāti, idaṃ dānam ahaṃ dātā, ahaṃ dānapatir ahaṃ sarvāstiparityāgī, ahaṃ buddhājñāṃ karomi, ahaṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ carāmi, tac ca dānaṃ datvopalambhayogena sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty anena me dānaphalenaite sattvā dṛṣṭa eva dharme sukhitā bhavantv anupādāya ca parinirvāntv iti, sa triṣu saṃyogeṣu saktas tad dānaṃ dadāti, katameṣu triṣu? yad utātmasaṃjñāyāṃ parasaṃjñāyāṃ dānasaṃjñāyām eṣu triṣu saṃyogeṣu sakto dānaṃ dadāti. iyam ucyate laukikī dānapāramitā. kena kāraṇenocyate laukikī dānapāramiteti? tathā hi lokato na carati noccarati, na ca saṃkrāmati tenocyate laukikī dānapāramitā.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> becomes a giver, a lord of giving, to ascetics, brahmins, the destitute, travelers, and beggars — giving food to those who seek food, drink to those who seek drink, vehicles to those who seek vehicles, clothing to those who seek clothing, flowers to those who seek flowers, garlands to those who seek garlands, perfume to those who seek perfume, ointment to those who seek ointment, shelter to those who seek shelter, bedding and seats to those who seek bedding and seats, requisites to those who seek requisites, medicine to those who seek medicine, and even various human accoutrements; he gives sons to those who seek sons, daughters to those who seek daughters, a wife to those who seek a wife, a kingdom to those who seek a kingdom; he gives his head to those who seek a head, his eyes to those who seek eyes, his limbs to those who seek limbs, his flesh, blood, and marrow to those who seek flesh, blood, and marrow. And he gives all this with attachment, thinking: 'I give, this person receives, this is the gift, I am the giver, I am the lord of giving, I renounce all possessions, I carry out the <s>Buddha</s>'s command, I practice the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>).' And having given that gift through the method of apprehension (<s>upalambhayoga</s>), he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) in common with all beings, thinking: 'By this fruit of my giving, may these beings be happy in this very life and may they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging.' He gives that gift while attached to three bonds (<s>saṃyoga</s>). Which three? Namely, the notion of self (<s>ātmasaṃjñā</s>), the notion of other (<s>parasaṃjñā</s>), and the notion of giving (<s>dānasaṃjñā</s>) — attached to these three bonds he gives. This is called the worldly perfection of giving (<s>laukikī dānapāramitā</s>). For what reason is it called the worldly perfection of giving? Because it does not go beyond, does not transcend, and does not cross over from the world — therefore it is called worldly.

body.text: tatra katamā lokottarā dānapāramitā? yad uta trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ.
body.translated_text: What then is the supramundane perfection of giving (<s>lokottarā dānapāramitā</s>)? It is the purity of the three circles (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ?
body.translated_text: What then is the purity of the three circles?

body.text: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvas tad dānaṃ dadann ātmānaṃ nopalabhyate pratigrāhakaṃ nopalabhyate dānaṃ nopalabhyate vipākañ (

children.text: ) ca nābhinandati. iyam āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ.
children.translated_text: ). This, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is the purity of the three circles of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.translated_text: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, while giving that gift, does not apprehend a self, does not apprehend a recipient, does not apprehend a gift, and does not rejoice in the ripening (

body.text: punar aparam āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra dānaṃ dadāti sarvasattvebhyaś ca tad dānaṃ niryātayati tāṃś ca sattvān nopalabhyate, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty api ca nimittaṃ na samanupaśyati. iyam ucyate āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra lokottarā dānapāramitā. kena kāraṇenocyate lokottarā dānapāramiteti? tathā hi lokottareti lokā carati saṃkrāmati tenocyate lokottarā dānapāramiteti.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, he gives the gift and dedicates that gift to all beings, yet does not apprehend those beings; he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening, yet does not perceive any sign (<s>nimitta</s>). This is called the supramundane perfection of giving (<s>lokottarā dānapāramitā</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>. For what reason is it called supramundane? Because it goes beyond, transcends, and crosses over from the world — therefore it is called supramundane.

body.text: asty āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra śīlapāramitā laukiky asti lokottarā.
body.translated_text: There is, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a worldly perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) and a supramundane one.

body.text: tatra katamā laukikī śīlapāramitā?
body.translated_text: What then is the worldly perfection of morality?

body.text: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsatvaḥ śīlaṃ rakṣati tac ca saṃniśrito bhavati tasyaivaṃ bhavaty aham śīlaṃ rakṣāmi sattvānām arthāya. idam śīlam ahaṃ buddhājñāṃ karomi tac ca śīlaṃ rakṣann upalambhayogena sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty anena me śīlaphalenaite sattvā dṛṣṭa eva dharmeṣu sukhino bhavantv anupādāya ca parinirvāntv iti. sa triṣu saṃjñeṣu saktas tac chīlaṃ rakṣati yad utātmasaṃjñāyāṃ parasaṃjñāyāṃ śīlasaṃjñāyām iyam ucyate laukikī śīlapāramiteti. tathā hi lokato na carati noccarati na saṃkrāmati tad ucyate laukikīti.
body.translated_text: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> guards morality (<s>śīla</s>), and does so with attachment, thinking: 'I guard morality for the benefit of beings. This is morality; I carry out the <s>Buddha</s>'s command.' And while guarding that morality, through the method of apprehension, he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening in common with all beings, thinking: 'By this fruit of morality, may these beings be happy in this very life and may they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging.' He guards that morality while attached to three notions — namely, the notion of self, the notion of other, and the notion of morality. This is called the worldly perfection of morality. Because it does not go beyond, does not transcend, and does not cross over from the world — it is called worldly.

body.text: tatra katamā lokottarā śīlapāramitā? yad uta trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ.
body.translated_text: What then is the supramundane perfection of morality? It is the purity of the three circles.

body.text: tatra katamā trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ?
body.translated_text: What then is the purity of the three circles?

body.text: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsatvaḥ śīlaṃ rakṣann ātmānaṃ nopalabhyate sattvān nopalabhyate śīlaṃ nopalabhyate vipākaṃ nābhinandati sarvasattvebhyaś ca tac chīlaṃ niryātayati. tāṃś ca sattvān nopalabhyate 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty api ca nimittaṃ na samanupaśyatīyam ucyate lokottarā śīlapāramitā tathā hi lokā carati uccarati saṃkrāmati tad ucyate lokottareti.
body.translated_text: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while guarding morality, does not apprehend a self, does not apprehend beings, does not apprehend morality, and does not rejoice in the ripening. He dedicates that morality to all beings, yet does not apprehend those beings; he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening, yet does not perceive any sign. This is called the supramundane perfection of morality. Because it goes beyond, transcends, and crosses over from the world — it is called supramundane.

body.text: asty āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra kṣāntipāramitā laukiky asti lokottarā.

body.text: asty āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra vīryapāramitā laukiky asti lokottarā.
body.translated_text: There is, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a worldly perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) and a supramundane one.

body.text: tatra katamā laukikī vīryapāramitā?
body.translated_text: What then is the worldly perfection of vigor?

body.text: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsatvo vīryam ārabhate, tac ca saṃniśrita ārabhate tasyaivaṃ bhavaty ahaṃ vīryam ārabhate sarvasattvānām arthāya, ayaṃ kāya idaṃ cittam idaṃ vīryam ahaṃ buddhājñāṃ karomy ahaṃ vīryapāramitāyāñ carāmi tac ca vīryam upalambhayogena sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarayāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati, anena me vīryaphalenaite sattvā dṛṣṭa eva dharmasukhino bhavatv anupādāya ca parinirvāntv iti. sa triṣu saṃjñeṣu saktas taṃ vīryam ārabhate, yad utātmasaṃjñāyāṃ parasaṃjñāyāṃ vīryasaṃjñāyām iyam ucyate laukikī vīryapāramiteti. tathā hi kokato na carati noccarati na saṃkrāmati tad ucyate laukikīti.
body.translated_text: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> exerts vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), and does so with attachment, thinking: 'I exert vigor for the benefit of all beings. This body, this mind, this vigor — I carry out the <s>Buddha</s>'s command, I practice the perfection of vigor.' And through the method of apprehension, he dedicates that vigor to unsurpassed perfect awakening in common with all beings, thinking: 'By this fruit of vigor, may these beings be happy in this very life and may they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging.' He exerts that vigor while attached to three notions — namely, the notion of self, the notion of other, and the notion of vigor. This is called the worldly perfection of vigor. Because it does not go beyond, does not transcend, and does not cross over from the world — it is called worldly.

body.text: tatra katamā lokottarā vīryapāramitā? yad uta trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ.

body.text: asty āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra dhyānapāramitā laukiky asti lokottarā.
body.translated_text: There is, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a worldly perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) and a supramundane one.

body.text: tatra katamā laukikī dhyānapāramitā?
body.translated_text: What then is the worldly perfection of meditation?

body.text: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsatvo dhyānaṃ samāpadyate, tac ca saṃniśritaḥ samāpadyate tasyaivaṃ bhavaty ahaṃ dhyānāni samāpadyate sarvasattvānām arthāya, imāni dhyānāni, ahaṃ buddhājñāṃ karomi tac ca dhyānaṃ samāpadyamāna upalambhayogena sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty anena me dhyānaphalenaite sattvā dṛṣṭa eva dharmasukhino bhavantv anupādāya ca parinirvāntv iti, sa triṣu saṃjñeṣu saktas tad dhyānaṃ samāpadyate, yad utātmasaṃjñāyāṃ parasaṃjñāyāṃ dhyānasaṃjñāyām iyam ucyate laukikī dhyānapāramiteti, tathā hi lokato na carati noccarati na saṃkrāmati, tad ucyate laukikīti.
body.translated_text: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> enters into meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and does so with attachment, thinking: 'I enter into meditation for the benefit of all beings. These are the meditations; I carry out the <s>Buddha</s>'s command.' And while entering that meditation, through the method of apprehension, he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening in common with all beings, thinking: 'By this fruit of meditation, may these beings be happy in this very life and may they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging.' He enters that meditation while attached to three notions — namely, the notion of self, the notion of other, and the notion of meditation. This is called the worldly perfection of meditation. Because it does not go beyond, does not transcend, and does not cross over from the world — it is called worldly.

body.text: tatra katamā lokottarā dhyānapāramitā? yad uta trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ.
body.translated_text: What then is the supramundane perfection of meditation? It is the purity of the three circles.

body.text: tatra katamā trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ?
body.translated_text: What then is the purity of the three circles?

body.text: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsatvo dhyānāni samāpadyamāna ātmānaṃ nopalabhyate sattvān nopalabhyate vipākaṃ ca nābhinandati, sarvasattvebhyaś ca tāni dhyānāni niryātayati, tāś ca sattvān nopalabhyate, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty api ca nimittan na samanupaśyatīyam ucyate lokottarā dhyānapāramitā tathā hi lokāc carati uccarati saṃkrāmati tad ucyate lokottareti.
body.translated_text: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while entering into meditation, does not apprehend a self, does not apprehend beings, and does not rejoice in the ripening. He dedicates those meditations to all beings, yet does not apprehend those beings; he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening, yet does not perceive any sign. This is called the supramundane perfection of meditation. Because it goes beyond, transcends, and crosses over from the world — it is called supramundane.

body.text: asty āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā laukiky asti lokottarā.
body.translated_text: There is, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a worldly perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) and a supramundane one.

body.text: tatra katamā laukikī prajñāpāramitā?
body.translated_text: What then is the worldly perfection of wisdom?

body.text: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsatvaḥ prajñāṃ bhāvayati, tāñ ca saṃniśrito bhāvayati sarvapāpaṃ pratideśayati, ātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ cārthāya sarvapuṇyam anumodyate sarvabuddhān adhyeṣate upalambhayogena tac ca sarvakuśalamūlam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty anupāyena tasyaivaṃ bhavaty ahaṃ prajñāṃ bhāvayāmi sarvasattvānām arthāya iyaṃ prajñā imāṃ buddhājñāṃ karomi. tāṃ ca prajñāṃ bhāvayann upalambhayogena sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati anena me prajñāphalenaite sattvā dṛṣṭa eva dharme sukhino bhavantv anutpādāya ca parinirvāntv iti, sa triṣu saṃjñeṣu saktas tāṃ prajñāṃ bhāvayanti, yad utātmasaṃjñāyāṃ parasaṃjñāyāṃ prajñāsaṃjñāyām iyam ucyate laukikī (

children.text: ) prajñāpāramitā tathā hi lokān na carati noccarati na saṃkrāmati tad ucyate laukikīti.
children.translated_text: ) the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>); for indeed, it does not move through the world, nor rise above it, nor pass beyond it — therefore it is called 'worldly' (<s>laukikī</s>).

body.translated_text: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> cultivates wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), and does so with attachment — he confesses all evil, rejoices in the merit of self and others, beseeches all <s>Buddha</s>s, and through the method of apprehension dedicates all those roots of merit to unsurpassed perfect awakening, yet without skillful means (<s>anupāya</s>), thinking: 'I cultivate wisdom for the benefit of all beings. This is wisdom; I carry out the <s>Buddha</s>'s command.' And while cultivating that wisdom, through the method of apprehension, he dedicates it to unsurpassed perfect awakening in common with all beings, thinking: 'By this fruit of wisdom, may these beings be happy in this very life and may they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging.' He cultivates that wisdom while attached to three notions — namely, the notion of self, the notion of other, and the notion of wisdom. This is called the worldly (

body.text: tatra katamā lokottarā prajñāpāramitā? yad uta trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the transcendent perfection of wisdom (<s>lokottarā prajñāpāramitā</s>)? It is the purity of the threefold circle (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ?
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the purity of the threefold circle?

body.text: ihāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsatvaḥ prajñāṃ bhāvayann ātmānaṃ nopalabhyate sattvān nopalabhyate prajñān nopalabhyate vipākaś ca nābhinandati, sarvasattvebhyaś ca prajñāṃ niryātayati, tāṃś ca sattvān nopalabhyate, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty api ca nimittan na samanupaśyatīyam ucyate lokottarā prajñāpāramitā tathā hi lokāc caraty uccarati saṃkrāmati tad ucyate lokottarā prajñāpāramiteti.
body.translated_text: Here, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> cultivating wisdom does not apprehend a self, does not apprehend beings, does not apprehend wisdom, and does not delight in its result; he transfers wisdom to all beings, yet does not apprehend those beings; he dedicates it toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), yet does not perceive any sign — this is called the transcendent perfection of wisdom, for indeed it moves through the world, rises above it, and passes beyond it — therefore it is called 'transcendent' (<s>lokottarā</s>).

body.text: evaṃ khalv āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu caran bodhimārgaṃ pariśodhayati.
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>) purifies the path to awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>).

body.text: āha: katamāyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ?
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: What, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>?

body.text: subhūtir āha: dānapāramitāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, śīlapāramitā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, kṣāntipāramitā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, vīryapāramitā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, dhyānapāramitā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: The perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.
