body.text: catvāri smṛtyupasthānāny āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, catvāri samyakprahāṇāni bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, catvāri ṛddhipādā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, pañcendriyāṇi bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, pañca balāni bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, sapta bodhyaṅgāni bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgo bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ.
body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the five powers (<s>bala</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>) is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: catvāry āryasatyāny āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, catvāri dhyānāni bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, catvāry apramāṇāni bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, catasra ārūpyasamāpattayo bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, aṣṭau vimokṣā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayo bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāni bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, pañcābhijñā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, sarvasamādhayo bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ.
body.translated_text: The four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the nine successive meditative attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>) — are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: daśatathāgatabalāny āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, catvāri vaiśāradyāni bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, catasraḥ pratisaṃvido bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, mahāmaitrī bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, mahākaruṇā bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ, aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmā āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhimārgaḥ.
body.translated_text: The ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) is the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the path to awakening of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: āha: sādhu sādhv āyuṣman subhūte katamasyā ayaṃ pāramitāyāḥ puruṣakāraḥ?
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: Excellent, excellent, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>! To which perfection does this effort (<s>puruṣakāra</s>) belong?

body.text: subhūtir āha: prajñāpāramitāyā āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputrāyaṃ puruṣakāraḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā (

children.text: ) janayitrī sarvakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ śrāvakadharmāṇāṃ pratyekabuddhadharmāṇāṃ buddhadharmāṇāṃ prajñāpāramitāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra parigrāhikā saṃgrāhikā sarvakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ śrāvakadharmāṇāṃ bodhisattvadharmāṇāṃ buddhadharmāṇāṃ prajñāpāramitāyām āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra caritaiḥ pūrvakais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddhāḥ, anāgatā apy āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra tathāgatārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā atraiva prajñāpāramitāyāñ caritvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate. ye 'pi te āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatārhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās tiṣṭhanti dhrīyante yāpayanti, te 'pīhaiva prajñāpāramitāyāñ caritvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhāḥ.
children.translated_text: ) is the mother (<s>janayitrī</s>) of all wholesome dharmas, of the dharmas of hearers (<s>śrāvaka</s>), of the dharmas of solitary buddhas (<s>pratyekabuddha</s>), and of the dharmas of buddhas. The perfection of wisdom, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, embraces and gathers all wholesome dharmas, the dharmas of hearers, the dharmas of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, and the dharmas of buddhas. Through practicing the perfection of wisdom, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, perfectly awakened ones of the past fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). The <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, perfectly awakened ones of the future also, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening through practicing in this very perfection of wisdom. And those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, perfectly awakened ones who presently abide, endure, and live in the world-systems of the ten directions, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> — they too have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening through practicing in this very perfection of wisdom.

body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: This effort belongs to the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>. For what reason? Because, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the perfection of wisdom (

body.text: sacet punar āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ na bhavati kāṅkṣāyitatvaṃ vā dhanvāyitatvaṃ vā veditavyam āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra viharaty ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nena vihāreṇa yad uta sarvasattvānāṃ trāṇāya sarvasattvānām aparityāgatāyai tac cānupalambhayogena viharaty ayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nena manasikāreṇa yad uta mahākaruṇā manasikārena.
body.translated_text: Moreover, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, if when the perfection of wisdom is being taught a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> has neither doubt nor hesitation, it should be known, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwells in this abiding, namely for the protection of all beings and for not abandoning all beings — and that through the yoga of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>). This <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwells with this mental attention, namely the mental attention of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>).

body.text: āha: viharatum āyuṣman subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'yam anena vihāreṇecchasi, avirahitaṃ cānena manasikāreṇa yad uta mahākaruṇā manasikāreṇa, evaṃ saty āyuṣman subhūte sarvasattvā bodhisattvā bhaviṣyanti. tat kasya hetoḥ? sarvasattvā hy āyuṣman subhūte 'virahitā manasikārena.
body.translated_text: He (<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>) said: Let this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwell in this abiding as you wish, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, and let him not be separated from this mental attention, namely the mental attention of great compassion. But if so, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, all beings would be <s>bodhisattva</s>s. For what reason? Because all beings, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are not separated from mental attention.

body.text: subhūtir āha: sādhu sādhv āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra upālapsye upālapsya iti. ata evāyuṣmatā śāradvatīputreṇa bhūtapadābhidhānena parigṛhītaḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? sattvāsattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā sattvābhāvatayā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā sattvāsvabhāvatayā manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā, sattvaśūnyatayā manasikārāśūnyatā veditavyā, sattvaviviktatayā manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā, sattvān abhisaṃbodhanatayā manasikārān abhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: Excellent, excellent, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> — you should challenge me, you should challenge me! For this very reason has Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> grasped the true meaning through his utterance of true words. For what reason? Because, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, through the non-existence of beings, the non-existence of mental attention should be understood; through the non-existence of beings, the non-existence of mental attention should be understood; through the lack of inherent nature of beings, the lack of inherent nature of mental attention should be understood; through the emptiness of beings, the emptiness of mental attention should be understood; through the seclusion of beings, the seclusion of mental attention should be understood; through the non-awakening to beings, the non-awakening to mental attention should be understood.

body.text: pratisaṃvidasattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā, pratisaṃvidabhāvatayā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā, pratisaṃvidasvabhāvatayā manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā, pratisaṃvidśūnyatayā manasikāraśūnyatā veditavyā, pratisaṃvidviviktatayā manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā, pratisaṃvidanabhisaṃbodhanatayā manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā,
body.translated_text: By the non-existence of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the non-existence of attention should be understood; by the non-being of the analytical knowledges, the non-being of attention should be understood; by the lack of inherent nature of the analytical knowledges, the lack of inherent nature of attention should be understood; by the emptiness of the analytical knowledges, the emptiness of attention should be understood; by the seclusion of the analytical knowledges, the seclusion of attention should be understood; by the non-full-awakening of the analytical knowledges, the non-full-awakening of attention should be understood.

body.text: mahāmaitryasattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā, mahāmaitryabhāvatayā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā, mahāmaitryasvabhāvatayā manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā, mahāmaitrīśūnyatayā manasikāraśūnyatā veditavyā, mahāmaitrīviviktatayā manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā, mahāmaitryanabhisaṃbodhanatayā manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā,
body.translated_text: By the non-existence of great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the non-existence of attention should be understood; by the non-being of great loving-kindness, the non-being of attention should be understood; by the lack of inherent nature of great loving-kindness, the lack of inherent nature of attention should be understood; by the emptiness of great loving-kindness, the emptiness of attention should be understood; by the seclusion of great loving-kindness, the seclusion of attention should be understood; by the non-full-awakening of great loving-kindness, the non-full-awakening of attention should be understood.

body.text: mahākaruṇāsattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā, mahākaruṇābhāvatayā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā, mahākaruṇā'svabhāvatayā manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā, mahākaruṇāśūnyatayā manasikāraśūnyatā veditavyā, mahākaruṇāviviktatayā manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā, mahākaruṇānabhisaṃbodhanatayā manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā,
body.translated_text: By the non-existence of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the non-existence of attention should be understood; by the non-being of great compassion, the non-being of attention should be understood; by the lack of inherent nature of great compassion, the lack of inherent nature of attention should be understood; by the emptiness of great compassion, the emptiness of attention should be understood; by the seclusion of great compassion, the seclusion of attention should be understood; by the non-full-awakening of great compassion, the non-full-awakening of attention should be understood.

body.text: āveṇikabuddhadharmāsattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā, āveṇikabuddhadharmābhāvatayā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā, āveṇikabuddhadharmāsvabhāvatayā manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā, āveṇikabuddhadharmaśūnyatayā manasikāraśūnyatā veditavyā, āveṇikabuddhadharmaviviktatayā manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā, āveṇikabuddhadharmānabhisaṃbodhanatayā manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā,
body.translated_text: By the non-existence of the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the non-existence of attention should be understood; by the non-being of the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, the non-being of attention should be understood; by the lack of inherent nature of the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, the lack of inherent nature of attention should be understood; by the emptiness of the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, the emptiness of attention should be understood; by the seclusion of the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, the seclusion of attention should be understood; by the non-full-awakening of the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, the non-full-awakening of attention should be understood.

body.text: sarvajñatāsattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā, sarvajñatābhāvatayā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā, sarvajñatāsvabhāvatayā (

body.text: mārgākārajñatāsattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā, mārgākārajñatābhāvatayā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā, mārgākārajñatāsvabhāvatayā manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā, mārgākārajñatāśūnyatayā manasikāraśūnyatā veditavyā, mārgākārajñatāviviktatayā manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā, mārgākārajñatānabhisaṃbodhanatayā manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā,
body.translated_text: By the non-existence of the knowledge of path-aspects (<s>mārgākārajñatā</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the non-existence of attention should be understood; by the non-being of the knowledge of path-aspects, the non-being of attention should be understood; by the lack of inherent nature of the knowledge of path-aspects, the lack of inherent nature of attention should be understood; by the emptiness of the knowledge of path-aspects, the emptiness of attention should be understood; by the seclusion of the knowledge of path-aspects, the seclusion of attention should be understood; by the non-full-awakening of the knowledge of path-aspects, the non-full-awakening of attention should be understood.

body.text: sarvākārajñatāsattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā, sarvākārajñatābhāvatayā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā, sarvākārajñatāsvabhāvatayā manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā, sarvākārajñatāśūnyatayā manasikāraśūnyatā veditavyā, sarvākārajñatāviviktatayā manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā, sarvākārajñatānabhisaṃbodhanatayā manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā.
body.translated_text: By the non-existence of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the non-existence of attention should be understood; by the non-being of the knowledge of all aspects, the non-being of attention should be understood; by the lack of inherent nature of the knowledge of all aspects, the lack of inherent nature of attention should be understood; by the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects, the emptiness of attention should be understood; by the seclusion of the knowledge of all aspects, the seclusion of attention should be understood; by the non-full-awakening of the knowledge of all aspects, the non-full-awakening of attention should be understood.

body.text: bodhyaṅgāsattayāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra manasikārāsattā veditavyā, bodhyaṅgābhāvatyā manasikārābhāvatā veditavyā, bodhyaṅgāsvabhāvatayā manasikārāsvabhāvatā veditavyā, bodhyaṅgaśūnyatayā manasikāraśūnyatā veditavyā, bodhyaṅgaviviktatayā manasikāraviviktatā veditavyā, bodhyaṅgānabhisaṃbodhanatayā manasikārānabhisaṃbodhanatā veditavyā.
body.translated_text: By the non-existence of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the non-existence of attention should be understood; by the non-being of the factors of awakening, the non-being of attention should be understood; by the lack of inherent nature of the factors of awakening, the lack of inherent nature of attention should be understood; by the emptiness of the factors of awakening, the emptiness of attention should be understood; by the seclusion of the factors of awakening, the seclusion of attention should be understood; by the non-full-awakening of the factors of awakening, the non-full-awakening of attention should be understood.

body.text: anenāyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'virahita eva tena manasikāreṇa veditavyaḥ, yad uta mahākaruṇāmanasikārena.
body.translated_text: By this method, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should be understood as never being separated from that attention, namely, attention rooted in great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇāmanasikāra</s>).

body.text: atha bhagavān āyuṣmate subhūtaye sādhukāram adāt: sādhu sādhu subhūte, evaṃ khalu subhūte bodhisattvebhyo mahāsattvebhyaḥ prajñāpāramitopadeṣṭavyā, yathā tvam upadiśasi yathāpi taṃ tathāgatasyānubhāvena evaṃ ca punar bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ, yathā tvam upadiśasi. asmin khalu punaḥ prajñāpāramitā parivartā.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> expressed his approval to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Well done, well done, <s>Subhūti</s>! Indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) should be taught to <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s just as you have taught it, and indeed through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Moreover, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should train in the perfection of wisdom just as you have taught. This indeed is the chapter on the perfection of wisdom.

body.text: āyuṣmatā subhūtinā bhāṣyamāne ayam trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍ vikāram akaṃpat prākaṃpat saṃprākaṃpat, avedhat prāvedhat saṃprāvedhat, acarat prācarat saṃprācarat, akṣubhyat (

body.translated_text: While the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> was speaking, this great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) shook in six ways: it trembled, trembled greatly, trembled exceedingly; it quaked, quaked greatly, quaked exceedingly; it moved, moved greatly, moved exceedingly; it shook violently,

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ smitaṃ prādur akārṣīt.
body.translated_text: Then at that moment, the <s>Bhagavat</s> produced a smile.

body.text: athāyuṣmāṃ subhūtir bhagavantam etad avocat: ko bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasyāviṣkaraṇe?
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: What is the cause, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, what is the condition for the manifestation of a smile?

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtim etad avocat: yathaivāhaṃ subhūte iha sahāyāṃ lokadhātau prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣe tathaiva pūrvasyāṃ diśy asaṃkhyeyeṣv aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā imām eva prajñāpāramitāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ bhāṣante,
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavat</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Just as I, <s>Subhūti</s>, here in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system teach the perfection of wisdom, so too in the eastern direction, in innumerable, immeasurable world-systems, <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, perfectly awakened ones teach this very same perfection of wisdom to <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s.

body.text: yathaivāhaṃ subhūte iha sahāyāṃ lokadhātau prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣe tathaiva dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśy asaṃkhyeyeṣv aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho imām eva prajñāpāramitāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ bhāṣante,
body.translated_text: Just as I, <s>Subhūti</s>, here in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system teach the perfection of wisdom, so too in the southern direction, in innumerable, immeasurable world-systems, <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, perfectly awakened ones teach this very same perfection of wisdom to <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s.

body.translated_text: Just as I, <s>Subhūti</s>, teach the perfection of wisdom here in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, so too in the upward direction, in innumerable and immeasurable world-systems, <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, perfectly awakened ones teach this very perfection of wisdom to <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s.

body.text: yasmin khalu punaḥ subhūte prajñāpāramitānirdeśe bhāṣyamāṇe dvādaśānām ayutānāṃ devamāṇuṣyakānāṃ prajñāpāramitāyā anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntir utpannā, teṣām api samantād daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣamāṇānām asaṃkhyeyānām aprameyānāṃ sattvānām anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni.
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, while this teaching of the perfection of wisdom was being spoken, one hundred and twenty thousand gods and humans attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (<s>anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣānti</s>) through the perfection of wisdom. And for innumerable and immeasurable beings in all world-systems throughout the ten directions where <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>Bhagavat</s>s are teaching the perfection of wisdom, the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) arose.

body.text: śatasāhasryāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ subhūtiparivartas trayodaśamaḥ
body.translated_text: End of the thirteenth chapter, the <s>Subhūti</s> chapter, of the Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines.

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānām indra āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtim etad avocat: ete bhadanta subhūte yāvantas trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau cāturmahārājakāyikā devāḥ trayastriṃśā devā yāmā devā tuṣitā devā nirmāṇaratayo devāḥ paranirmitavaśavartino devā brahmakāyikā devā ābhāsvarā devāḥ śubhakṛtsnā devā bṛhatphalā devāḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devās te sarve saṃnipatitā bhadanta subhūte dharmaśravaṇāya prajñāpāramitopadeśaṃ śrotukāmāḥ.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, all the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> gods, <s>Yāma</s> gods, <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, and <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> gods throughout the three-thousand great thousand world-system — they have all assembled, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, to hear the Dharma, wishing to hear the instruction on the perfection of wisdom.

body.text: kathaṃ bhadanta subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam?
body.translated_text: How, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abide in the perfection of wisdom?

body.text: katamā ca bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā?
body.translated_text: And what is the perfection of wisdom of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>?

body.text: kathaṃ ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāraitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam?
body.translated_text: And how should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> train in the perfection of wisdom?

body.text: evam ukte āyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakram devānām indram etad avocat: tena hi kauśika śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikurūpadeśyāmi buddhānubhāvena buddhādhiṣṭhānena ca bodhisattvebhyo mahāsattvebhyaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yathā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyaṃ yathā ca śikṣitavyam. yaiś ca devaputrair anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye cittaṃ notpāditam, tair apy anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye cittam utpādayitavyam. ye punar avakrāntasamyaktvanyāmāt, te pratibalā anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye cittam utpādayitum. tat kasya hetoḥ?
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: Well then, <s>Kauśika</s>, listen well and attentively — I shall teach, through the power and blessing of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s concerning the perfection of wisdom: how a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should abide in the perfection of wisdom and how he should train. And those <s>devaputra</s>s who have not yet generated the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening should generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening. But those who have entered the certainty of the correct course (<s>samyaktvanyāma</s>) are not able to generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening. For what reason?

body.text: baddhasimā hi te saṃsārasrotasaḥ.
body.translated_text: For they have fixed boundaries in the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: api tu khalu punas teṣām apy anumode saced anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhyaye cittam utpādayati, nāhaṃ teṣāṃ kuśalapakṣasyāntarāyaṃ karomi viśiṣṭebhyo hi dharmebhyo viśiṣṭatamā dharmā adhyālambitavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: However, I rejoice in them if they generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening — I do not create obstacles to their wholesome practices. For from excellent dharmas, the most excellent dharmas should be grasped.

body.text: tatra katamā kauśika bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā?
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>Kauśika</s>, what is the perfection of wisdom of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>?

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carann evaṃ pratisaṃśikṣate dharmā evaite dharmān abhiṣyandayanti pariṣyandayanti paripūrayanti parispharayanti parimīmāṃsyante, nāsty atrātmā vā ātmīyaṃ va. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi yad bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya pariṇāmanācittaṃ tad bodhicitte na samavahitaṃ, yad bodhicittaṃ tat pariṇāmanācitte na samavahitaṃ, yat kauśika pariṇāmanācittaṃ tad bodhicitte na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate, yad bodhicittaṃ tat pariṇāmanācitte na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate. iyaṃ kausika bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā yad evaṃ sarvadharmāś ca pratyavekṣate na kvacid dharmeṣu paricarati.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) trains thus: 'These are just dharmas that flow into dharmas, overflow into dharmas, fulfill dharmas, pervade dharmas, and are investigated — there is here no self nor anything belonging to a self.' For what reason? For indeed, that which is the mind of dedication (<s>pariṇāmanācitta</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not established in the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), and that which is the mind of awakening is not established in the mind of dedication. <s>Kauśika</s>, the mind of dedication is not found, not apprehended in the mind of awakening, and the mind of awakening is not found, not apprehended in the mind of dedication. This, <s>Kauśika</s>, is the perfection of wisdom of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> — that he thus examines all dharmas yet does not engage anywhere in dharmas.

body.text: kathaṃ bodhicittaṃ pariṇāmanācitte na samavahitam?

body.text: subhūtir āha: yat kauśika pariṇāmanācittaṃ tad acittaṃ, yad bodhicittaṃ tad acittam, iti hi yad acittaṃ tad acintyaṃ, yad acintyaṃ tad acittaṃ na hy acittatā acittatāyāṃ pariṇāmayati, nācintyatā acintyatāyāṃ pariṇāmayati, iti hi yā acittatā sā acintyatā yā acintyatā sā acittatā, iyaṃ kauśika bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: <s>Kauśika</s>, the mind of dedication is no-mind (<s>acitta</s>); the mind of awakening is no-mind. For indeed, that which is no-mind is inconceivable (<s>acintya</s>); that which is inconceivable is no-mind. For no-mind-ness does not transform no-mind-ness; inconceivability does not transform inconceivability. For indeed, that which is no-mind-ness is inconceivability; that which is inconceivability is no-mind-ness. This, <s>Kauśika</s>, is the perfection of wisdom of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtim āmantrayate sma: sādhu sādhu subhūte sādhu khalu punas tvaṃ bodhisattvebhyo mahāsattvebhyaḥ prajñāpāramitām upadiśasy utsāhaṃ dadāsi.
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Well done, well done, <s>Subhūti</s>! Well done indeed that you instruct the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s in the perfection of wisdom and give them encouragement.

body.text: subhūtir āha: kṛtajñena mayā bhagavan bhavitavyaṃ nākṛtajñena, tathā hi paurvakānāṃ tathāgatānām arham arhantāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānām antike taiḥ śrāvakais tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūtaḥ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu codito 'nuśiṣṭāḥ saṃdarśitaḥ samādāyitaḥ samuttejitaḥ saṃpraharṣitaḥ niveśitaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ yato bhagavaṃ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūtaḥ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu śikṣitaḥ. anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ evam eva bhagavann asmābhir bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsv avavaditavyā anuśikṣitavyāḥ saṃharṣitavyā, samādāpayitavyāḥ, samuttare jñayitavyā, saṃpraharṣayitavyāḥ niveśayitavyā, pratiṣṭhāpayitavyā, asmābhir api bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsv avavaditā anuśiṣṭāḥ saṃharṣitāḥ samādāpitaḥ samuttejitāḥ saṃpraharṣitaḥ niveśitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: I must be grateful, Blessed One, not ungrateful. For indeed, in the presence of the former <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones, by those <s>śrāvaka</s>s the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One — when formerly a <s>bodhisattva</s> — was exhorted, instructed, shown, caused to undertake, encouraged, gladdened, established, and firmly grounded in the six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>). Since the Blessed One, when formerly a <s>bodhisattva</s>, trained in the six perfections and fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), in the same way, Blessed One, we should admonish, instruct, gladden, cause to undertake, encourage, delight, establish, and firmly ground the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s in the six perfections. Having been admonished, instructed, gladdened, caused to undertake, encouraged, delighted, established, and firmly grounded by us in the six perfections, these <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s too will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: athāyuṣmān subhūtiḥ śakram devānām indram etad avocat: tena hi kauśika śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru bhāṣiṣye yathā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyaṃ, yathā ca na sthātavyaṃ rūpaṃ kauśika rūpeṇa śūnyaṃ, vedanā vedanayā śūnyā, saṃjñā saṃjñayā śūnyā, saṃskārāḥ saṃskāraiḥ śūnyāḥ, vijñānaṃ vijñānena śūnyaṃ, bodhisattvo bodhisattvena śūnyaḥ, iti hi kauśika rūpaśūnyatā ca vedanāśūnyatā ca saṃjñāśūnyatā ca saṃskāraśūnyatā ca vijñānaśūnyatā ca bodhisattvaśūnyatā cādvayam etad advaidhīkāram. evaṃ khalu kauśika bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam.
body.translated_text: Then Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, listen well and carefully attend — I shall explain how the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should stand in the perfection of wisdom, and how he should not stand. <s>Kauśika</s>, form is empty of form; feeling is empty of feeling; perception is empty of perception; formations are empty of formations; consciousness is empty of consciousness; the <s>bodhisattva</s> is empty of <s>bodhisattva</s>. For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, the emptiness of form, the emptiness of feeling, the emptiness of perception, the emptiness of formations, the emptiness of consciousness, and the emptiness of the <s>bodhisattva</s> — this is non-dual (<s>advaya</s>), undivided (<s>advaidhīkāra</s>). Thus indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should stand in the perfection of wisdom.

body.translated_text: One should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)'; should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>)'; should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>)'; should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill the faculties (<s>indriya</s>)'; should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill the powers (<s>bala</s>)'; should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>)'; should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>)'; should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall enter the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s assured state (<s>bodhisattvaniyāma</s>)'; the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'having entered the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s assured state, I shall stand on the Buddha-stage (<s>buddhabhūmi</s>)'.

body.text: pañcabodhisattvābhijñāḥ paripūrayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, pañcasu bodhisattvābhijñāsu sthitvā aprameyāny asaṃkhyeyāni buddhakṣetrāṇy upasaṃkramiṣyāmi buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya śrutvā ca tathatvāya parebhyo deśayiṣyāmīti bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: One should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill the five <s>bodhisattva</s> superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>)'; the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'having stood in the five <s>bodhisattva</s> superknowledges, I shall visit immeasurable, innumerable buddha-fields for the purpose of seeing, paying homage to, and attending upon the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>s, for hearing the Dharma, and having heard it, I shall teach it to others in accordance with its true nature'.

body.text: yādṛśāni ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhakṣetrāni tadṛśāni eva pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, sattvān bodhau paripācayiṣyāmīti bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection buddha-fields just like those of those Blessed <s>Buddha</s>s'; the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall ripen beings toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>)'.

body.text: aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāṃś ca lokadhātuṃ gatvā tān tathāgatān arhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān satkariṣyāmīti gurukariṣyāmīti mānayiṣyāmīti pūjayiṣyāmīti, puṣpamālyagandhavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākābhiḥ koṭīniyutaśatasahasraiś ca tāṃs tathāgatāṃ pūjayiṣyāmīty evam api na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāṃ sattvān anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmīti bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: One should also not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'having gone to immeasurable, innumerable world-systems, I shall honor, revere, respect, and worship those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones, and I shall worship those <s>Tathāgata</s>s with hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi</s>s of <s>niyuta</s>s of flowers, garlands, perfume, ointment, powder, robes, parasols, banners, and flags'; the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall establish immeasurable, innumerable beings in unsurpassed perfect awakening'.

body.text: pañcacakṣuṣy utpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena. katamāni pañca? māṃsacakṣur divyacakṣuḥ prajñācakṣur dharmacakṣur buddhacakṣur utpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, sarvasamādhīṃ paripūrayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, yena yena punaḥ samādhīn ākāṅkṣayiṣyāmi vikrīḍituṃ tena tena samādhinā vikrīḍiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogema, sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: One should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall produce the five eyes (<s>cakṣus</s>).' Which five? One should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall produce the fleshly eye (<s>māṃsacakṣus</s>), the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>), the wisdom eye (<s>prajñācakṣus</s>), the dharma eye (<s>dharmacakṣus</s>), and the Buddha eye (<s>buddhacakṣus</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall fulfill all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'with whatever concentrations I wish to sport, with those very concentrations I shall sport'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection all the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>)'.

body.text: daśatathāgatabalāni pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, catvāri vaiśāradyāni pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, mahāmaitrīṃ pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, mahākaruṇāṃ pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, aṣṭādaśāveṇikān buddhadharmān pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti evam api bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, dvātriṃśatāni mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni kāye pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam (

children.text: ) upalambhayogena, aśīty anuvyañjanāni kāye pariniṣpādayiṣyāmīti bodhisattvena mahāsattvena na sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
children.translated_text: — the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection the eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>) on my body'.

body.translated_text: One should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>)'; even thus the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection the eighteen exclusive qualities of a Buddha (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I shall bring to perfection the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) on my body' —

body.text: śuddhānusārīni na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, dharmānusārīni na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, aṣṭamaka iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, srotaāpanna iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, saptakṛtvabhavaparamam iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, kulaṃkula ity ekavīcika iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, samaśīrṣapudgala iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, āyuḥkṣaye kleśakṣaye ceti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, avinipātadharmā iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, sakṛdāgāmi sakṛd imaṃ lokam āgamya duḥkhasyāṃ taṃ kariṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, anāgagāmiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratikannaka iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, anāgāmi tatraiva nirvāsyatīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, arhatphalasākṣātkriyāyaiḥ pratipannaka iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, arhann ihaivānupadhiśeṣanirvāṇadhātau parinirvāpayiṣyatīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, pratyekabuddha iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, atikramya śrāvakabhūmiṃ pratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ ca bodhisattvabhūmau sthāsyāmīti iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: One should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am a follower of purity (<s>śuddhānusārin</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am a follower of the Dharma (<s>dharmānusārin</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am an eighth person (<s>aṣṭamaka</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am one with at most seven rebirths (<s>saptakṛttvabhavaparama</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am one reborn in a family (<s>kulaṃkula</s>)' or 'one with a single interval (<s>ekavīcika</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am an equal-headed person (<s>samaśīrṣapudgala</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'at the exhaustion of life, at the exhaustion of the defilements'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am one who is not subject to falling into lower realms (<s>avinipātadharma</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'as a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), coming once more to this world, I shall make an end of suffering'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am one progressing toward the realization of the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmin</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'as a non-returner, I shall attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> right there'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am one progressing toward the realization of the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'as an <s>arhat</s>, I shall attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> right here in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇadhātu</s>)'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'I am a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>'; one should not stand through the method of apprehension in thinking 'having gone beyond the <s>śrāvaka</s>-stage and the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-stage, I shall stand on the <s>bodhisattva</s>-stage'.

body.text: mārgākārajñatājñāne sarvākārajñatāyāṃ ca na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, sarvākāraiḥ sarvadharmān abhisaṃbuddhā sarvāvāsanā na saṃvikte śakṣayāyāṃ na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhya dharmacakrapravartayiṣyāmīti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, buddhakārye kṛtvā aprameyān asaṃkhyeyān lokadhātūn parinirvāpayiṣyāmīti, evam api na sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: One should not abide in the knowledge of path-aspects (<s>mārgākārajñatā</s>) and in the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'having fully awakened to all dharmas in all their aspects, I shall not be able to eliminate all latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>)' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening, I shall turn the wheel of the Dharma (<s>dharmacakra</s>)' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'having accomplished the <s>Buddha</s>'s work, I shall lead beings in immeasurable and innumerable world-systems to final <s>nirvāṇa</s>' through the method of apprehension.

body.text: caturṣu ṛddhipādeṣu sthitvā tathārūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpatsye yathārūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadya gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpān tiṣṭheyam iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, aparimitaś ca me āyur bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: One should not abide thinking 'abiding in the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), I shall attain such a concentration that, having attained it, I could remain for aeons as numerous as the grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'my lifespan would be immeasurable' through the method of apprehension.

body.text: dvātriṃśatāṃ me mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānām ekaikalakṣaṇaṃ śatapuṇyapariniṣpannaṃ bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavaḥ pūrveṇa, yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavo dakṣiṇena, yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavaḥ paścimena, yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātava uttareṇa, yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavaḥ uttarapūrveṇa, yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopamā (

children.text: ) lokadhātavaḥ pūrvadakṣiṇena, yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavo dakṣiṇapaścimena, yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavaḥ paścimottareṇa, tāvanta ekaṃ me buddhakṣetraṃ bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, vajropamo me trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
children.translated_text: in the southeast, however many in the southwest, however many in the northwest — all of those would comprise my single <s>Buddha</s>-field' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'my great trichiliocosm would be diamond-like' through the method of apprehension.

body.translated_text: One should not abide thinking 'each of my thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) would be perfected by a hundred merits' through the method of apprehension. One should not abide thinking 'however many world-systems as numerous as the grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> there are in the east, however many in the south, however many in the west, however many in the north, however many in the northeast, however many

body.text: bodhivṛkṣāś ca me tādṛśo gandho niścaret, ye sattvās taṃ gandham ājighreyus teṣām na rāgadveṣamohāś ca vyābādheyur iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, na śrāvakacittaṃ na pratyekabuddhacittam utpadyeyur iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, sarve ca te niyatā bhaveyur anuttarāyā samyaksaṃbuddhāv iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, ye ca sattvās taṃ bodhivṛkṣagandham ājighreyus teṣāṃ na kaścid vyādhir bhaved kāye vā citte veti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: One should not abide thinking 'from my <s>Bodhi</s>-tree such a fragrance would emanate that whatever beings smell that fragrance, desire, hatred, and delusion would not afflict them' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'no thought of a hearer (<s>śrāvaka</s>) nor thought of a solitary awakened one (<s>pratyekabuddha</s>) would arise in them' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'all of them would become determined for unsurpassed perfect awakening' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'whatever beings smell the fragrance of that <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, no disease whatsoever would arise in their body or mind' through the method of apprehension.

body.text: tatra ca me buddhakṣetre na rūpaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, na vedanāśabdo bhaven na saṃjñāśabdo bhaven na saṃskāraśabdo bhaven na vijñānaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena,
body.translated_text: One should not abide thinking 'in my <s>Buddha</s>-field there would be no word 'form'' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'feeling,' no word 'perception,' no word 'formations,' no word 'consciousness'' through the method of apprehension.

body.text: na dhātuśabdo nāyatanaśabdo na pratītyasamutpādaśabdo bhaved iti sthātavyam upalambhayogena,
body.translated_text: One should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'element,' no word 'sense-base,' no word 'dependent origination'' through the method of apprehension.

body.text: na dānapāramitāśabdo bhaven na śīlapāramitāśabdo bhaven na kṣāntipāramitāśabdo bhaven na vīryapāramitāśabdo bhaven na dhyānapāramitāśabdo bhaven na prajñāpāramitāśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena,
body.translated_text: One should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'perfection of giving,' no word 'perfection of morality,' no word 'perfection of patience,' no word 'perfection of vigor,' no word 'perfection of meditation,' no word 'perfection of wisdom'' through the method of apprehension.

body.text: nādhyātmaśūnyatāśabdo bhaven na bahirdhāśūnyatāśabdo bhaven nādhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatāśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, na śūnyatāśūnyatāśabdo bhaven na mahāśūnyatāśabdo bhaven na paramārthaśūnyatāśabdo bhaven na saṃsrtaśūnyatāśabdo bhaven nāsaṃskṛtaśūnyatāśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, nātyantaśūnyatāśabdo bhaven nānavarāgraśūnyatāśabdo bhaven nānavakāraśūnyatāśabdo bhaven na prakṛtiśūnyatāśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, na sarvadharmaśūnyatāśabdo bhaven na svalakṣaṇaśūnyatāśabdo bhaven nānupalambhaśūnyatāśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, nābhāvaśūnyatāśabdo bhaven na svabhāvaśūnyatāśabdo bhaven nābhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, (

children.text: ) na smṛtyupasthānaśabdo bhaven na samyakprahāṇaśabdo bhaven na ṛddhipādaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, nendriyaśabdo bhaven na balaśabdo bhaven na bodhyaṅgaśabdo bhaven nāryāṣṭāṅgamārgaśabdo bhaven nāryasatyaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavaym upalambhayogena, na dhyānaśabdo bhaven nāpramāṇaśabdo bhaven nārūpyasamāpattiśabdo bhaven na vimokṣaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, nānupūrvavihārasamāpattiśabdo bhaven na śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhaśabdo bhaven nābhijñāśabdo bhaven na samādhiśabdo bhaven na dhāraṇīmukhaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, na tathāgatabalaśabdo bhaven na vaiśāradyaśabdo bhaven na pratisaṃvidśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, na mahāmaitrīśabdo bhaven na mahākaruṇāśabdo bhaven nāveṇikabuddhadharmaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, na srotaāpattiśabdo bhaven na sakṛdāgāmiśabdo bhaven nānāgāmiśabdo bhaven nārhattvaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena, na pratyekabuddhaśabdo bhaven na buddhaśabdo bhaved iti na sthātavyam upalambhayogena. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhya sarvadharmā nopalabdhāḥ.
children.translated_text: one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'foundations of mindfulness,' no word 'right efforts,' no word 'bases of supernatural power'' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'faculties,' no word 'powers,' no word 'factors of awakening,' no word 'noble eightfold path,' no word 'noble truths'' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'meditative absorptions,' no word 'immeasurables,' no word 'formless attainments,' no word 'liberations'' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'successive abiding attainments,' no word 'gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness,' no word 'superknowledges,' no word 'concentrations,' no word 'gateways of retention'' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,' no word 'fearlessnesses,' no word 'analytical knowledges'' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'great loving-kindness,' no word 'great compassion,' no word 'exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>'' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word 'stream-entry,' no word 'once-returning,' no word 'non-returning,' no word '<s>arhat</s>ship'' through the method of apprehension; one should not abide thinking 'there would be no word '<s>pratyekabuddha</s>,' no word '<s>Buddha</s>'' through the method of apprehension. Why is that? Because when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one attained unsurpassed perfect awakening, he did not apprehend any dharmas whatsoever.

body.text: evaṃ khalu kauśika bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ na sthātavyam upalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: Thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not abide in the perfection of wisdom through the method of apprehension.

body.text: athāyuṣmataḥ śāradvatīputasyaitad abhūt: kathaṃ punar bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyam?
body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in the Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: How then should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abide in the perfection of wisdom?

body.text: athāyuṣmataḥ subhūtir āyuṣmataḥ śāradvatīputrasya cetasyaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāyāyuṣmataṃ śāradvatīputram āmantrayati sma. tat kiṃ manyase? āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra kva tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sthitaḥ.
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, knowing in his own mind the mental deliberation of the Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, addressed the Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: What do you think, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>? Where does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one abide?

body.text: āha: na kvacid āyuṣman subhūte tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sthita iti apratisthitamānasaḥ khalu punar āyuṣman subhūte tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sa rūpe na sthito vedanāyāṃ na sthitaḥ saṃjñāyāṃ na sthitaḥ saṃskāreṣu na sthito vijñāne na sthitaḥ.
body.translated_text: He said: Nowhere, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one abide. Indeed, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one has a mind that is unestablished (<s>apratiṣṭhita</s>). He does not abide in form, does not abide in feeling, does not abide in perception, does not abide in formations, does not abide in consciousness.

body.text: na cakṣuṣi sthito na śrotre sthito na ghrāṇe sthito na jihvāyāṃ sthito na kāye sthito na manasi sthitaḥ.

body.text: evaṃ khalv āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ sthātavyam ity asthānayogena.
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should train in the perfection of wisdom and should abide — through the yoga of non-abiding (<s>asthānayoga</s>).

body.text: atha khalu tatra parṣadi keṣāñcid devaputrāṇām etad abhavat: yāni tāni yakṣāṇāṃ yakṣapadāni yakṣamantritāni yakṣarutāni yakṣapravyāhṛtāni vijñāyante, tāni mantrayamāṇāni, idaṃ punar api na vijñāyate yad āryasubhūtiḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣate pravyāharati deśayati vibhajaty uttānīkaroti upadiśati.
body.translated_text: Then certain <s>devaputra</s>s in that assembly had this thought: The words, spells, utterances, and expressions of <s>yakṣa</s>s that are known — even those, when being recited, [can be understood]; but this cannot be understood — that which the noble <s>Subhūti</s> speaks, utters, teaches, analyzes, elucidates, and instructs concerning the perfection of wisdom.

body.text: athāyuṣmān subhūtis teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāya tān devaputrān āmantrayate sma, na vijñāyate devaputrāṇām āmantrayate.
body.translated_text: Then Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, knowing with his mind the thoughts of those <s>devaputra</s>s, addressed those <s>devaputra</s>s: 'Is it not understood, O <s>devaputra</s>s?'

body.text: devaputrā āhuḥ: na vijñāyate āryasubhūte.
body.translated_text: The <s>devaputra</s>s said: 'It is not understood, noble <s>Subhūti</s>.'

body.text: subhūtir āha: tathā hi devaputrā ekākṣaram api na pravyāhrite tan na śruyate yan na śruyate tan na vijñāyate. tat kasya hetoḥ? na hy akṣarāṇi prajñāpāramitā na cātra kaścid deśayitā na śrotā na vijñātā. tat kasya hetoḥ? anakṣarā hi devaputrās tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ bodhiḥ tad yathāpi nāma devaputrās tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho buddhanirmitaṃ nirmimīte. sa ca punar nirmitaś catasraparṣado nirmimītaḥ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: For indeed, <s>devaputra</s>s, not a single syllable is uttered — what is not uttered is not heard, and what is not heard is not understood. For what reason? Because the perfection of wisdom is not syllables, and here there is no teacher, no hearer, and no one who understands. For what reason? Because, <s>devaputra</s>s, the awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, perfectly awakened ones is without syllables. Just as, <s>devaputra</s>s, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened one creates a magical creation (<s>buddhanirmita</s>), and that magical creation further creates the four assemblies — monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen —

body.text: atha sa nirmitaḥ tābhyo nirmitābhyaś catasṛbhyaḥ parṣadbhyo dharmaṃ deśayet. tat kiṃ manyadhve? devaputrāḥ. api tu tatra parṣadi kenacid deśitaṃ bhavet? kenacic chrutam ājñātaṃ ca bhavet?
body.translated_text: and then that magical creation teaches the Dharma to those four magically created assemblies — what do you think, <s>devaputra</s>s? Has anything been taught by anyone in that assembly? Has anything been heard or understood by anyone?

body.text: āhuḥ: no hīdaṃ bhadanta subhūte.
body.translated_text: They said: No indeed, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>.

body.translated_text: Then those <s>devaputra</s>s had this thought: 'The noble elder <s>Subhūti</s> will surely clarify and elucidate the perfection of wisdom!' — yet he teaches what is deeper than the deep and enters what is subtler than the subtle.

body.translated_text: Then Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, knowing with his mind the thoughts of those <s>devaputra</s>s, said this to them: Indeed, <s>devaputra</s>s, form is neither deep nor subtle; feeling is neither deep nor subtle; perception is neither deep nor subtle; formations are neither deep nor subtle; consciousness is neither deep nor subtle. body.text: na khalu punar iha dharmadeśanāyāṃ srotaāpannaḥ prajñapito na srotaāpattiphalaṃ prajñapitaṃ, na sakṛdāgāmī prajñapito na sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prajñapitaṃ, nānāgāmī prajñapito nānāgāmīphalaṃ prajñapitaṃ, nārhat prajñapito nārhattvaṃ na prajñapitaṃ, na pratyekabuddhaḥ prajñapito na pratyekabodhiḥ prajñapitā, na bodhisattvaḥ prajñapito na bodhisattvabhūmayaḥ prajñapitāḥ, na buddhaḥ prajñapito na bodhiḥ prajñapitā, nākṣarāṇi prajñapitāni.
body.translated_text: Moreover, in this teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, the stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) is not designated, nor is the fruit of stream-entry designated; the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) is not designated, nor is the fruit of once-returning designated; the non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) is not designated, nor is the fruit of non-returning designated; the <s>arhat</s> is not designated, nor is <s>arhat</s>ship designated; the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> is not designated, nor is <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening designated; the <s>bodhisattva</s> is not designated, nor are the stages of the <s>bodhisattva</s> (<s>bodhisattvabhūmi</s>) designated; the <s>Buddha</s> is not designated, nor is awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) designated; nor are syllables designated.

body.text: athāyuṣmān subhūtis tān devaputrān etad avocat: evam etad devaputrā evam etad iti tad anabhilāpyā tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddānāṃ bodhiḥ, apravyāhārā sā na kenacid chrutā na vijñātā.
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to those <s>devaputra</s>s: So it is, <s>devaputra</s>s, so it is! The awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the <s>Arhat</s>s, the Perfectly Awakened Ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), is indeed inexpressible (<s>anabhilāpya</s>); it is beyond verbal expression (<s>apravyāhāra</s>) — it has been heard by no one and cognized by no one.

body.text: tena hi devaputrā ye srotaāpattiphale sthātukāmāḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkartukāmā nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya, ye sakṛdāgāmiphale sthātukāmāḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkartukāmā nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya, ye 'nāgāmīphale sthātukāmā anāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkartukāmā nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya, ye 'rhattve sthātukāmā arhattvaṃ sākṣātkartukāmā nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya, ye pratyekabodhau sthātukāmāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ sākṣātkartukamā nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya, ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau sthātukāmā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ sākṣātkartukāmā nemāṃ kṣāntim anāgamya.
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>devaputra</s>s, those who wish to abide in the fruit of stream-entry and wish to directly realize the fruit of stream-entry — they cannot do so without attaining this patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>). Those who wish to abide in the fruit of once-returning and wish to directly realize the fruit of once-returning — they cannot do so without attaining this patient acceptance. Those who wish to abide in the fruit of non-returning and wish to directly realize the fruit of non-returning — they cannot do so without attaining this patient acceptance. Those who wish to abide in <s>arhat</s>ship and wish to directly realize <s>arhat</s>ship — they cannot do so without attaining this patient acceptance. Those who wish to abide in <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening and wish to directly realize <s>pratyeka</s>-awakening — they cannot do so without attaining this patient acceptance. Those who wish to abide in unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) and wish to directly realize unsurpassed perfect awakening — they cannot do so without attaining this patient acceptance.

body.text: evaṃ khalu devaputrā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prathamacittotpādam upādāya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyaṃ, apravyāhārā śravaṇatām upādāya.
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>devaputra</s>s, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, from the first generation of the mind of awakening (<s>prathamacittotpāda</s>), should abide in the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), from the standpoint of hearing that which is beyond verbal expression.

body.text: śatasāhasryāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā dvitīyakhaṇḍe caturdaśamaḥ parivartaḥ samāptaḥ.
body.translated_text: End of the fourteenth chapter in the second section of the Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā.

body.text: atha khalu teṣāṃ devaputrāṇām etad abhūt: kīdṛgrūpāḥ subhūteḥ sthavirasya dhārmaśravaṇikā eṣṭavyāḥ?
body.translated_text: Then those <s>devaputra</s>s had this thought: What kind of listeners of the <s>Dharma</s> should be sought for the elder <s>Subhūti</s>?

body.text: athāyuṣmān subhūtis teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāya tān devaputrān etad avocat: māyopamā me devaputrā dharmadeśanā māyopamā me devaputrā dhārmaśravaṇikā eṣṭavyāḥ. nirmitopamā me devaputrā dharmadeśanā nirmitopamā me devaputrā dhārmaśravaṇikā eṣṭavyāḥ. te naiva kiṃcic chroṣyanti na sākṣātkariṣyanti.
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, knowing with his mind the mental reflection of those <s>devaputra</s>s, said this to those <s>devaputra</s>s: My teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>devaputra</s>s, is like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>); my listeners of the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>devaputra</s>s, should be sought as like an illusion. My teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>devaputra</s>s, is like a magical creation (<s>nirmita</s>); my listeners of the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>devaputra</s>s, should be sought as like a magical creation. They will neither hear anything nor directly realize anything.

body.text: atha khalu devaputrā āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtim etad avocan: kiṃ punar bhadanta subhūte māyopamās te sattvā māyopamās te dhārmaśravaṇikā, nirmitopamās te sattvā nirmitopamās te dhārmaśravaṇikāḥ.
body.translated_text: Then those <s>devaputra</s>s said this to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are those beings like an illusion and those listeners of the <s>Dharma</s> like an illusion? Are those beings like a magical creation and those listeners of the <s>Dharma</s> like a magical creation?

body.text: subhūtir āha: evam etad devaputrā evam etad, māyopamās te sattvā māyopamās te dhārmaśravaṇikā, nirmitopamās te sattvā nirmitopamās te dhārmaśravaṇikāḥ. svapnopamās te devaputrāḥ sattvāḥ, māyopamās te devaputrāḥ sattvāḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: So it is, <s>devaputra</s>s, so it is! Those beings are like an illusion and those listeners of the <s>Dharma</s> are like an illusion; those beings are like a magical creation and those listeners of the <s>Dharma</s> are like a magical creation. Those beings, <s>devaputra</s>s, are like a dream; those beings, <s>devaputra</s>s, are like an illusion.

body.translated_text: Then those <s>devaputra</s>s said this to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: You say, <s>Subhūti</s>, that even awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is like a dream, like an illusion. Do you then also say that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is like a dream, like an illusion?

body.text: subhūtir āha: nirvāṇam apy ahaṃ devaputrāḥ svapnopamaṃ māyopamaṃ vadāmi, sacet tato nirvāṇād anyaḥ kaścid dharmo viśiṣṭataro bhavet, tam apy ahaṃ svapnopamaṃ māyopamaṃ vadeyam. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi devaputrāḥ svapnaś ca māyā ca nirvāṇaṃ cādvayam etad advaidhīkāram.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: I say, <s>devaputra</s>s, that even <s>nirvāṇa</s> is like a dream, like an illusion. If there were any <s>dharma</s> more excellent than <s>nirvāṇa</s>, I would say that it too is like a dream, like an illusion. For what reason? For indeed, <s>devaputra</s>s, dream, illusion, and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is non-dual (<s>advaya</s>), without division (<s>advaidhīkāra</s>).

body.translated_text: And the displays of superknowledge (<s>abhijñāvikrīḍita</s>) of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s are taught. Thus they will become ones whose superknowledges do not decline, and they will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field. And whatever roots of merit they desire — to honor, respect, revere, and worship those <s>Buddha Bhagavat</s>s — those roots of merit will be accomplished accordingly. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> they hear in the presence of those <s>Buddha Bhagavat</s>s will never be cut off, until they attain the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). And they will always be in concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), undistracted, through the practice of concentration.

body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: For what reason, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are the three vehicles taught in detail in this perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), through the practice of non-apprehension? For what reason, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the support of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s taught? body.text: bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyābhijñāvikrīḍitāny upadiśyate. evaṃkila bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranta upapādukā bhaviṣyanti. evam abhijñāsv aparihāṇadharmāṇo bhaviṣyanti, buddhakṣetrād buddhakṣetraṃ saṃkramiṣyanti, yaiś ca kuśalamūlair ākāṅkṣiṣyanti. tān buddhān bhagavataḥ satkartuṃ gurukartuṃ mānayituṃ pūjayituṃ tāni tathārūpāṇi kuśalamūlāni samṛtsyanti, yañ ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatām antikād dharmaṃ śroṣyanti, sa na kadācid ācchetsyate, yāvat sarvākārajñatām anuprāpsyanti. sadāsamāhitāś ca bhaviṣyanty avikṣiptasamāhitayogena. asaṅgapratibhānaś ca bhaviṣyanti, anācchedyapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti. samāhitapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, yuktapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, śliṣṭapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, arthavatpratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, sarvalokābhyudgataviśiṣṭapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhaviṣyanty anupalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: The displays of the superknowledges (<s>abhijñāvikrīḍita</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> are taught. Thus indeed, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s practicing the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) will be spontaneously born. Thus, having the nature of non-decline in the superknowledges, they will travel from <s>Buddha</s>-field to <s>Buddha</s>-field, and whatever roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) they desire — to honor, revere, respect, and worship those <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones — those very roots of merit will prosper; and whatever <s>Dharma</s> they will hear from those <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, will never be cut off, until they attain the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). They will always be concentrated, undistracted through the practice of concentration. They will possess unobstructed eloquence, uninterrupted eloquence, concentrated eloquence, skillful eloquence, well-connected eloquence, meaningful eloquence, and eloquence surpassing all worlds — the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s will possess these through the practice of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>).

body.translated_text: The displays of superknowledge (<s>abhijñāvikrīḍita</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> are taught. Indeed, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s practicing in the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) will be spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>). Thus, they will be ones whose superknowledges do not decline, and they will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field. With whatever roots of merit they aspire to, they will honor, revere, esteem, and worship those <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>s, and they will accumulate such roots of merit. And the <s>Dharma</s> that they hear from those <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>s will never be cut off, until they attain the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). They will always be concentrated and undistracted through the practice of concentration. They will have unobstructed eloquence (<s>asaṅgapratibhāna</s>), uninterrupted eloquence (<s>anācchedyapratibhāna</s>), concentrated eloquence (<s>samāhitapratibhāna</s>), well-reasoned eloquence (<s>yuktapratibhāna</s>), coherent eloquence (<s>śliṣṭapratibhāna</s>), meaningful eloquence (<s>arthavatpratibhāna</s>), and eloquence surpassing all worlds (<s>sarvalokābhyudgataviśiṣṭapratibhāna</s>) — the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s through the method of non-apprehension.

body.text: bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyābhijñāvikrīḍitāny upadiśyante. evaṃkila bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranta upapādukā bhaviṣyanti. evam abhijñāṃ ca parihāṇadharmāṇo bhavanti, buddhakṣetrād buddhakṣetraṃ saṃkramiṣyanti, yaiś ca kuśalamūlair ākāṅkṣiṣyanti. tān buddhān bhagavataḥ satkartuṃ gurukartuṃ mānayituṃ pūjayituṃ tāni tathārūpāṇi kuśalamūlāni samṛtsyanti, yañ ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatām antikād dharmaṃ śroṣyanti. sa na kadācid ācchetsyate, yāvat sarvākārajñatām anuprāpsyanti. sadāsamāhitāś ca bhaviṣyanty avikṣiptāś ca samāhitayogena. asaṅgapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, anācchedyapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti. samāhitapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, yuktapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, śliṣṭapratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, arthavatpratibhānāś ca bhaviṣyanti, sarvalokābhyudgataviśiṣṭapratibhānaś ca bhaviṣyanti bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anupalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: The displays of the superknowledges (<s>abhijñāvikrīḍita</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> are taught. Thus indeed, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s practicing the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) will be spontaneously born. Thus, having the nature of non-decline in the superknowledges, they will travel from <s>Buddha</s>-field to <s>Buddha</s>-field, and whatever roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) they desire — to honor, revere, respect, and worship those <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones — those very roots of merit will prosper; and whatever <s>Dharma</s> they will hear from those <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, will never be cut off, until they attain the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). They will always be concentrated, undistracted through the practice of concentration. They will possess unobstructed eloquence, uninterrupted eloquence, concentrated eloquence, skillful eloquence, well-connected eloquence, meaningful eloquence, and eloquence surpassing all worlds — the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s through the practice of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>).

body.text: atha khalu śakrasya devānām indrasyaitad abhūt: asyāḥ sarvadharmavṛṣṭeḥ subhūtinā sthavireṇa bhāṣyamāṇāyāḥ yan nv ahaṃ puṣyāṇy abhinirmāya buddhaṃ bhagavataṃ bodhisattvāṃś ca mahāsattvān bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca subhūtisthaviram asyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pūjākarmaṇe avakireyam abhyavakireyam abhiprākireyaṃ, yāvantaś ca trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau cāturmahārājikā devās trāyastriṃśā devā yāmā devās tuṣitā devāḥ nirmāṇaratayo devāḥ paranirmitavaśavartino devā brahmakāyikā devā brahmapurohitā devā brāhmaparṣadyā devā mahābrahmāṇo devā ābhā devāḥ parīttābhā devā apramāṇābhā devāḥ ābhāsvarā devāḥ śubhā devāḥ parittaśubhā devā apramāṇaśubhā devāḥ śubhakṛtsnā devā bṛhā devāḥ parīttabṛhā devā apramāṇabṛhā devā bṛhatpharā devā abṛhā devā atapā devāḥ sudṛśā devā sudarśanā devā akaniṣṭhā devās teṣām etad abhūvan: asyā dharmavṛṣṭeḥ subhūtinā sthavireṇa bhāṣyamāṇāyāḥ. yaṃ nūnaṃ vayaṃ puṣpāṇy abhinirmāya buddhaṃ bhagavataṃ bodhisattvāṃś ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca subhūtisthavirañ cāsyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pūjākarmaṇe avikireyam.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, had this thought: While this rain of all dharmas is being spoken by the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, I should magically create flowers and shower them upon the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s, the community of monks, and the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, as an act of worship for this perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). And all the gods in this great trichiliocosm — the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s> gods, the Great <s>Brahmā</s> gods, the <s>Ābha</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Śubha</s> gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Bṛha</s> gods, the <s>Parīttabṛha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇabṛha</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, the <s>Abṛha</s> gods, the <s>Atapa</s> gods, the <s>Sudṛśa</s> gods, the <s>Sudarśana</s> gods, the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — they also had this thought: While this rain of <s>Dharma</s> is being spoken by the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, let us magically create flowers and shower them upon the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva</s>s, the community of monks, and the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, as an act of worship for this perfection of wisdom.

body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Subhūti</s> had this thought: Never before have I seen such excellent flowers in any of the divine abodes (

body.text: atha śakro devānām indraḥ subhūteḥ sthavirasya cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāya āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtisthaviram etad avocan: aniryātāni bhadanta subhūte imāni puṣpāṇi, na manomayāni na stambhaniryātāni.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, knowing with his mind the mental deliberation of the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, said this to the Venerable elder <s>Subhūti</s>: Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, these flowers have not grown [from stalks]; they are not mind-made and not stalk-grown.

body.text: subhūtir āha: yat punaḥ kauśika evaṃ vadasi, aniryātānīmāni puṣpāṇi nemāni puṣpāṇi manoniryātāni na stambhaniryātāni, yāni kauśikāniryātāni netāni puṣpāṇi.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: But <s>Kauśika</s>, you say these flowers have not grown, and these flowers are not mind-produced and not stalk-grown. <s>Kauśika</s>, that which has not grown — those are not flowers.

body.text: śakra āha: kiṃ punar bhadanta subhūte, imāny eva puṣpāṇy aniryātāni, atha rūpam apy anirjātam evaṃ vedanāpy aniyātā saṃjñāpy aniryātā saṃskārā apy aniryātā vijñānam apy aniryātam.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are only these flowers not produced, or is form too not produced, and likewise feeling not produced, perception not produced, formations not produced, and consciousness not produced?

body.text: subhūtir āha: yat kauśikaivaṃ vadasi, na kauśikemāny eva puṣpāny aniryātānīti, rūpam api kauśikāniryātaṃ yac cāniryātaṃ na tad rūpaṃ, vedanāpi kauśikāniryātā yā cāniryātā na sā vedanā, saṃjñāpi kauśikāniryātā yā cāniryātā na sā saṃjñā, saṃskārā api kauśikāniryātā ye cāniryātā na te saṃskārāḥ, vijñānam api kauśikāniryātaṃ yac cāniryātaṃ na tad vijñānam.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: That, <s>Kauśika</s>, you say so — it is not, <s>Kauśika</s>, that only these flowers are not produced. Form too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not form; feeling too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not feeling; perception too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not perception; formations too, <s>Kauśika</s>, are not produced, and what is not produced is not formations; consciousness too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not consciousness.

body.text: cakṣuḥ kauśikāniryātaṃ yac cāniryātaṃ na tac cakṣuḥ, śrotraṃ kauśikāniryātaṃ yac cāniryātaṃ na tac chrotraṃ, ghrāṇaṃ kauśikāniryātaṃ yac cāniryātaṃ na tad ghrāṇaṃ, jihvā kauśikāniryātā yā cāniryātā na sā jihvā, kāyaḥ kauśikāniryāto yaś cāniryāto na sa kāyaḥ, manaḥ kauśikāniryātaṃ yac cāniryātaṃ na tan manaḥ.
body.translated_text: The eye, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not the eye; the ear, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not the ear; the nose, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not the nose; the tongue, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not the tongue; the body, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not the body; the mind, <s>Kauśika</s>, is not produced, and what is not produced is not the mind.
