body.text: atha khalu śakrasya devānām indrasyaitad abhūt: gambhīraprajño batāyaṃ subhūtisthaviro yatra hi nāma prajñaptiṃ ca na virodhayati dharmatāñ copadiśati.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, had this thought: How profoundly wise indeed is this elder <s>Subhūti</s>, that he does not contradict conventional designation (<s>prajñapti</s>) while teaching the true nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>).

body.text: atha bhagavān śakraṃ devānām indram āmantrayate sma: evam etat kauśikaivam etad gambhīraprajño batāyaṃ subhūtiḥ sthaviraḥ yatra hi nāmaṃ prajñaptiṃ ca na virodhayati dharmatāṃ copadiśati.
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is! The elder <s>Subhūti</s> is indeed of profound wisdom, for he does not contradict conventional designation (<s>prajñapti</s>) and yet teaches the true nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>).

body.text: atha śakro devānām indro bhagavantam etad avocat: kathaṃ bhagavan subhūtiḥ sthaviraḥ prajñaptiṃ ca na virodhayati dharmatāṃ copadiśati?
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: How is it, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that the elder <s>Subhūti</s> does not contradict conventional designation and yet teaches the true nature of things?

body.text: evam ukte bhagavāñ chakraṃ devānām indram etad avocat: rūpaṃ kauśika prajñaptimātraṃ yat prajñaptimātraṃ sā dharmatā tāṃ subhūtiḥ sthaviro 'virodhenopadiśati, vedanā kauśika prajñaptimātrā yat prajñaptimātraṃ sā dharmatā tāṃ subhūtiḥ sthaviro 'virodhenopadiśati, saṃjñā kauśika prajñaptimātraṃ yat prajñaptimātraṃ sā dharmatā tāṃ subhūtiḥ sthaviro 'virodhenopadiśati, saṃskārāḥ kauśika prajñaptimātraṃ yat prajñaptimātraṃ sā dharmatā tāṃ subhūtiḥ sthaviro 'virodhenopadiśati, vijñānaṃ kauśika prajñaptimātraṃ yat prajñaptimātraṃ sā dharmatā tāṃ subhūtiḥ sthaviro 'virodhenopadiśati. tat kasya hetoḥ? yā kauśika dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā sā na rudhyate na virudhyate, yā na rūdhyate na virūdhyate tāṃ subhūtiḥ sthavira upadiśati na ca virodhayati.

The once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), <s>Kauśika</s>, is a mere designation; that which is a mere designation is the nature of dharmas; that is what the elder <s>Subhūti</s> teaches without contradiction. body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is! Just as the <s>Bhagavat</s> has taught all dharmas as mere designations. Thus indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having understood all dharmas as mere designations, should train in the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, there is no acquisition of form — for form does not grasp form, based on internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>). For indeed, there is no acquisition of formations — for formations do not grasp formations, based on internal-and-external emptiness. For indeed, there is no acquisition of consciousness — for consciousness does not grasp consciousness, based on internal-and-external emptiness.

body.text: evaṃ khalv āyuṣmañ chāradvatīputra bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvadharmāṇām anutpādāyānirodhāyānāgrahāyānutsargāyāsaṃkleśāyāvyavadānāyānācayāyānāpacayāyāhānaye avṛddhaye prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitvā sarvākārajñatāyāṃ niryāsyaty aśikṣā aniryānayogena.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, said this to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: This is your power, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, this is your authority, that the Noble (

body.text: śakra āha: niradhiṣṭhāṇeṣu bhadanta subhūte sarvadharmeṣu katham evaṃ vadasi? tathāgatasyaiṣānubhāvas tathāgatasyaitad adhiṣṭhānaṃ, na cātra niradhiṣṭhānadharmatāyās tathāgata upalabhyate, na cātra tathāgatāyās tathāgata upalabhyate.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, when all dharmas are without foundation, how do you speak thus? body.text: subhūtir āha: evam etat kauśikaivam etat, nānyatra niradhiṣṭhānadharmatāyās tathāgata upalabhyate, nānyatra tathātāyās tathāgata upalabhyate, na ca niradhiṣṭhānadharmatāyāṃ tathāgata upalabhyate, na tathāgate niradhiṣṭhānadharmatopalabhyate, na ca tathatāyāṃ tathāgata upalabhyate, na tathāgate tathatopalabhyate,
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. The <s>Tathāgata</s> is not apprehended apart from the true nature of being without foundation, nor is the <s>Tathāgata</s> apprehended apart from suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). body.text: yat punaḥ kauśikaivaṃ vadasi, kuto bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitā gaveṣitavyeti?
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Kauśika</s>, as you say thus: 'From where should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> seek the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>)?'

body.text: na kauśika rūpato gaveṣitavyā nānyatra rūpato gaveṣitavyā, na vedanāto gaveṣitavyā nānyatra vedanāto gaveṣitavyā, na saṃjñāto gaveṣitavyā nānyatra saṃjñāto gaveṣitavyā, na saṃskārebhyo gaveṣitavyā nānyatra saṃskārebhyo gaveṣitavyā, na vijñānato gaveṣitavyā nānyatra vijñānato gaveṣitavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśika yac ca rūpaṃ yā ca vedanā yā ca saṃjñā ye ca saṃskārā yac ca vijñānaṃ, yaś ca bodhisattvo yā ca prajñāpāramitā yā ca mahākaruṇā yā ca gaveṣaṇā sarvam ete dharmā na saṃyuktā na visaṃyuktā arūpiṇo 'nidarśanā apratighā ekalakṣaṇā yad utālakṣaṇāḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, it should not be sought from form (<s>rūpa</s>), nor should it be sought apart from form; it should not be sought from feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), nor should it be sought apart from feeling; it should not be sought from perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), nor should it be sought apart from perception; it should not be sought from formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), nor should it be sought apart from formations; it should not be sought from consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), nor should it be sought apart from consciousness. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, that which is form, that which is feeling, that which is perception, that which is formations, that which is consciousness, and that which is a <s>bodhisattva</s>, that which is the perfection of wisdom, that which is great compassion, and that which is the seeking — all these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, invisible, non-resistant, of one characteristic, namely characteristiclessness.

Why is that? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, the measure of the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness is not apprehended. Just as, <s>Kauśika</s>, the measure of space is not apprehended, so too, <s>Kauśika</s>, the measure of the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness is not apprehended. By the immeasurability of space, the immeasurability of the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; by the immeasurability of the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the immeasurability of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,

body.text: śakra āha: nedaṃ bhadanta subhūte dharmādhivacanaṃ nādharmādhivacanam āgantukam etan nāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptam avastukam etan nāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptam anārambaṇam etan nāmadheyaṃ prakṣiptaṃ yad uta sattvaḥ sattva iti.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, this is not a designation of a dharma, nor a designation of a non-dharma. This name has been assigned adventitiously; this name has been assigned without substance; this name has been assigned without a basis — what is called 'a being, a being.'

body.text: subhūtir āha: tat kiṃ manyase? kauśika kācid iha prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sattvaparidīpanā kṛtā.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Has any illumination of beings been made in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?

body.text: śakra aha: no hīdaṃ bhadanta subhūte.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: No indeed, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>.

body.text: subhūtir āha: yatra kauśika na sattvaparidīpanā kṛtā kācit tatra sattvānantatā sacet kauśika tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpān tiṣṭha ca sattvaḥ sattva iti vācaṃ bhāṣeta, tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu tatra kaścit sattva utpadyate vā niruddhyate vā.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: Where, <s>Kauśika</s>, no illumination of beings whatsoever has been made, there is the infinitude of beings. If, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, were to remain for eons equal to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> and were to utter the word 'being, being,' what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would any being arise or cease thereby?

body.text: śakra āha: no hīdaṃ bhadanta subhūte. tat kasya hetoḥ? ādi viśuddhatvā sattvasya.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: No indeed, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>. Why is that? Because a being is primordially pure.

body.text: subhūtir āha: tad anena te kauśika paryāyeṇa sattvānantatyā prajñāpāramitānantatā veditavyā.
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, you should understand that by the infinitude of beings comes the infinitude of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha sendrakā devāḥ sabrahmakā devāḥ saprajñāpatikā devāḥ sanārīnaragaṇās triskṛtvā udānam udānayati sma, aho svākhyāto dharmaḥ aho svākhyāto dharmā aho svākhyāto dharmasya dharmatā yeyaṃ subhūtinā sthavireṇa bhāṣyate yad uta tathāgataprādurbhāvo ya tathāgatasyādhiṣṭhānena tathāgatasyānubhāvena sūcyate deśyate prakāsyate.
body.translated_text: Then the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, the gods together with <s>Brahmā</s>, the gods together with <s>Prajāpati</s>, with their hosts of men and women, uttered an exclamation three times: 'Oh, the <s>Dharma</s> is well taught! Oh, the <s>Dharma</s> is well taught! Oh, the true nature of the <s>Dharma</s> is well taught — that which is spoken by the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, which is indicated, taught, and illuminated through the appearance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by the empowerment and might of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: api nu tathāgatam eva vayaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ dhārayiṣyāmaḥ. yo na yā prajñāpāramitayā avirahitā bhaviṣyati, na ca nāma kaścid dharma upalabhyate.
body.translated_text: We will indeed, Bhagavān, regard as a <s>Tathāgata</s> that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who will not be separated from this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, yet no dharma whatsoever is apprehended —

body.text: rūpaṃ vā vedanā vā saṃjñā vā saṃskārā vā vijñānaṃ vā.

body.text: anyair anyaiś cāparimāṇair buddhadharmair avirahito 'bhūvan tac cānupalambhayogena. tadāhaṃ devaputrās tena dīpaṃkareṇa tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena vyākṛtānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ mānavānāgate 'dhvani bhadrakalpe, asminn eva lokadhātāv asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpaiḥ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ sāstā devānāṃ ca maṇuṣyāṇāṃ buddho buddho bhagavān.
body.translated_text: And I was endowed with other innumerable Buddha-qualities, and that too through the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>). Then, sons of the gods, I was prophesied by that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening: 'You, young man, will become in the future, in the Fortunate Aeon (<s>Bhadrakalpa</s>), in this very world-system, after incalculable aeons, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One.'

body.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s, monks, nuns, male lay followers, female lay followers, sons of good family, daughters of good family, sons of the gods, or daughters of the gods will take up this perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), will retain it, will master it, will cultivate it, and will extensively illuminate it for others, and will not be separated from the mind directed toward the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) — <s>Māra</s> the Evil One and the deities of <s>Māra</s>'s host will not find an opening against them.

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi taiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhiś ca rūpaśūnyataiva svadhiṣṭhitā bhaviṣyati, vedanāśūnyataiva svadhiṣṭhitā bhaviṣyati, saṃjñāśūnyataiva svadhiṣṭhitā bhaviṣyati, saṃskārāśūnyataiva svadhiṣṭhitā bhaviṣyati, vijñānaśūnyataiva svadhiṣṭhitā bhaviṣyati. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi na śūnyatā śūnyatāyā avatāraṃ labhate, nānimittam ānimittasyāvatāraṃ labhate, nāpraṇihitam apraṇihitasyāvatāraṃ labhate.
body.translated_text: For what reason? For indeed, those sons and daughters of good family will have established themselves in the emptiness of form (<s>rūpaśūnyatā</s>), will have established themselves in the emptiness of feeling (<s>vedanāśūnyatā</s>), will have established themselves in the emptiness of perception (<s>saṃjñāśūnyatā</s>), will have established themselves in the emptiness of formations (<s>saṃskāraśūnyatā</s>), will have established themselves in the emptiness of consciousness (<s>vijñānaśūnyatā</s>). For what reason? For indeed, emptiness does not gain entry into emptiness, signlessness does not gain entry into signlessness, wishlessness does not gain entry into wishlessness.

body.translated_text: For indeed, by those sons of good family or daughters of good family, the emptiness of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatāśūnyatā</s>) alone will have been established as their own ground; the emptiness of the knowledge of path-aspects alone will have been established as their own ground; the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects alone will have been established as their own ground. For what reason? For indeed, the inherent nature of those [dharmas] is not found — neither that by which one might gain entry, nor that into which one might gain entry, nor that whose entry one might gain.

body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, neither humans nor non-humans will gain entry — seeking to find an opening — into those sons of good family or daughters of good family. For what reason? For indeed, by those sons of good family or daughters of good family, toward all beings (

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi taiḥ kulaputrair vā kuladuhitṛbhir vā dānapāramitāyāṃ caradbhiḥ sarvasattvā samyakparihāreṇa nopasthitā yo vā kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau, cāturmahārājakāyikā devāḥ trāyastriṃśā devā yāmā devās tuṣitā devā nirmāṇaratayo devāḥ paranirmitavaśavartino devāḥ brahmakāyikā devā brahmapārṣadyā devā brahmapurohitā devā mahābrahmā devā ābhāsvarā devāḥ śubhakṛtsnā devā bṛhatphalā devā anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye saṃprasthitāḥ, yaiś ca devaputrair iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā na srutā nodgṛhītā na dhāritā paryavāptā tair devaputrair iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā śrotavyodgṛhītavyā dhārayitavyā paryavāptavyā yoniso manasikartavyā sarvākārajñatācittena cāvirahitena bhavitavyam.
body.translated_text: For what reason? For indeed, by those sons of good family or daughters of good family, while practicing the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), all beings have been properly cared for. Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>), the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> realm, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, and the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods — those who have set forth toward unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and those divine sons by whom this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has not been heard, taken up, retained, or mastered — by those divine sons this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be heard, taken up, retained, and mastered; it should be properly attended to in the mind; and they should not be separated from the mind of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatācitta</s>).

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika ye kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś cemāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti yonisaś ca manasikariṣyanti sarvākārajñatācittena cāvirahito bhaviṣyanti.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, master it, and properly attend to it in the mind — they will not be separated from the mind of the knowledge of all aspects.

body.text: na khalu punas teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca śūnyāgāragatānāṃ vābhyavakāśagatānāṃ cotpathagatānāṃ vā bhayaṃ vā stambhitatvaṃ vā bhaviṣyanti. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi taiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhiś cādhyātmaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, bahirdhāśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, śūnyatāśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, mahāśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, paramārthaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, saṃskṛtaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, asaṃskṛtaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, atyantaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, anavarāgraśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, anavakāraśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, prakṛtiśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, sarvadharmaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, svalakṣaṇaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, anupalambhaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, abhāvaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, svabhāvaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena, abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāsu bhāvitā tac cānupalambhayogena.
body.translated_text: Moreover, those sons and daughters of good family who have gone to an empty dwelling, or gone to the open, or gone to a path will not have fear or paralysis. For what reason? For those sons and daughters of good family have cultivated internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension; have cultivated the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension.

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ yāvantas trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau cāturmahārājakāyikā devā trāyastriṃśā devā yāmā devās tuṣitā devā nirmāṇaratayo devāḥ paranirmitavaśavartino devā brahmakāyikā devā ābhāsvarā devāḥ śubhakṛtsnā devā bṛhatphalā devāḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devās te sarve bhagavantam etad avocan: vayaṃ bhagavan teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca satatasamitaṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmo ya imāṃ gaṃbhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitām adhimokṣante udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti yonisaś ca manasikariṣyanti, parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, avirahitaś ca bhaviṣyanti sarvākārajñatā manasikāreṇa. tat kasya hetoḥ? bodhisattvaṃ hi bhagavan mahāsattvam āgamya narakā ucchidyante, yamaloka ucchidyante devadāridyam ucchidyante manuṣyadāridyam ucchidyante, ityupadravopasargā sarva ucchidyante vinasyanti, na bhavanti durbhikṣakāntārāḥ sarva ucchidyante bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam āgamya daśānāṃ kuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ loke purādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇām apramāṇānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, catasṛṇām ārūpyasamāpattīnāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, pañcānām abhijñānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati.
body.translated_text: Then at that time, all the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, and the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> gods in the great trichiliocosm — all of them said this to the Blessed One: Blessed One, we shall constantly provide protection, shelter, and guardianship to those sons and daughters of good family who have faith in this profound perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), who will take it up, hold it, recite it, master it, and attend to it wisely, and who will explain it extensively to others, and who will not be separated from the mental attention to the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). For what reason? For, Blessed One, depending on the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the hells are cut off, the world of <s>Yama</s> is cut off, the poverty of gods is cut off, the poverty of humans is cut off, and all calamities and misfortunes are cut off, destroyed, and cease to exist. All famines and wastelands are cut off depending on the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Depending on the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the ten wholesome courses of action arise in the world, the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>) arise in the world, the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) arise in the world, the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) arise in the world, and the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) arise in the world.

body.text: dānapāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, śīlapāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, kṣāntipāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, vīryapāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, dhyānapāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, prajñāpāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati.
body.translated_text: The perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) arises in the world, the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) arises in the world, the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) arises in the world, the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) arises in the world, the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) arises in the world, the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) arises in the world.

body.text: adhyātmaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, bahirdhāśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, śūnyatāśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, mahāśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, paramārthaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, saṃskṛtaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, asaṃskṛtaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, atyantaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, anavarāgraśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, anavakāraśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, prakṛtiśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, sarvadharmaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, svalakṣaṇaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, anupalambhaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, abhāvaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, svabhāvaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati.
body.translated_text: Internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world, the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) arises in the world.

body.text: caturṇāṃ smṛtyupasthānānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇāṃ samyakprahāṇānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇām ṛddhipādānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, pañcānām indriyānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, pañcānāṃ balānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, saptānāṃ bodhyaṅgānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, āryāṣṭāṅgasya mārgasya loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇām āryasatyānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇām apramāṇānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇām ārūpyasamāpattīnāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, aṣṭānāṃ vimokṣāṇāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, navānām anupūrvavihārasamāpattīnāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, trayāṇāṃ vimokṣamukhānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, pañcānām abhijñānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, sarvasamādhīnāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, sarvadhāraṇīmukhānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, daśānāṃ tathāgatabalānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇāṃ vaiśāradyānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, catasṛṇāṃ pratisaṃvidāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, mahāmaitryā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, mahākaruṇāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, aṣṭādaśānām āveṇikabuddhadharmāṇāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, sarvajñatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, mārgākārajñatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, sarvākārajñatāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhavati.
body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) arise in the world, the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) arise in the world, the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) arise in the world, the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>) arise in the world, the five powers (<s>bala</s>) arise in the world, the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) arise in the world, the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>) arises in the world, the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>) arise in the world, the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>) arise in the world, the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) arise in the world, the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) arise in the world, the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) arise in the world, the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>) arise in the world, the three gateways of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>) arise in the world, the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) arise in the world, all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>) arise in the world, all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>) arise in the world, the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>) arise in the world, the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) arise in the world, the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) arise in the world, great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) arises in the world, great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) arises in the world, the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>) arise in the world, omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) arises in the world, the knowledge of path-aspects (<s>mārgākārajñatā</s>) arises in the world, the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) arises in the world.

body.text: bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam āgamya kṣatriyamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, brāhmaṇamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, gṛhapatimahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, rājānaś cakravartinaḥ prajñāyante, cāturmahārajakāyikā devāḥ prajñāyante, trāyastriṃśā devāḥ prajñāyante, yāmā devāḥ prajñāyante, tuṣitā devāḥ prajñāyante, nirmāṇaratayo devāḥ prajñāyante, paranirmitavaśavartino devāḥ prajñāyante, brahmakāyikā devāḥ prajñāyante, brahmapurohitā devāḥ prajñāyante, brahmapārṣadyā devāḥ prajñāyante, mahābrahmaṇo devāḥ prajñāyante, ābhāsvara devāḥ prajñāyante, parīttābhā devāḥ prajñāyante, apramāṇābhā devāḥ prajñāyante, ābhāsvarā devāḥ prajñāyante, śubhā devāḥ prajñāyante, parīttaśubhā devāḥ prajñāyante, apramāśubhā devāḥ prajñāyante, śubhakṛtsnā devāḥ prajñāyante, bṛhā devāḥ prajñāyante, parīttabṛhā devāḥ prajñāyante, apramāṇabṛhā devāḥ prajñāyante, bṛhatphalā devāḥ prajñāyante, abṛhā devāḥ prajñāyante, (

children.translated_text: ) the <s>Atapa</s> gods come into being, the <s>Sudṛśa</s> gods come into being, the <s>Sudarśana</s> gods come into being, the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods come into being.

body.translated_text: Depending on the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the great families of <s>Kṣatriya</s>s come into being, the great families of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s come into being, the great families of householders come into being, universal monarch kings (<s>rāja cakravartin</s>) come into being, the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods come into being, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods come into being, the <s>Yāma</s> gods come into being, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods come into being, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods come into being, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods come into being, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods come into being, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods come into being, the <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s> gods come into being, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods come into being, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods come into being, the <s>Parīttābhā</s> gods come into being, the <s>Apramāṇābhā</s> gods come into being, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods come into being, the <s>Śubha</s> gods come into being, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods come into being, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods come into being, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods come into being, the <s>Bṛhā</s> gods come into being, the <s>Parīttabṛha</s> gods come into being, the <s>Apramāṇabṛha</s> gods come into being, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods come into being, the <s>Abṛha</s> gods come into being (

body.text:
bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam āgamya srotaāpattiphalaṃ prajñāyate, srotaāpanno prajñāyate, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prajñāyate, sakṛdāgāmī prajñāyate, anāgāmiphalaṃ prajñāyate, anāgāmī prajñāyate, arhattvaṃ prajñāyate, arhan prajñāyate, pratyekabodhiḥ prajñāyate, pratyekabuddhaḥ prajñāyate,
bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam āgamya sattvaḥ paripākaḥ prajñāyate, buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiṃ prajñāyate, tathāgatā arhata samyaksaṃbuddhā loke prajñāyante, dharmacakrapravartaṃ prajñāyate, buddharatnaṃ prajñāyate, dharmaratnaṃ prajñāyate, saṃgharatnaṃ prajñāyate.
body.translated_text: Depending on the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>) comes into being, stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) come into being, the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>) comes into being, once-returners (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) come into being, the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) comes into being, non-returners (<s>anāgāmin</s>) come into being, <s>arhat</s>ship comes into being, <s>arhat</s>s come into being, solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>) comes into being, solitary awakened ones (<s>pratyekabuddha</s>) come into being. Depending on the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the ripening of beings comes into being, the purification of buddha-fields (<s>buddhakṣetrapariśuddhi</s>) comes into being, <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones come into being in the world, the turning of the wheel of the Dharma (<s>dharmacakrapravartana</s>) comes into being, the jewel of the <s>Buddha</s> comes into being, the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s> comes into being, the jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> comes into being.

body.text: anena ca bhagavan paryāyeṇa bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya sadevamānuṣāsureṇa lokena rakṣāvaraṇaguptiḥ saṃvidhyatavyā.
body.translated_text: And by this method, Blessed One, the world including its gods, humans, and <s>asura</s>s should provide protection, shelter, and guardianship to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: evam ukte bhagavāṃc chakraṃ devānām indram etad avocat: evam etad kauśika evam etad, bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam āgamya daśānāṃ kuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, caturṇām apramāṇānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, catasṛṇām ārūpyasamāpattīnāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, pañcānām abhijñānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati.
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. Depending on the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the ten wholesome courses of action arise in the world, the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>) arise in the world, the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) arise in the world, the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) arise in the world, and the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) arise in the world.

body.translated_text: were it to be completely filled with <s>śrāvaka</s>s and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, as dense as a reed thicket, or a sugar-cane grove, or a bamboo thicket, or a reed grove, or a forest of <s>śāri</s> birds, or a sesame field — and were some son or daughter of good family to honor, respect, and venerate them for their entire lifetime with all provisions — and were another to honor, respect, esteem, and venerate a single <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has just generated the first thought of awakening and who is not separated from the six perfections, this latter person would produce far, far more merit than the former. Why is that? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, depending on those <s>śrāvaka</s>s and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not discerned in the world, nor is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One discerned in the world.

body.translated_text: But, <s>Kauśika</s>, depending on the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, all <s>śrāvaka</s>s and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s are discerned in the world, and <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones are discerned in the world. body.text: Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā II-4
body.translated_text: <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> II-4

Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how these <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s, taking up, retaining, reciting, and mastering the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and attending to it wisely, grasp these qualities of the <s>Dharma</s>, ripen beings, purify buddha-fields, travel from buddha-field to buddha-field, attend upon the <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>Bhagavān</s>s, and with whatever roots of merit they wish to honor, respect, esteem, and venerate those <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>Bhagavān</s>s — those roots of merit are fulfilled. And the <s>Dharma</s> they hear from those <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>Bhagavān</s>s they do not forget, until they have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. And they grasp the excellence of family, the excellence of mother, the excellence of birth, the excellence of retinue, the excellence of marks, the excellence of radiance, the excellence of vision, the excellence of voice, the excellence of concentration, the excellence of retention. And through skillful means, having fashioned themselves into the form of a <s>Buddha</s>, they travel from world-system to world-system, and where there is no appearance of <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>Bhagavān</s>s, having gone there, they praise the perfection of giving, praise the perfection of morality, praise the perfection of patience, praise the perfection of vigor, praise the perfection of meditation, and praise the perfection of wisdom.

'So be it, Blessed One,' replied <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, to the Blessed One. body.text: ime te kauśika bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bodhisattvacārikāṃ caratā dṛṣṭadhārmikā na guṇānuśaṃsā bhaviṣyanti, saṃparāye cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhya dharmacakraṃ pravartya sattvānyathāpratiṣṭhāne pratiṣṭhāpyānupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyati.
body.translated_text: These, <s>Kauśika</s>, are the benefits and advantages visible in this very life for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct. And in the future, having fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), having turned the wheel of the Dharma (<s>dharmacakra</s>), having established beings who dwell on wrong foundations on the right foundation, he will attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> realm without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>).

body.text: ime kauśika bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya sāṃparāyikā guṇānuśaṃsā bhaviṣyanti.
body.translated_text: These, <s>Kauśika</s>, are the benefits and advantages for the future for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: ) yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, na tatra pṛthivīpradeśe māro vā mārakāyikā vā devatā anyatīrthikā vā parivrājakā ādhimānika vā pudgalāḥ śakṣyanty asyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā vigrahāya vā vivādāya vā virodhāya vāntardhānāya vā parākramitum uttare ca teṣāṃ guṇānuśaṃsā bhaviṣyanti. yadāsyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ śravaṇagrahaṇabhāvanābhir anupūrveṇa tribhir yānair niryāya duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyanti, tad yathāpi nāma kauśika maghinām auṣadhīḥ sarvaviṣapraśamaṇī tatrāśīviṣeṇa vā jantunā vā kṣudhābhibhūtenāhārānveṣiṇā kiṃcid eva prāṇijātaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavet. sa tat prāṇakajātaṃ khāditukāmatayānugacchet. atha tat prāṇakajātaṃ maraṇabhayabhītaṃ yena sā maghī nām' auṣadhis tenopasaṃkrāman tataḥ sa āśīviṣas tasyā auṣadhyā gandhenaiva pratyudāvartitavyaṃ manyeta. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tasyā auṣadhyā bhaiṣajyaguṇo yaṃ tasyāśīviṣasya tad viṣam abhibhavaty eva balavatī hi kauśika sā maghī auṣadhiḥ.
body.translated_text: ) and will properly attend to it in the mind, in that region of the earth neither <s>Māra</s>, nor the deities of <s>Māra</s>'s host, nor heretical wandering ascetics, nor conceited individuals will be able to strive for disputation, quarrel, opposition, or disappearance against this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; and moreover, superior benefits of qualities will arise for them. Through hearing, grasping, and cultivating this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will gradually go forth by the three vehicles and make an end of suffering. Just as, <s>Kauśika</s>, there is a medicine called <s>maghī</s>, which pacifies all poisons — suppose a poisonous snake or some creature overcome by hunger and searching for food were to see some living being. It would pursue that living being, wishing to devour it. Then that living being, frightened by the fear of death, would approach the place where that medicine called <s>maghī</s> is located; then that poisonous snake, by the very scent of that medicine, would think it must turn back. For what reason? For indeed, the medicinal quality of that medicine overcomes the poison of that poisonous snake. Powerful indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, is that medicine called <s>maghī</s>.

body.text: evam eva kauśika yo hi kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, tatra kauśika ya utpannotpannā vigrahavivādavirodhā bhaviṣyanti, te prajñāpāramitāyās tejasā prajñāpāramitāyā balena kṣipram evāntardhāsyanti, upaśamiṣyanti, yato yata evotpatsyante tatra tatraivāntardhāsyanti, na vivardhayiṣyante. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā sarveṣāṃ pāpakānāṃ dharmāṇām upaśamayitrī na vivardhikā yad uta rāgadveṣamohāṇām upaśamayitrī na vivardhikā.
body.translated_text: Just so, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and properly attend to it in the mind — <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever disputes, quarrels, and oppositions arise there, they will quickly disappear and be pacified by the splendor and power of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; wherever they arise, right there they will disappear and will not increase. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the pacifier of all unwholesome dharmas, not their increaser — namely, she is the pacifier of passion, hatred, and delusion, not their increaser.

Practicing in the six perfections, whatever giving he gives, having made it shared with all beings, he will dedicate it to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening through the method of non-apprehension. Whatever morality he guards, having made it shared with all beings, he will dedicate it to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening through the method of non-apprehension. body.text: sa ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu caran yad dānaṃ dāsyati tat sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayiṣyaty anupalambhayogena, yac chīlaṃ rakṣiṣyati tat sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayiṣyaty anupalambhayogena, yāṃ kṣāntiṃ bhāvayiṣyati tat sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayiṣyaty anupalambhayogena, yad vīryaṃ ārapsyate tat sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayiṣyaty anupalambhayogena, yad dhyānaṃ samāpadyate tat sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayiṣyaty anupalambhayogena, yāṃ prajñāṃ bhāvayiṣyati tat sarvasattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayiṣyaty anupalambhayogena.

evaṃ carataḥ kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu smṛtir utpatsyate, saced dānaṃ na dāsyāmi durgateṣu kuleṣūpapatsya na ca me sattvaparipāko bhaviṣyati na buddhakṣetrapariśodhanaṃ na sarvākārajñatāṃ pratilapsye, sacet chīlaṃ na rakṣiṣyāmi tisṛṣu me durgatīṣūpapattir bhaviṣyati, na ca me manuṣyapratilambho bhaviṣyati, na sattvaparipāko na buddhakṣetrapariśodhanaṃ na sarvākārajñatāṃ pratilapsye, sacen na kṣāntiṃ bhāvayiṣyāmi, indriyāṇi me paribhetsyate mukhamaṇḍalaṃ me dhyāmībhaviṣyati, na ca rūpasaṃpadaṃ pratilapsye, yayā rūpasaṃpadayā bodhisattvacārikāḥ carataḥ sattvasahadarśane naiva niyatā bhaviṣyanty anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau na ca rūpasaṃpadā sattvān paripācayiṣyāmi na buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhayiṣyāmi na mārgākārajñatāṃ pratilapsye, sacet kusīdo bhaviṣyati nemaṃ śakṣyāmi bodhimārgam anuprāptaṃ na ca me sattvaparipāko bhaviṣyati, na buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhanaṃ na sarvākārajñataṃ pratilapsye, saced vikṣiptacitto bhaviṣyāmi nedaṃ śaksyāmi samādhim utpādayituṃ yena samādhinā sattvān paripācayiṣyāmi na me buddhakṣetrapariśodhanaṃ bhaviṣyāmi na sarvākārajñatām anuprāpsye, saced (

children.text: ) duṣprajño bhaviṣyāmi na śakṣyāmi prajñopāyakauśalena śrāvakabhūmipratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ cātikramya sattvān paripācya buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhya sarvākārajñatām anuprāptuṃ, sa evaṃ pratisaṃśikṣiṣyate, ayuktam etad bhaved yo māṃ mātsaryavaśena dānapāramitāṃ na paripūrayeyaṃ dauḥśīlyavaśena śīlapāramitāṃ na paripūrayeyaṃ vyāpadavaśena kṣāntipāramitāṃ na paripūrayeyaṃ kauśīdyavaśena vīryapāramitāṃ na paripūrayeyaṃ vikṣepavaśena dhyānapāramitāṃ na paripūrayeyaṃ dauṣprajñāvaśena prajñāpāramitāṃ na paripūrayeyaṃ, aparipūrayan dānapāramitāṃ śīlapāramitāṃ kṣāntipāramitāṃ vīryapāramitāṃ dhyānapāramitāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ na niryāsyāmi sarvākārajñatāyām.
children.translated_text: ) I become one of poor wisdom, I will be unable, through the skill in wisdom and means, to transcend the levels of the <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, ripen beings, purify buddha-fields, and attain the knowledge of all aspects.' He will train himself thus: 'It would be improper if, through the power of miserliness, I should not fulfill the perfection of giving; through the power of immorality, I should not fulfill the perfection of morality; through the power of ill-will, I should not fulfill the perfection of patience; through the power of laziness, I should not fulfill the perfection of vigor; through the power of distraction, I should not fulfill the perfection of meditation; through the power of poor wisdom, I should not fulfill the perfection of wisdom. Without fulfilling the perfection of giving, the perfection of morality, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom, I will not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects.'

body.translated_text: For a son of good family or daughter of good family practicing in the six perfections, mindfulness will arise thus: 'If I do not give gifts, I will be reborn in destitute families, and I will not achieve the ripening of beings, nor the purification of buddha-fields, nor will I obtain the knowledge of all aspects. If I do not guard morality, I will be reborn in the three unfortunate destinies, and I will not obtain a human rebirth, nor the ripening of beings, nor the purification of buddha-fields, nor will I obtain the knowledge of all aspects. If I do not cultivate patience, my faculties will be damaged, my countenance will become dark, and I will not obtain the excellence of physical form by which, when practicing the conduct of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, beings upon merely seeing me will become determined toward unsurpassed perfect complete awakening, nor through excellence of form will I ripen beings, nor purify buddha-fields, nor obtain the knowledge of path-aspects. If I become lazy, I will be unable to reach this path to awakening, nor will the ripening of beings occur for me, nor the purification of buddha-fields, nor will I obtain the knowledge of all aspects. If I become distracted in mind, I will be unable to produce that concentration by which I would ripen beings, nor will the purification of buddha-fields occur for me, nor will I attain the knowledge of all aspects. body.text: evaṃ khalu kauśika sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikāṃś ca sāṃparāyikāṃś ca guṇānuśaṃsān pratilapsyate, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, avirahitaś ca bhaviṣyati sarvākārajñatācittena.
body.translated_text: Thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up, retains, recites, and masters this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and attends to it wisely, and is not separated from the mind of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatācitta</s>) — they will obtain benefits both in this life and in the future.
<s>Śakra</s> said: It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> stands ready for the purpose of taming and humbling <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s.

body.text: śakra āha: āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvad iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ paridamanārthāyānunnāmārthāya ca pratyupasthitā.
bhagavān āha: yathā punaḥ kauśika bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitāparidamanārthāyānunnamārthāya ca pratyupasthitā.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, how does the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> stand ready for the purpose of taming and humbling <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s?

body.text: śakra āha: iha bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo laukikyāṃ dānapāramitāyāṃ caran buddhebhyo bhagavadbhyaḥ pratyekabuddhebhyaḥ śrāvakebhyaś ca dānaṃ dadāti, tasyaivaṃ bhavaty ahaṃ dānaṃ dadāmi buddhebhyo bhagavadbhyaḥ pratyekabuddhebhyaḥ śrāvakebhyaś ca sa kṛpaṇavanīyakārthena yācanakebhyaś ca sa tena dānenānupāyakauśalenonnāmaṃ gacchati, laukikyāṃ śīlapāramitāyāṃ carataḥ, evaṃ bhavaty ahaṃ śīlapāramitāyāṃ carāmy ahaṃ śīlapāramitāṃ paripūrayāmi sa tenonnāmaṃ gacchati, laukikyāṃ kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ carataḥ, evaṃ bhavaty ahaṃ kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ carāmy ahaṃ kṣāntipāramitāṃ paripūrayāmi sa tenonnāmaṃ gacchati, laukikyāṃ vīryapāramitāyāṃ carataḥ, evaṃ bhavaty ahaṃ vīryapāramitāyāṃ carāmy ahaṃ vīryapāramitāṃ paripūrayāmi sa tenonnāmaṃ gacchati, laukikyāṃ dhyānapāramitāyāṃ carataḥ. evaṃ bhavaty ahaṃ dhyānapāramitāyāṃ carāmy ahaṃ dhyānapāramitāṃ paripūrayāmi sa tenonnāmaṃ gacchati, laukikyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ (

He cultivates the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) yet does not apprehend it, because the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been well cultivated. Thus indeed, Blessed One, for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is present for the purpose of taming and for the purpose of non-conceit.

body.text: śatasāhasryāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ parivartaḥ saptadaśamaḥ
body.translated_text: The seventeenth chapter of the <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

Then the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family will take up this profound perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), will retain it, will recite it, will master it, will study it, and will wisely attend to it — if, having entered the midst of a great battle, having mounted to the forefront of battle, that son or daughter of good family were to descend there while reciting this profound perfection of wisdom and, having descended, were to stand there — that son or daughter of good family will not go to defeat; victory alone will be theirs, and they will emerge from that battle unharmed and unhurt. It is impossible, <s>Kauśika</s>, there is no occasion, that a son or daughter of good family reciting this perfection of wisdom, having mounted into battle, should meet with danger to life — this situation does not exist. And if someone were to hurl a weapon or an arrow at their body, it would not fall upon their body. For what reason? For indeed, that son or daughter of good family, having long practiced the six perfections (<s>ṣaṭ pāramitā</s>), has conquered their own weapons and arrows of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and has conquered others' weapons and arrows of passion; has conquered their own weapons and arrows of hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) and has conquered others' weapons and arrows of hatred; has conquered their own weapons and arrows of delusion (<s>moha</s>) and has conquered others' weapons and arrows of delusion; has conquered their own weapons and arrows made of views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) and has conquered others' weapons and arrows made of views; has conquered their own weapons and arrows of mental afflictions (<s>paryutthāna</s>) and has conquered others' weapons and arrows of mental afflictions; has conquered their own weapons and arrows of latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) and has conquered others' weapons and arrows of latent tendencies — relying on this very perfection of wisdom and cultivating that perfection of wisdom. By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, weapons or arrows hurled at the body of that son or daughter of good family in the midst of battle will not strike their body.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāñ chakro devānām indram etad avocat: yo hi kaścit kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati svādhyāpayiṣyati, yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, abhirūḍho saṃgrāmamadhye vartamāne mahati saṃgrāmaśīrṣavyārūḍhaḥ, tatra sacet kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ gambhīrāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ svādhyāyann avataret, tatrāvatīrya tiṣṭheta nāsau kulaputro vā kuladuhitā yā parājayaṃ yāsyati, jaya evāsya bhaviṣyaty akṣataś cānupahataś ca taṃ saṃgrāmam uttariṣyati, asthānaṃ kauśikānavakāśo yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ svādhyāyaṃs tatra saṃgrāme samabhirūḍho jīvitāntarāyaṃ nigacchen nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate, sacet punar asya kaścid eva śastraṃ vā kāṇḍaṃ vā śarīre kṣipet na tasya śarīre patiṣyati. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitā vā dīrgharātraṃ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu caratā, ātmanaś ca rāgaśastrāṇi rāgakāṇḍāni nirjitāni pareṣāṃ rāgaśastrāṇi rāgakāṇḍāṇi nirjitāni, ātmanaś ca dveṣaśastrāṇi dveṣakāṇḍāṇi nirjitāni pareṣāṃ dveṣaśastrāṇi dveṣakāṇḍāni nirjitāni, ātmanaś ca mohaśastrāṇi mohakāṇḍāṇi nirjitāni pareṣāṃ mohaśastrāṇi mohakāṇḍāni nirjitāni, ātmanaś ca dṛṣṭikṛtaśastrāṇi dṛṣṭikṛtakāṇḍāṇi nirjitāni pareṣāṃ ca dṛṣṭikṛtaśastrāṇi dṛṣṭikṛtakāṇḍāni nirjitāni, ātmanaś ca paryutthānaśastrāṇi paryutthānakāṇḍāṇi nirjitāni pareṣāṃ ca paryutthānaśastrāṇi paryutthānakāṇḍāni nirjitāni, ātmanaś cānuśayaśastrāṇy anuśayakāṇḍāṇi nirjitāni pareṣāṃ cānuśayaśastrāṇy anuśayakāṇḍāni nirjitāni, imām eva prajñāpāramitām āgamya tāṃ ca prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayatāṃ, anena kauśika paryāyeṇa tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā saṃgrāmamadhyagatasya śastrāṇi vā kāṇḍāni vā kṣiptāni śarīre na nipatiṣyati.

punar aparaṃ kauśika sacet kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, sarvajñatācittena cāvirahito bhaviṣyati. tasya kaścid abhaiṣajyam avakiret kākhordaṃ vā kuryād agnikhadā copanāmayet, śastreṇa vā dadyād viṣaṃ vā dadyād udake cainaṃ chorayet sarvaṃ tat tasya na kramiṣyati. tat kasya hetoḥ? mahāvidyeyaṃ kauśika vidyā yad uta prajñāpāramitā anuttareyaṃ kauśika vidyā yad uta prajñāpāramitā, (

children.text: ) niruttareyaṃ kauśika vidyā yad uta prajñāpāramitā, atra ca vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇeḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā nātmavyābādhāya cetayate na paravyābādhāya cetayate nobhayavyābādhāya cetayate. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi so 'tra śikṣamāṇo nātmānam upalabhate na sattvam upalabhate na jīvam upalabhate na jantum upalabhate na poṣam upalabhate na puruṣam upalabhate na pudgalam upalabhate na manujam upalabhate na mānavam upalabhate na kārakam upalabhate na vedakaṃ upalabhate na jānakam upalabhate na paśyakam upalabhate.
children.translated_text: ) this is a peerless <s>vidyā</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, namely the perfection of wisdom. And the son or daughter of good family training in this <s>vidyā</s> does not intend harm to themselves, does not intend harm to others, does not intend harm to both. For what reason? For indeed, the one training therein does not apprehend a self, does not apprehend a being, does not apprehend a life-force, does not apprehend a creature, does not apprehend a nourisher, does not apprehend a person, does not apprehend an individual, does not apprehend a human, does not apprehend a man, does not apprehend a doer, does not apprehend an experiencer, does not apprehend a knower, does not apprehend a seer.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son or daughter of good family will take up this perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), will retain it, will recite it, will master it, and will wisely attend to it, and will not be separated from the mind directed toward omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) — if someone were to sprinkle them with poison, or perform sorcery (<s>kākhorda</s>) against them, or thrust them toward a fire pit, or strike them with a weapon, or give them poison, or throw them into water — none of that will take effect on them. For what reason? This is a great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-spell), <s>Kauśika</s>, namely the perfection of wisdom; this is an unsurpassed <s>vidyā</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, namely the perfection of wisdom (

body.text: na rūpam upalabhate, na vedanām upalabhate, na saṃjñām upalabhate, na saṃskārān upalabhate, na vijñānam upalabhate.
body.translated_text: He does not apprehend form (<s>rūpa</s>), does not apprehend feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), does not apprehend perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), does not apprehend formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), does not apprehend consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).

body.text: na cakṣur upalabhate, na śrotram upalabhate, na ghrāṇam upalabhate, na jihvām upalabhate, na kāyam upalabhate, na mana upalabhate.

body.text: na rūpam upalabhate, na śabdam upalabhate, na gandham upalabhate, na rasam upalabhate, na sparśam upalabhate, na dharmān upalabhate.
body.translated_text: He does not apprehend visible form (<s>rūpa</s>), does not apprehend sound (<s>śabda</s>), does not apprehend smell (<s>gandha</s>), does not apprehend taste (<s>rasa</s>), does not apprehend touch (<s>sparśa</s>), does not apprehend mental objects (<s>dharma</s>).

body.text: na cakṣurvijñānam upalabhate, na śrotravijñānam upalabhate, na ghrāṇavijñānam upalabhate, na jihvāvijñānam upalabhate, na kāyavijñānam upalabhate, na manovijñānam upalabhate.

body.translated_text: He does not apprehend internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), does not apprehend the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: na smṛtyupasthānāny upalabhate, na samyakprahāṇāny upalabhate, na ṛddhipādān upalabhate, nendriyāṇy upalabhate, na balāny upalabhate, na bodhyaṅgāny upalabhate, nāryāṣṭāṅgamārgam upalabhate, nāryasatyāny upalabhate, na dhyānāny upalabhate, nāpramāṇāny upalabhate, na ārūpyasamāpattīr upalabhate, na vimokṣān upalabhate, nānupūrvavihārasamāpattīr upalabhate, na śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāny upalabhate, nābhijñā upalabhate, na samādhīn upalabhate, na dhāraṇīmukhāny upalabhate, na tathāgatabalāny upalabhate, na vaiśāradyāny upalabhate, na pratisaṃvida upalabhate, na mahāmaitrīm upalabhate, na mahākaruṇām upalabhate, nāveṇikabuddhadharmān upalabhate.
body.translated_text: He does not apprehend the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), does not apprehend the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), does not apprehend the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), does not apprehend the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), does not apprehend the powers (<s>bala</s>), does not apprehend the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), does not apprehend the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), does not apprehend the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), does not apprehend the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), does not apprehend the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), does not apprehend the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), does not apprehend the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), does not apprehend the successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), does not apprehend the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), does not apprehend the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), does not apprehend the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), does not apprehend the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), does not apprehend the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), does not apprehend the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), does not apprehend the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), does not apprehend great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), does not apprehend great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), does not apprehend the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>).

body.text: na srotaāpattiphalam upalabhate, na sakṛdāgāmiphalam upalabhate, nānāgāmiphalam upalabhate, nārhattvam upalabhate, na pratyekabodhim upalabhate, na mārgākārajñatām upalabhate, na sarvākārajñatām upalabhate.
body.translated_text: He does not apprehend the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), does not apprehend the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), does not apprehend the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), does not apprehend <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhattva</s>), does not apprehend solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>), does not apprehend the knowledge of path-aspects (<s>mārgākārajñatā</s>), does not apprehend the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>).

body.text: anupalambhamāno nātmavyābādhāya cetayate na paravyābādhāya cetayate nobhayavyābādhāya cetayate, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ pratilabhate, sarvasattvānāṃ cittāni vyavalokayati. tat kasya hetoḥ? atra vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇair atītais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddhā, ye 'pi te bhaviṣyaty anāgate 'dhvani tathāgatārhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās te 'py atra vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate, ye 'pi te etarhi pratyutpanne 'dhvani daśasu dikṣv aprameyāsaṃkhyeyās tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, te 'py atraiva vidyāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate.
body.translated_text: Not apprehending, he does not intend harm to himself, does not intend harm to others, does not intend harm to both; he attains unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) and surveys the minds of all beings. For what reason? Past <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones, training in this <s>vidyā</s>, have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. And those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones who will appear in the future, training in this <s>vidyā</s>, will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. And those innumerable, incalculable <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones who now exist in the ten directions in the present, training in this very <s>vidyā</s>, will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening.

Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, wherever this perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) has been written down and is held — even if one does not study it, recite it, master it, or wisely attend to it — in that house, village, or city, no human or non-human being will find an opportunity to gain entry. For what reason? For indeed, for the worship of this very perfection of wisdom, the divine sons of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s>, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> divine sons, the <s>Yāma</s> divine sons, the <s>Tuṣita</s> divine sons, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> divine sons, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> divine sons, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> divine sons, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> divine sons, the <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s> divine sons, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Ābhā</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābhā</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇābhā</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Śubha</s> gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhā</s> gods, the <s>Parīttabṛha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇabṛha</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, the <s>Abṛha</s> gods, the <s>Atapa</s> gods, the <s>Sudṛśa</s> gods, the <s>Sudarśana</s> gods, the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — those in the great trichiliocosm, as well as those in immeasurable and innumerable world-systems — will constantly provide protection, shelter, and guardianship to those sons and daughters of good family who hold this perfection of wisdom in written form. Those divine sons will come and, having honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped this perfection of wisdom, will depart. Whoever, <s>Kauśika</s>, holds this perfection of wisdom in written form will gain these benefits and advantages visible in this very life. Just as, <s>Kauśika</s>, those who have gone to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), and those in the surrounding area of the seat of awakening, and those beings born in animal states within the seat of awakening, or those who are human — they cannot be harmed or injured by any human or non-human being. For what reason? For it was seated here that the previous <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Those who will be <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones in the future will also awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening seated in this very place. body.text: ) lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās tiṣṭhanti te 'py atraiva niṣadyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddhāḥ. taiḥ sarvatathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhya sarvasattvānām abhayāyāvairāyāsapannāya pratipadyāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvā devamānuṣīṣu saṃpattiṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyante pratiṣṭhāpyante ca, srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyante pratiṣṭhāpyante ca, sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyante pratiṣṭhāpyante ca, anāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyante pratiṣṭhāpyante ca, arhattve pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyante pratiṣṭhāpyante ca, pratyekabodhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyante pratiṣṭhāpyante ca. tat kasya hetoḥ? anayaiva kauśika prajñāpāramitayā sa pṛthivīpradeśe sarvasattvānāṃ caityabhūtaḥ kṛto vandanīyo namaskaraṇīyo mānanīyaḥ pūjanīyaḥ satkaraṇīyo gurukaraṇīyaḥ puṣpair dhūpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhiḥ.

Having awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones, taking the path of fearlessness, non-hostility, and non-distress for all beings, have established, will establish, and are establishing immeasurable and innumerable beings in the prosperities of gods and humans; have established, will establish, and are establishing them in the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have established, will establish, and are establishing them in the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have established, will establish, and are establishing them in the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have established, will establish, and are establishing them in <s>arhat</s>ship; have established, will establish, and are establishing them in solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>). For what reason? <s>Kauśika</s>, through this very perfection of wisdom, that spot of earth has been made a shrine (<s>caitya</s>) for all beings — worthy of reverence, salutation, honor, and worship, to be venerated with flowers, incense, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags.

<s>Śakra</s> said: Blessed One, if any son or daughter of good family were to write this perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), make it into a book, and hold it, and were to honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, incense, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags; and if another were to enshrine the relics of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One who has attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in a <s>stūpa</s> made of the seven precious substances, or were to construct an elevated one of the seven precious substances and maintain it, and were to honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, incense, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags — which of those two would produce a greater heap of merit?

body.text: śakra āha: yo hi kaścid bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā, imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā dhāraya tāṃ ca puṣpair dhūpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhiḥ satkuryād gurukuryād mānayet pūjayed, yaś ca tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya saptaratnamayastūpe tathāgataśarīrāni pratiṣṭhāpayet parihared vā saptaratnamaye samudgate kṛtvā tāni ca satkuryād gurukurād mānayet pūjayet puṣpair dhūpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhiḥ, kataras tayor bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasavet?

bhagavān āha: tena hi kauśika tvām evātra pariprakṣyāmi, yathā te kṣamate tathā vyākuru. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśika yeyaṃ tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena sarvākārajñatā anuprāptā yaś cāyam ātmabhāvo 'bhinivartitaḥ. katamasyāṃ pratipati śikṣamāṇena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena sarvākārajñatānuprāptā ayaṃ cātmabhāvo 'bhinivartitaḥ.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Well then, <s>Kauśika</s>, I shall question you about this very matter; answer as it seems fit to you. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? This knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) that has been attained by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and this bodily existence that has been produced — through training in what practice did the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One attain the knowledge of all aspects and produce this bodily existence?

body.text: śakra āha: ihaiva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena sarvākārajñatā anuprāptā ayaṃ cātmabhāvo 'bhinivartitaḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: Blessed One, it was through training in this very perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) that the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One attained the knowledge of all aspects and produced this bodily existence.

children.translated_text: ) that the knowledge of all aspects was attained and this bodily existence was produced. However, <s>Kauśika</s>, it is not through obtaining this bodily form that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is reckoned as '<s>Tathāgata</s>.' It is through the attainment of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is reckoned as '<s>Tathāgata</s>.' That which, <s>Kauśika</s>, is the knowledge of all aspects — that has issued forth from the perfection of wisdom. Thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, this bodily existence serves as the support for that knowledge of all aspects, and relying on this support, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One attained the knowledge of all aspects. Thus this bodily existence, being the support of the knowledge of all aspects, has become a shrine (<s>caitya</s>) for all beings — worthy of reverence, honor, worship, veneration. Even after his final <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, there will be such worship of the relics — but that is not the same as worship of the Dharma. <s>Kauśika</s>, whoever, whether a son or daughter of good family, writes this perfection of wisdom and takes it up, holds it, recites it, masters it, wisely attends to it, and honors, respects, esteems, and worships it with flowers, incense, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags — by that person, worship of the knowledge of all aspects will have been performed. Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family who wishes to worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> should write this very perfection of wisdom, take it up, hold it, recite it, master it, wisely attend to it, and honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, incense, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags. <s>Kauśika</s>, if one were to enshrine the relics of a <s>Tathāgata</s> who has passed away in <s>stūpa</s>s of the seven precious substances, or construct an elevated one and maintain it, and were to honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, incense, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags — and if another were to write this perfection of wisdom, take it up, hold it, recite it, master it, wisely attend to it, and honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, incense, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags — this latter one would produce a far greater heap of merit. bhagavān āha. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāyaṃ jāmbūdvīpakā manuṣyā ye buddhe abhedyaprasādena samanvāgatā ye dharma abhedyaprasādena samanvāgatā ye saṃghe abhedyaprasādena samanvāgatā, ye buddhe niṣkāṅkṣā dharme niṣkāṅkṣā saṃghe niṣkāṅkṣāḥ, ye buddhe niṣṭhāṅgatā dharme niṣṭhāṅgatāḥ saṃghe niṣṭhāṅgatāḥ.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? body.translated_text: By this method, <s>Kauśika</s>, you should understand thus: few are those beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who are endowed with unshakeable faith (<s>abhedyaprasāda</s>) in the <s>Buddha</s>, endowed with unshakeable faith in the <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with unshakeable faith in the <s>Saṃgha</s>; fewer still are those who attain the three gates of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>); fewer still are those who attain the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>); fewer still are those who attain the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>); fewer still are those who attain the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>); fewer still are those who attain the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>); fewer still are those humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who, through the abandonment of three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), are stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpanna</s>); fewer still are those who, through the diminishment of passion, hatred, and delusion, are once-returners (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>); fewer still are those who, through the abandonment of the five lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya saṃyojana</s>), are non-returners (<s>anāgāmin</s>); fewer still are those who, through the abandonment of the five higher fetters (<s>mūrdhabhāgīya saṃyojana</s>), are <s>Arhats</s>; fewer still are those humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who have set out toward solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); fewer still are those who have set out toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>); fewer still are those who practice for awakening with sincere resolve — that is the conclusion, <s>Kauśika</s>, regarding humans. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? body.text: kiyantas te jāmbūdvīpakāḥ prāṇino ye trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāt srotaāpannā ye rāgadveṣamohatanutvāt sakṛdāgāmino ye pañcānām avarabhāgīyāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād anāgāminaḥ, ye pañcānām ūrdhvabhāgīyānāṃ prahāṇād arhantaḥ, ye pratyekabodhaye saṃprasthitāḥ kiyants te jāmbūdvīpakāḥ prāṇino ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau niṣkāṅkṣā buddhe dharme saṃghe niṣkāṅkṣāḥ kiyantas te jāmbūdvīpakāḥ prāṇino ye mātṛjñāḥ ye pitṛjñāḥ śrāmaṇyāḥ kule jyeṣṭopacāyakā dānāni dadati śīlaṃ rakṣanti kṣāntipoṣadham upavaśanti, kāṣṭādīna ca saṃjñino viharanti, evam anityasaṃjñinaḥ, anātmasaṃjñino 'śucisaṃjñinaḥ sarvalokeṣv anabhirati saṃjñanaḥ kiyantas te jāmbūdvīpakāḥ prāṇino ye 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitāḥ.
body.translated_text: How many are those living beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who, through the abandonment of three fetters, are stream-enterers; who, through the diminishment of passion, hatred, and delusion, are once-returners; who, through the abandonment of the five lower fetters, are non-returners; who, through the abandonment of the five higher fetters, are <s>Arhats</s>; who have set out toward solitary awakening? How many are those living beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who are free from doubt regarding unsurpassed perfect awakening, free from doubt regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>? How many are those living beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who are grateful to their mothers, grateful to their fathers, who are devoted ascetics, who honor the elders of the family, who give gifts, who observe morality, who keep the observance day of patience (<s>kṣāntipoṣadha</s>), who dwell with the perception of impermanence, and likewise with the perception of non-self, the perception of impurity, and the perception of non-delight in all worlds? How many are those living beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who have set out toward unsurpassed perfect awakening?

<s>Śakra</s> said: Few, O Blessed One, are those living beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who attain the thirty-seven factors of awakening, who attain the three gates of liberation, who attain the eight liberations, who attain the nine successive abiding attainments, who attain the four analytical knowledges, who attain the six superknowledges, who through the abandonment of three fetters are stream-enterers, who through the diminishment of passion, hatred, and delusion are once-returners, who through the abandonment of the five lower fetters are non-returners, who through the abandonment of the five higher fetters are <s>Arhats</s>, who have set out toward solitary awakening. Few, O Blessed One, are those living beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who have set out toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: ihāhaṃ kauśikānāvaraṇena buddhacakṣuṣā pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātuṣu paśyāmy aprameyāsaṃkhyeyān sattvān anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye carati, prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalavirahitās tata eko vā dvau vā avaivartyabhūmau saṃpratiṣṭe te yad bhūyastvena śrāvakabhūmau vā pratyekabuddhabhūmau vā saṃtiṣṭhante. tat kasya hetoḥ? durabhisaṃbhavā hi kauśikānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ, kusīdair hīnavīryair hīnādhimuktikair duṣprajñaiḥ.
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Kauśika</s>, with my unobstructed <s>Buddha</s>-eye I see in the eastern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, immeasurable and countless beings practicing toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, yet being devoid of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>), among them only one or two become established on the stage of non-regression (<s>avaivartya</s>); for the most part they remain on the stage of <s>Śrāvakas</s> or the stage of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Kauśika</s>, unsurpassed perfect awakening is difficult to attain — by the indolent, by those of inferior vigor, by those of inferior aspiration, and by those of poor wisdom.
