body.text: ihāhaṃ kauśikānāvaraṇena buddhacakṣuṣā dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātuṣu paśyāmy aprameyāsaṃkhyeyān sattvān anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye carati, prajñāpāramitopāyakauśalavirahitās tata eko vā dvau vā avaivartyabhūmau saṃpratiṣṭe te yad bhūyastvena śrāvakabhūmau vā pratyekabuddhabhūmau vā saṃtiṣṭhante. tat kasya hetoḥ? durabhisaṃbhavā hi kauśikānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ, kusīdair hīnavīryair hinādhimuktikair duṣprajñaiḥ.
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Kauśika</s>, with my unobstructed <s>Buddha</s>-eye I see in the southwestern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, immeasurable and countless beings practicing toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, yet being devoid of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and skill in means, among them only one or two become established on the stage of non-regression; for the most part they remain on the stage of <s>Śrāvakas</s> or the stage of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Kauśika</s>, unsurpassed perfect awakening is difficult to attain — by the indolent, by those of inferior vigor, by those of inferior aspiration, and by those of poor wisdom.

body.text: tasmāt tarhi kauśika ye te kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś cānuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye saṃprasthitās taiḥ kṣipraṃ sukhaṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbodhukamair iyaṃ prajñāpāramitābhīkṣaṇaṃ srotavyodgṛhītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyāḥ, yoniśaś ca manasikartavyāḥ. tair iyaṃ prajñāpāramitodgṛhya dhārayitvā vācayitvā paryavāpya yoniśaś ca manasikṛtvā, sarvabuddhā dharmā manasikartavyāḥ.
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who have set out for unsurpassed perfect complete awakening, who wish to quickly and easily awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening, should constantly hear, grasp, retain, recite, and master this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and should properly attend to it in the mind. Having grasped, retained, recited, mastered, and properly attended to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in the mind, they should attend to all the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>s.

body.text: tad yathā dānapāramitā śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: Namely: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: adhyātmaśūnyatā bahirdhāśūnyatā adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā śūnyatāśūnyatā mahāśūnyatā paramārthaśūnyatā saṃskṛtaśūnyatā asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā atyantaśūnyatā anavarāgraśūnyatā anavakāraśūnyatā prakṛtiśūnyatā sarvadharmaśūnyatā svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā anupalambhaśūnyatā abhāvaśūnyatā svabhāvaśūnyatā abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni catvāri samyakprahāṇāni catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ pañcendriyāṇi pañca balāni sapta bodhyaṅgāni āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ catvāry āryasatyāni catvāri dhyānāni catvāry apramāṇāni catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni pañcābhijñāḥ sarvasamādhayaḥ sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni daśa tathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ mahāmaitri mahākaruṇā aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the three gateways of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>), the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>).

body.text: anye 'py aparimāṇā buddhadharmā yatra prajñāpāramitāyām antargatā te py udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā yoniśaś ca manasikartavyāḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśika te kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś caivaṃ jñāsyanti, atra hi tathāgataḥ pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ śikṣito yad uta prajñāpāramitāyāṃ dhyānapāramitāyāṃ vīryapāramitāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ śīlapāramitāyāṃ dānapāramitāyām.
body.translated_text: And the other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> that are contained within the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — those too should be grasped, retained, recited, mastered, and properly attended to in the mind. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will know thus: 'It was herein that the <s>Tathāgata</s> formerly trained in the conduct of a <s>bodhisattva</s> — namely, in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, in the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), in the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), in the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), in the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), and in the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>).'

body.translated_text: In the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), in the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), in the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), in the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), in the five powers (<s>bala</s>), in the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), in the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), in the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), in the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), in the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), in the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), in the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), in the three gateways of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>), in the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), in all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), in all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), in the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), in the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), in the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), in great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), in great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), in the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), and in other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> —

body.text: asmābhir apy anuśikṣitavyam eṣāsmākaṃ śāstā yad uta prajñāpāramitā, yāvad anye 'py aparimāṇā buddhadharmā etad buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śāsanaṃ pratyekabuddhānām arhatām anāgāmināṃ sakṛdāgāmināṃ srotaāpannānāṃ yad uta prajñāpāramitā atra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā dhyānapāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā vīryapāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā śīlapāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā dānapāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇā.
body.translated_text: 'We too should train in these. This is our teacher — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and likewise all other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>. This is the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, of <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, <s>arhat</s>s, non-returners (<s>anāgāmin</s>), once-returners (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), and stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Training herein, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, training in the perfection of meditation, training in the perfection of vigor, training in the perfection of patience, training in the perfection of morality, training in the perfection of giving.'

body.text: tasmāt tarhi kauśika kulaputrair vā kuladuhitṛbhir vā tiṣṭhati tathāgataparinirvṛte vā tathāgate, prajñāpāramitaiva taiḥ pratisatkartavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ? eṣaiva kauśika prajñāpāramitā sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇaṃ yāvat sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ prajāyāḥ pratiśaraṇaṃ, dhyānapāramitaiva taiḥ pratisatkartavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ? eṣaiva kauśika dhyānapāramitā sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇaṃ yāvat sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ prajāyāḥ pratiśaraṇaṃ, vīryapāramitaiva taiḥ pratisatkartavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ? eṣaiva kauśika vīryapāramitā sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇaṃ yāvat sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ prajāyāḥ pratiśaraṇaṃ, kṣāntipāramitaiva taiḥ pratisatkartavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ? eṣaiva kauśika kṣāntipāramitā sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇaṃ yāvat sadevamānuṣāsurayāḥ prajāyāḥ pratiśaraṇaṃ, śīlapāramitaiva taiḥ pratisatkartavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ? eṣaiva kauśika śīlapāramitā sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇaṃ yāvat sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ prajāyāḥ pratiśaraṇaṃ, dānapāramitaiva taiḥ pratisatkartavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ? eṣaiva kauśika dānapāramitā sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pratiśaraṇaṃ yāvat sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ prajāyāḥ pratisaraṇam.

body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the trichiliocosm filled with <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>stūpa</s>s. Whatever beings there are in the trichiliocosm, <s>Kauśika</s> — if each one of those beings, for the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, were to have a <s>stūpa</s> made of the seven precious substances constructed, and were to honor, respect, esteem, and worship it for as long as they live with divine flowers, divine garlands, divine fragrances, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine flags, and divine music — yet a son or daughter of good family who writes this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, takes it up, retains it, recites it, masters it, wisely attends to it, and will not be separated from the mind directed toward the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), and who honors, respects, esteems, and worships them with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music — this latter one would produce a far greater heap of merit.

body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: So it is, Blessed One; so it is, <s>Sugata</s>. body.translated_text: as many beings as there are in the world-systems in the upward direction, equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> — if each one of those beings, for the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, were to have a <s>stūpa</s> made of the seven precious substances constructed, one <s>yojana</s> in height and one <s>yojana</s> in breadth, and were to honor, respect, esteem, and worship them for a <s>kalpa</s> or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s> with divine flowers, divine garlands, divine fragrances, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine flags, and divine music — what do you think, Blessed One? Would that son or daughter of good family produce a great heap of merit on that account?

body.text: bhagavān āha: bahu kauśika.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: A great deal, <s>Kauśika</s>.

body.text: śakra āha: ataḥ sa bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvodgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati, yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, tāṃś ca satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati, puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ. tat (

children.text: ) kasya hetoḥ? atra hi bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyām antargatāḥ sarve kuśalā dharmās tad yathā daśa kuśalaḥ karmapathāś catvāri dhyānāni catvāry apramāṇāni catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ.
children.translated_text: ) reason? For indeed, Blessed One, all wholesome dharmas are contained within this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, namely: the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ</s>), the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), and the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>).

body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: That son or daughter of good family, Blessed One, who writes this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, takes it up, retains it, recites it, masters it, wisely attends to it, and honors, respects, esteems, and worships them with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music — that one produces a far greater heap of merit than the former. For what (

body.text: dānapāramitā śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: The perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: adhyātmaśūnyatā bahirdhāśūnyatā adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā śūnyatāśūnyatā mahāśūnyatā paramārthaśūnyatā saṃskṛtaśūnyatā asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā atyantaśūnyatā anavarāgraśūnyatā anavakāraśūnyatā prakṛtiśūnyatā sarvadharmaśūnyatā svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā anupalambhaśūnyatā abhāvaśūnyatā svabhāvaśūnyatā abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: smṛtyupasthānāni samyakprahāṇāni ṛddhipādā indriyāṇi balāni bodhyaṅgāni āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ, trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitā catvāry āryasatyāni duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasamudayaṃ duḥkhanirodhā mārgaḥ ṣaḍ abhijñā aṣṭā vimokṣā navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ sarvasamādhayaḥ sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni daśatathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvido mahāmaitrī mahākaruṇā aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ sarvajñatā mārgākārajñatā sarvākārajñatā idaṃ tad buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śāsanaṃ yatra sarvaśrāvkapratyekabuddhānām atitānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhā bhagavantaḥ śikṣitvā sarvadharmāṇāṃ pāraṅgatā gacchati gamiṣyati ca.
body.translated_text: The foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the powers (<s>bala</s>), the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the three gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihita</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>) — suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path — the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), the knowledge of path-aspects (<s>mārgākārajñatā</s>), and the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). This is the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, wherein all <s>śrāvaka</s>s and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s of the past, present, and future, as well as the <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, having trained in it, have gone beyond, are going beyond, and will go beyond the culmination of all dharmas.

body.text: śatasāhasryāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ parivarto nāmāṣṭādaśamaḥ
body.translated_text: The eighteenth chapter of the <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

Then the Blessed One said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. That son of good family or daughter of good family will produce much merit — immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, and boundless merit will that son of good family or daughter of good family produce — who, having written this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and made it into a book, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it, and moreover will honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, pennants, and various kinds of music. For what reason? For the omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavāñ chakraṃ devānāṃ indram etad avocat: evam etat kauśikaivam etat, bahu te kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaro vā puṇyaṃ prasaviṣyaty aprameyam asaṃkhyeyam acintyam atulyam aparimāṇaṃ te kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaro vā puṇyaṃ prasaviṣyati ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvodgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyanti, uttare ca satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti mānayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyanti, puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? prajñāpāramitā niryātā hi kauśika tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ sarvajñatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitāniryātā vīryapāramitā prajñāpāramitāniryātā kṣāntipāramitā prajñāpāramitāniryātā śīlapāramitā prajñāpāramitāniryātā dānapāramitā prajñāpāramitāniryātā.

adhyātmaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, bahirdhāśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, śūnyatāśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, mahāśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, paramārthaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, saṃskṛtaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, atyantaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, anavarāgraśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, anavakāraśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, prakṛtiśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, sarvadharmaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, anupalambhaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, abhāvaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, svabhāvaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā, abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā prajñāpāramitāniryātā.
body.translated_text: Internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family will write this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, make it into a book, take it up, retain it, master it, wisely attend to it, and will honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, pennants, and various kinds of music — the former heap of merit, <s>Kauśika</s>, does not approach even a hundredth part of this heap of merit produced by that person, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a ten-millionth part, nor a billionth part, nor a ten-billionth part, nor a hundred-billionth part; it does not bear comparison by any fraction, calculation, reckoning, analogy, or approximation. For what reason? For as long as, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will remain in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, so long will there be no disappearance of the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel, no disappearance of the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, no disappearance of the <s>Saṃgha</s>-jewel. So long will there be the manifestation in the world of the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśa kuśala karmapatha</s>), the manifestation in the world of the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), the manifestation in the world of the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the manifestation in the world of the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and the manifestation in the world of the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>).

The arising of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s will be made known, the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge will be made known, the turning of the wheel of the Dharma will be made known, the ripening of beings will be made known, and the purification of buddha-fields will be made known.

body.text: atha khalu ye 'smiṃs trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau cāturmahārājakāyikā devās trāyastriṃśā yāmās tuṣitā nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavasavartinā brahmakāyikā brahmapurohitā brahmapārṣadyā mahābrahmaṇo ābhāḥ parīttabhā apramāṇābhā ābhāsvarāḥ śubhāḥ parīttaśubhā apramāṇaśubhāḥ śubhakṛtsnā bṛhāḥ parīttabṛhā apramāṇabṛhā bṛhatphalā abṛhā atapāḥ sudṛśāḥ sudarśanā akaniṣṭhā devās taṃ śakraṃ devānām indram āmantrayate : udgṛhītavyā mārṣa prajñāpāramitā dhārayitavyā mārṣa prajñāpāramitā vācayitavyā mārṣa prajñāpāramitā paryavāptavyā mārṣa prajñāpāramitā, yoniśaś ca manasikartavyā mārṣa prajñāpāramitā, etayā mārṣa prajñāpāramitayodgṛhītayā dhārayitayā vācayitayā paryavāptayā yoniśaś ca manasikṛtayā buddhanetryā (
body.translated_text: Then, the gods in this trichiliocosm — the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Ābhā</s>, <s>Parīttābhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇābhā</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Śubha</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Bṛha</s>, <s>Parīttabṛha</s>, <s>Apramāṇabṛha</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Avṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be taken up, sir; the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be retained, sir; the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be recited, sir; the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be mastered, sir; the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be wisely attended to, sir. For when, sir, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been taken up, retained, recited, mastered, and wisely attended to, led by the <s>Buddha</s> (

body.text: ) vācayitayā paryavāptayā yoniśaś ca manasikṛtayā buddhanetryā avyavacchedo bhaviṣyati, dharmanetryā avyavacchedo bhaviṣyati, saṃghanetryā avyavacchedo bhaviṣyati buddhanetryā mārṣa avyavacchedo 'nudharmanetryā avyavacchedo 'nusaṃghanetryā avyavacchedaḥ.
body.translated_text: ) recited, mastered, and wisely attended to, led by the <s>Buddha</s>, there will be no interruption of the lineage of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhanetri</s>); there will be no interruption of the lineage of the Dharma (<s>dharmanetri</s>); there will be no interruption of the lineage of the <s>Saṃgha</s> (<s>saṃghanetri</s>). Sir, there will be no interruption of the lineage of the <s>Buddha</s>, no interruption of the lineage of the Dharma, no interruption of the lineage of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: dānapāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, śīlapāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, kṣāntipāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, vīryapāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, dhyānapāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, prajñāpāramitāyā loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: There will be the appearance in the world of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.translated_text: There will be the appearance in the world of internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>).

body.translated_text: There will be the appearance in the world of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the powers (<s>bala</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) (

body.text: srotaāpattiphalasya loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, sakṛdāgāmiphalasya loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, anāgāmiphalasya loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, arhattvasya loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, pratyekabodher loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodher loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: there will be the appearance in the world of the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhattva</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>), there will be the appearance in the world of unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: atha bhagavāñ chakraṃ devānām indram āmantrayate: udgṛhāṇa tvaṃ kauśikemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ dhāraya vācaya paryavāpnuhi yoniśaś ca manasikuruṣvemāṃ prajñāpāramitām. tat kasya hetoḥ? yadā kauśikāsurāṇām evaṃ samudācārā bhaviṣyati, devāṃs trāyastriṃśān yodhayiṣyāmo devais trāyastriṃśaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmayiṣyāmas tadā tvaṃ kauśikemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ samanvāhṛtya manasā svadhyāya kuryāḥ yoniśaś ca manasikuryā evaṃ teṣām asurāṇāṃ te samudācārāḥ.
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: Take up, <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? When, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>asura</s>s will have such hostile intentions — 'We will fight the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, we will do battle with the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods' — then you, <s>Kauśika</s>, having brought to mind this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, should recite it and wisely attend to it. In this way, those hostile intentions of those <s>asura</s>s

body.text: punar evāntarddhāsyati na punas te cittotpādā vivardhiṣyanti, yeṣāṃ ca devaputrāṇāṃ devakanyānāṃ cyutikālaḥ syāṃ te cātmanaḥ pāpopapattiṃ paśyeyus teṣāṃ tvaṃ kauśika purataḥ imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ svādhyāyaṃ kuryās te tena prajñāpāramitā śravaṇakuśalamūlena prajñāpāranutā prasādena ca tatraiva devabhavaneṣūpapatsyate. tat kasya hetoḥ? evaṃ mahārthikā hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā śravaṇaṃ yasya kasyacit kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā śrotāvabhāsaṃ gamiṣyanti sarve te tena kuśalamūlenānupūrveṇānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśika ye te 'bhūvan atīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ sa śrāvakasaṃghās te 'pīhaiva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate, ye 'pi ta etarhi daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ saśrāvakasaṃghās tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti, sarve te ihaiva prajñāpāramitāyām anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhāḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśikātra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sarve bodhipakṣā dharmā antargatāḥ śrāvakadharmā vā pratyekabuddhadharmā vā bodhisattvadharmā vā buddhadharmā vā.
body.translated_text: will quickly disappear, and those mental intentions will not increase. And for those divine sons and divine daughters for whom the time of death has come and who see their own unfortunate rebirth, you, <s>Kauśika</s>, should recite this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> before them. Through the wholesome root of hearing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and through faith in it, they will be reborn right there in the divine realms. For what reason? So great is the benefit of hearing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, that whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, or divine son or divine daughter for whom this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will reach the range of hearing — all of them, through that wholesome root, will gradually fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones with their <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>saṃgha</s>s there were in the past — they too, having trained right here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. And whatever <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones with their <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>saṃgha</s>s now abide, dwell, and live in the ten directions and their world-systems — all of them fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening right here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, within this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all factors conducive to awakening are included — whether the dharmas of <s>śrāvaka</s>s, or the dharmas of <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, or the dharmas of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, or the dharmas of <s>Buddha</s>s.

body.text: śakra āha: mahāvidyeyaṃ bhagavan yad uta prajñāpāramitā anuttareyaṃ bhagavan vidyā yad uta prajñāpāramitā asamasameyaṃ bhagavan vidyā yad uta prajñāpāramitā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan (

children.translated_text: ) the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the upholder of all wholesome dharmas.

body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: This is a great knowledge (<s>mahāvidyā</s>), Blessed One — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an unsurpassed knowledge, Blessed One — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an unequalled knowledge, Blessed One — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? For indeed, Blessed One (

body.text: bhagavān āha: evam etat kauśikaivam etat mahāvidyeyaṃ kauśika vidyā yad uta prajñāpāramitā anuttareyaṃ vidyā yad uta prajñāpāramitā, asamasameyaṃ vidyā yad uta prajñāpāramitā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśika ye te 'bhūvann atīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās ta etāṃ vidyām āgamya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā ye 'pi te bhaviṣyanty anāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās te 'py etām eva vidyām āgamyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate, ye 'pi ta etarhi daśa dig lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās tiṣṭhanti dhriyanti yāpayanti, te 'py etām eva vidyām āgamyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśikemāṃ vidyām āgamya daśakuśalā karmapathāḥ loke prajñāyante, catvāri dhyānāni loke prajñāyante, catvāry apramāṇāni loke prajñāyante, catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ loke prajñāyante, pañcābhijñā loke prajñāyante.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. This is a great knowledge, <s>Kauśika</s> — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an unsurpassed knowledge — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is an unequalled knowledge — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones there were in the past — they all, having relied on this knowledge, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. And whatever <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones there will be in the future — they too, having relied on this very knowledge, will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. And whatever <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones now abide, dwell, and live in the world-systems of the ten directions — they too, having relied on this very knowledge, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. For what reason? children.translated_text: ) practices the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), practices the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), practices the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), practices the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), practices the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), practices the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), practices the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), practices great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and practices the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>). And he does not fall into the level of a <s>śrāvaka</s>, does not directly realize the level of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, yet he ripens beings and purifies the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (buddha-field), acquires the endowment of lifespan, acquires the endowment of beings, acquires the endowment of the buddha-field, acquires the endowment of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, and attains the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>).

body.translated_text: He practices the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), practices the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), practices the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), practices the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), practices the powers (<s>bala</s>), practices the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), practices the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), practices the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), practices the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), practices the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), practices the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), practices the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), practices the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>) (

Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son or daughter of good family grasps this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, and wisely attends to it — that person will be endowed with benefits visible in this very life (<s>dṛṣṭadhārmika guṇa</s>) and will also be endowed with benefits pertaining to the next life (<s>sāṃparāyika guṇa</s>).

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, sa ebhir dṛṣṭadhārmikair guṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhaviṣyati sāṃparāyikaiś ca guṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhaviṣyati.

śakra āha: katamair bhagavan dṛṣṭadhārmikair guṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bhaviṣyati, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: With what benefits visible in this life, Blessed One, will that son or daughter of good family be endowed — one who grasps this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, and wisely attends to it?

body.text: bhagavān āha: yo hi kaścit kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, sa na viṣeṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati, na śastreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyati, nāgninā kālaṃ kariṣyati, nodakena kālaṃ kariṣyati, yāvan naikottareṇa rāgaśatena kālaṃ kariṣyati, sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākaṃ, ye ca puna rājakulād upadravā bhaviṣyanti, sacet kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ svādhyāyan rājakulam upasaṃkramiṣyati, na tasya te 'vatāraprekṣiṇām avatāraṃ lapsyate, rājaputrāś ca rājamahāmātrāś cālapitavyaṃ maṃsyante, ābhāṣitavyaṃ maṃsyante, pratisaṃmoditavyaṃ maṃsyante. tat kasya hetoḥ? yathāpi tad asyā eva prajñāpāramitāyās tejonubhāvena sacet kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ svādhyāyan rājakulam upasaṃkramiṣyati, tam enaṃ te rājaputrā vā rājamahāmātrā vā priyavacanair ālapitavyaṃ maṃsyante, ābhāṣitavyaṃ maṃsyate, pratisaṃmoditavyaṃ maṃsyate. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśika teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ vā sarvasattvānām antike maitracittaṃ pratyupasthitaṃ karuṇācittaṃ muditācittam upekṣācittaṃ pratyupasthitaṃ, ebhiḥ kauśika dṛṣṭadhārmikair guṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sa kulaputro vā (

children.text: ) kuladuhitā vā bhaviṣyati ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati.
children.translated_text: ) — one who grasps this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, and wisely attends to it.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Whatever son or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, will grasp this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it — that person will not meet death by poison, will not meet death by weapon, will not meet death by fire, will not meet death by water, and indeed will not meet death by even a hundred successive passions (<s>rāga</s>) — setting aside the ripening of previous <s>karma</s>. And whatever dangers may arise from the royal court — if that son or daughter of good family approaches the royal court while reciting this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, those who look for an opportunity against them will not find any opening. Princes and royal ministers will think them worthy of being addressed, worthy of being spoken to, worthy of being greeted. For what reason? For indeed, by the power and majesty of this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, if that son or daughter of good family approaches the royal court while reciting this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, those princes and royal ministers will think them worthy of being addressed with kind words, worthy of being spoken to, worthy of being greeted. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the presence of all beings, the mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) is present in those sons and daughters of good family, the mind of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), the mind of sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and the mind of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) are present. With these benefits visible in this very life, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son or daughter of good family will be endowed (

body.text: katamaiś ca kauśika sāṃparāyikair guṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati, yad uta na jātu daśabhiḥ karmapathair avirahitā bhaviṣyati, na caturbhir dhyānair na caturbhir apramāṇair na catasṛbhir ārūpyasamāpattibhiḥ, na ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhir na smṛtyupasthānair na samyakprahāṇair na ṛddhipādair nendriyair na balair na bodhyaṅgair na mārgeṇa nāryasatyair na dhyānair nāpramāṇair nārūpyasamāpattibhir na vimokṣair nānupūrvavihārasamāpattibhir na śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhair nābhijñābhir na samādhibhir na dhāraṇīmukhair na tathāgatabalair na vaiśāradyair na pratisaṃvidbhir nāveṇikabuddhadharmair virahitā bhaviṣyanti, na kadācin narakeṣūpapadyate, na tiryagyonau na yamaloke, anyatra praṇidhānavaśena sattvaṃ paripākaṃ kariṣyati, sa na kadācid aṅgavihīno bhaviṣyati, na kadācid daridrakuleṣu pratyājaniṣyati, veṇukarakule vā puṣkasakule vā mauṣṭhikacaṇḍālaurānikasaukārikakuleṣu vā śūdrakuleṣu vā satatasamitaṃ dvātriṃśan mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhaviṣyati, yatra ca lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantas tiṣṭhanti dhrīyante yāpayanti tatra lokadhātuṣūpapatsyate, na jātu bodhisattvābhijñābhir virahito bhaviṣyati. sa ākāṅkṣaṃ buddhakṣetrād buddhakṣetraṃ saṃkramiṣyati, buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya sa buddhakṣetrād buddhakṣetraṃ saṃkrāman sattvāṃś ca paripācayiṣyati, buddhakṣetraṃ ca pariśodhayiṣyati, tasmāt tarhi kauśika kulaputrair vā kuladuhitṛbhir vā imāṃ guṇasaṃpadām ākāṅkṣadbhir iyaṃ prajñāpāramitodgṛhītavyā dhārayitavā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā yoniśaś ca manasikartavyā, sarvākārajñatācittena cāvirahitena bhavitavyaṃ, ta ebhir dṛṣṭadhārmikaiḥ sāṃparāyikaiś ca guṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhaviṣyanti, yāvad anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante.
body.translated_text: And with what future qualities is he endowed, <s>Kauśika</s>? Namely, he will never be separated from the ten courses of action (<s>karmapatha</s>), nor from the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), nor from the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), nor from the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), nor from the six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), nor from the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), nor from the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), nor from the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), nor from the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), nor from the powers (<s>bala</s>), nor from the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), nor from the path (<s>mārga</s>), nor from the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), nor from the meditative absorptions, nor from the immeasurables, nor from the formless attainments, nor from the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), nor from the successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), nor from the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), nor from the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), nor from the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), nor from the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), nor from the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), nor from the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), nor from the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), nor from the exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>). He will never be reborn in the hells, nor in the animal realm, nor in the world of <s>Yama</s>, except by the power of his vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) he will mature beings. He will never be deficient in limbs, and he will never be reborn in poor families — neither in families of basket-weavers, nor flower-scavengers, nor boxers, <s>caṇḍāla</s>s, charioteers, or pig-keepers, nor in <s>śūdra</s> families. He will always be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>dvātriṃśan mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), and he will be reborn in those world-systems where <s>Buddha</s>s, Blessed Ones, dwell, abide, and live. He will never be separated from the <s>bodhisattva</s> superknowledges (<s>bodhisattvābhijñā</s>). If he wishes, he will travel from <s>Buddha</s>-field to <s>Buddha</s>-field for the sake of seeing, venerating, and attending upon the <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones. Traveling from <s>Buddha</s>-field to <s>Buddha</s>-field, he will mature beings and purify the <s>Buddha</s>-field. Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, sons or daughters of good family who desire this perfection of qualities should take up this perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it, and should not be separated from the mind directed toward the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). They will be endowed with these qualities visible in this very life and in the future, until they fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: śatasāhasryāṃ prajñāpāramitāyām ūnaviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: The nineteenth chapter of the <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Then a hundred heretical wandering ascetics (<s>anyatīrthikaparivrājaka</s>) with hostile intentions approached toward the Blessed One.

body.text: athānyatīrthikaparivrājakānāṃ śatam upārambhābhiprāyāṇāṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāmaṃ nyāsīt.

atha khalu śakrasya devānām indrasyaitad abhūd, idam anyatīrthikānāṃ śatam upārambhābhiprāyāṇāṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāmanti sma, ya nv ahaṃ yāvan mayā bhagavato 'ntikāt, itaḥ prajñāpāramitāyā udgṛhītaṃ tat svādhyāyaṃ kuryāṃ, yadi me 'nyatīrthikaparivrājakām upasaṃkramya bhagavato 'ntarāyaṃ ca kuryuḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyām.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, had this thought: These hundred heretical wandering ascetics with hostile intentions are approaching toward the Blessed One. Let me now recite what I have grasped from the Blessed One of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, lest these heretical wandering ascetics, having approached, should create an obstacle for the Blessed One while the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is being spoken.

body.text: atha śakro devānām indro yāvad bhagavato 'ntikāt prajñāpāramitāyām udgṛhītaṃ tāvat svādhyāyaṃ karoti sma.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, began to recite what he had grasped of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> from the Blessed One.

body.text: atha te 'nyatīrthikaparivrājakā dūreṇa dūraṃ bhagavataṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya, tenaiva mārgena tenaiva dvāreṇa punar eva prakrāntāḥ
body.translated_text: Then those heretical wandering ascetics circumambulated the Blessed One from a great distance, and departed again by the very same path and the very same gate.

body.text: atha bhagavān āyuṣmataḥ śāradvatīputrasyaitad abhūt, kim atra kāraṇaṃ yena me 'nyatīrthikaparivrājakā dūreṇa dūraṃ bhagavantaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tenaiva mārgena tenaiva dvāreṇa punar eva prakrāntāḥ
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One — the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> had this thought: What is the reason that these heretical wandering ascetics circumambulated the Blessed One from a great distance and departed again by the very same path and the very same gate?

body.text: atha bhagavān āyuṣmataś chāradvatīputrasya cetasaiva cetaḥ, parivitarkam ājāyāyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputram āmantrayataḥ śakreṇa sāradvatīputra devānām indreṇeyaṃ prajñāpāramitā samanvāhṛtā tenaite 'nyatīrthikacarakaparivrājakā dūreṇa dūraṃ tāṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya, tenaiva mārgena tenaiva dvāreṇa punar eva prakrāntāḥ, na hi śāradvatīputra eṣām anyatīrthikacarakaparivrājakānām ekasyāpi śuklāṅgaṃ samanupaśyāmi, sarva ete 'nyatīrthikaparivrājakāḥ pratihatacittā upārambhābhiprāyā imāṃ parṣadam upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃyante nāhaṃ taṃ śāradvatīputra samanupaśyāmi, sadevaloke samārake sabrahmake saśravaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ yo 'syāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pratihatacitto vā upārambhābhiprāyo vā upasaṃkramen nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi śāradvatīputra ya iha trisāhasre mahāsāhasre lokadhātau cāturmahārājakāyikā devaputrās trāyastriṃśā yāmās tuṣitā nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartino devaputrā brahmakāyikā brahmapurohitā brahmapārṣadyā mahābrahmaṇa ābhaḥ parīttābhā apramāṇābhā ābhāsvarāḥ śubhāḥ parīttaśubbā apramāṇaśubhāḥ śubhakṛtsnā bṛhāḥ parīttabṛhā apramāṇabṛhā bṛhatphalā anabhrakā abṛhā atapāḥ sudṛśāḥ sudarśanā akaniṣṭhā devāḥ, ye ca śrāvakā ye ca pratyekabuddhā ye 'pi (

children.text: ) bodhisattvā mahāsattvās tair iyaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ udgṛhītā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi te prajñāpāramitā niryātāḥ sarvam.
children.translated_text: ) the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s — by all of them has this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> been taken up. For what reason? For indeed, they have all issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the thought of the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> with his own mind, addressed the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> was brought to mind by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods. Therefore these heretical wandering ascetics (<s>anyatīrthikacarakaparivrājaka</s>) circumambulated it from a great distance and departed again by the very same path and the very same gate. For indeed, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, I do not see even one wholesome quality (<s>śuklāṅga</s>) in any of these heretical wandering ascetics. All these heretical wandering ascetics, with hostile minds and hostile intentions, thought they should approach this assembly. I do not see, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, in this world with its gods, <s>Māra</s>s, and <s>Brahmā</s>s, in this generation with its ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, anyone who could approach this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with a hostile mind or hostile intention — this is not possible. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, in this trichiliocosm, the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> realm, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, the <s>Yāma</s>, the <s>Tuṣita</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, the <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Ābhā</s>, the <s>Parīttābhā</s>, the <s>Apramāṇābhā</s>, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, the <s>Śubha</s>, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, the <s>Bṛhā</s>, the <s>Parīttabṛhā</s>, the <s>Apramāṇabṛhā</s>, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, the <s>Anabhraka</s>, the <s>Abṛhā</s>, the <s>Atapa</s>, the <s>Sudṛśā</s>, the <s>Sudarśana</s>, the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and the <s>śrāvaka</s>s and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, and also (

body.text: punar aparaṃ śāradvatīputra ye 'pi te pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavantaḥ saśrāvakasaṃghāḥ pratyekabuddhā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakiṃnaramahoragās taiḥ sarvair iyaṃ prajñāpāramitānuparigṛhītā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi prajñāpāramitā niryātās te sarve,
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, in the eastern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, whatever <s>Buddha</s>s, Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of <s>śrāvaka</s>s, <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s, gods, <s>nāga</s>s, <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>gandharva</s>s, <s>asura</s>s, <s>garuḍa</s>s, <s>kiṃnara</s>s, and <s>mahoraga</s>s there are — by all of them has this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> been embraced. Then <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, had this thought: These four assemblies of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, have come together, and these gods of the desire realm and form realm have also come together. Without doubt, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s will be given prophecies here regarding unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Let me now approach the Blessed One and create confusion.

body.text: atha khalu mārasya pāpīyas etad abhūd, imās tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya catasraḥ parṣadaḥ saṃmukhībhūtā ime ca kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarāś ca devāḥ saṃmukhībhūtā niḥsaṃśayam atra bodhisattvā mahāsattvā vyākariṣyante, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau ya nv ahaṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrameyaṃ vicakṣuṣ karaṇīya.
atha māra pāpīyāṃś caturaṅgabalakāyam abhinirmāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkramitukāmo 'bhūt.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, having magically created a fourfold army (<s>caturaṅgabalakāya</s>), wished to approach the Blessed One.

body.text: atha śakrasya devānām indrasyaitad abhūt, māro batāyaṃ pāpīyāṃ caturaṅgabalakāyam abhinirmāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkramitukāmaḥ, yaś cāyaṃ mārapāpīyāñ caturaṅgabalakāyasya vyūho nāyaṃ rājño bimbisārasya caturaṅgasya balakāyasyaivaṃrūpo vyūho na rājñaḥ prasenajito na sākyānāṃ na licchavīnāṃ caturaṅgasya balakāyasyaivaṃrūpavyūhaḥ yo 'yaṃ caturaṅgo varakāyo māreṇa pāpiyasā nirmitaḥ dīrgharātraṃ khalu punar mārapāpīyān bhagavato 'vatārasaṃprekṣyāvatāragaveṣī samyakprayuktānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ viheṭhanābhiprāyaḥ, ya nv aham imāṃ (

children.text: ) prajñāpāramitāṃ samanvāhareyaṃ smṛtyā ca svādhyāyaṃ kuryāt.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, had this thought: This evil <s>Māra</s>, having magically created a fourfold army, wishes to approach the Blessed One. This array of <s>Māra</s>'s fourfold army is not like the array of King <s>Bimbisāra</s>'s fourfold army, nor like the array of King <s>Prasenajit</s>'s, nor the <s>Śākya</s>s', nor the <s>Licchavī</s>s' fourfold army — such is this fourfold army magically created by the evil <s>Māra</s>. For a long time indeed has the evil <s>Māra</s> been watching for an opportunity against the Blessed One, seeking an opening, with the intention of harming beings who are properly engaged. Let me now bring to mind this (

body.text: atha śakro devānām indra imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ samanvāharati sma, smṛtyā ca svādhyāyaṃ karoti sma, yathā yathā śakro devānām indra imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ svādhyāyaṃ karoti sma, tathā tathā mārapāpīyāṃs tenaiva mārgeṇa tenaiva dvāreṇa punar eva pratyudāvartate sma.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, attended to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and recited it from memory. As <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, recited this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, by that very path and that very gate, turned back again.

body.text: atha tatra parṣadi cāturmahārājakāyikā devaputrā yāvad akaniṣṭhā devās te divyāni puṣpāṇi vāsāṃsi cābhinirmāya vaihāyasy antarikṣe sthitvaiva yena bhagavāṃs tenākṣipanti sma, yena bhagavāṃs tenābhiprakiranti sma. evaṃ ca vācam abhāṣanta, ciraṃ bateyaṃ jāmbūdvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ prajñāpāramitā bhagavatāṃ yāvat kileyaṃ jāmbūdvīpakān manuṣyān prajñāpāramitānuvartiṣyante tāvan na tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntardhānaṃ bhaviṣyati saddharmasya ca cirasthitikatāṃ bhaviṣyati, saṃgharatnasya ca loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ caryāviśeṣaḥ prajñāsyate, yatra ca digbhāge imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ te kulaputrā kuladuhitaro vā likhiṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti pustakagatām api kṛtvā ālokajātā ca sā dik pratikāṅkṣitavyā sanāthāvigatās tamondhakārā ca me sā dik pratikāṅkṣitavya.
body.translated_text: Then, in that assembly, the divine sons of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, having magically created divine flowers and garments and standing in mid-air, cast them toward the Blessed One and scattered them upon the Blessed One. And they spoke these words: 'Long indeed may this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> endure among the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! As long as the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> will follow this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, so long will there be no disappearance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One; and the true Dharma will long endure; and the jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> will appear in the world; and the distinction of the conduct of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s will be made known. And in whatever direction those sons or daughters of good family will write this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, and make it into a book — that direction should be regarded as filled with light, that direction should be regarded by me as having a protector and as free from the darkness of obscurity.'

Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the divine sons up to those of <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, and said: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. So it is, divine sons, so it is. As long as the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> will follow this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, so long will there be no disappearance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and the true Dharma will long endure, and the jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> will be known in the world — and likewise throughout the trichiliocosm and throughout the world-systems in the ten directions in all quarters — there will be no disappearance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and all dharmas will long endure, and the jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> will appear in the world, and the distinction of the conduct of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s will be made known. And in whatever direction those sons or daughters of good family will write this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, and make it into a book — that direction should be regarded as filled with light, that direction having a protector and free from the darkness of obscurity appears to me.

body.text: atha bhagavāñ chakraṃ devānām indrakāṃś cākaniṣṭhaparyato devaputrān etad avocat: evam etat kauśikaivam etat, evam etad devaputrā evam etat, yāvad imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ jāmbūdvīpakā manuṣyā anuvartiṣyante, tāvat tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntardhānaṃ bhaviṣyati saddharmasya ca cirasthitikatā bhaviṣyati saṃgharatnasya ca loke prajñāyate yāvat trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau yāvat samanto daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatasyārhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntardhānaṃ bhaviṣyati, sarvadharmasya ca cirasthitikatā bhaviṣyati, saṃgharatnasya ca loke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati, bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ caryāviśeṣaḥ prajñāsyate, yatra ca digbhāge imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ te kulaputrā kuladuhitaro vā likhiṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti pustakagatām api kṛtvā ālokajātā ca sā dik pratikāṅkṣitavyā sanāthāvigatās tamondhakārā ca me sā dik pratibhāti.

atha te devaputrā punar api divyāni kusumāni abhinirmāya yena bhagavāṃs tenābhiprakiranti sma, evañ ca vācam abhāṣanta, yo hi kaścid bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati (

children.text: ) dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśas manasikariśyati. na tasya māro vā mārakāyikā vā devatā avatāraprakṣiṇo 'vatāraṃ lapsyante, vayam api bhagavaṃs tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā satatasamitaṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmaḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? śāstāram eva bhagavaṃs tam asya mahāśāstāram anyataraṃ vā yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vemāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati, yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati.
children.translated_text: ) will retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it — neither <s>Māra</s> nor the deities of <s>Māra</s>'s host will find an opportunity to gain entry against that person. We too, Blessed One, will constantly provide protection, guarding, and defense for that son of good family or daughter of good family. For what reason? Blessed One, we regard that person as a teacher, indeed a great teacher — or any son of good family or daughter of good family who will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it.'

body.translated_text: Then those divine sons, having again magically created divine blossoms, scattered them upon the Blessed One, and spoke these words: 'Whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, Blessed One, will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (

body.text: atha śakro devānām indro bhagavantam etad avocat: na te bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitaro vā avarakena kuśalamūlena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati, yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, sarvajinamanasikārās te bhagavan kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca bhaviṣyanti, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyanti, bahubuddhaparyupāsitāś ca te bhagavan kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca bhaviṣyanti, kalyāṇamitraparigṛhītāś ca te bhagavan kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaraś ca bhaviṣyanti, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyanti. tat kasya hetoḥ? ato hi bhagavan sarvākārajñatā gaveṣitavyā yad uta prajñāpāramitāyāḥ, ataś ca punar bhagavan prajñāpāramitā gaveṣitavyā, yad uta sarvākārajñatāyāḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan nānyā prajñāpāramitānyā sarvākārajñatānyā prajñāpāramitā iti hi prajñāpāramitā ca sarvākārajñatā nānyādvayam etad advaidhīkāram.
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: Those sons of good family or daughters of good family, Blessed One, will not be endowed with merely inferior roots of merit — those who will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it. Those sons of good family and daughters of good family, Blessed One, will be ones whose attention is directed toward all the Victorious Ones (<s>jina</s>) — those who will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it. Those sons of good family and daughters of good family, Blessed One, will be ones who have attended upon many <s>Buddha</s>s, and those sons of good family or daughters of good family, Blessed One, will be ones who have been taken under the care of spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) — those who will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it. For what reason? For indeed, Blessed One, the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) is to be sought from this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and furthermore, Blessed One, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be sought from the knowledge of all aspects. For what reason? For indeed, Blessed One, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not other than the knowledge of all aspects, nor is the knowledge of all aspects other than the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — for the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, without division.

body.text: bhagavān āha: evam etat kauśikaivam etat prajñāpāramitāniryātā hi kauśika tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ sarvākārajñatā, sarvākārajñātāniryātā ca prajñāpāramitā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi kauśika nānyā prajñāpāramitānyā sarvākārajñatā nānyā sarvākārajñatānyā prajñāpāramitā iti hi prajñāpāramitā ca sarvākārajñatā cādvayam etad advaidhīkāram.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones has issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has issued forth from the knowledge of all aspects. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not other than the knowledge of all aspects, nor is the knowledge of all aspects other than the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — for the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and the knowledge of all aspects are non-dual, without division.

body.text: śatasāhasryāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ viṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: The twentieth chapter of the <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: The Blessed One does not proclaim the name of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) in the same way, does not proclaim the name of the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) in the same way, does not proclaim the name of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) in the same way, does not proclaim the name of the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) in the same way, does not proclaim the name of the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) in the same way, as the Blessed One proclaims the name of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: bhagavān āha: prajñāpāramitā ānandaḥ pūrvāṅgamā pariṇāyikā yad uta pañcānāṃ pāramitānāṃ sarvaśūnyatānāṃ saptatriṃśānāṃ bodhipakṣāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ, āryasatyānāṃ caturṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ caturṇām apramāṇānāṃ catasṛṇām ārūpyasamāpattīnām aṣṭāṇāṃ vimokṣāṇāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattīnāṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhānām abhijñānāṃ samādhīnāṃ dhāraṇīmukhānāṃ daśatathāgatabalānāṃ caturṇāṃ vaiśāradyānāṃ pratisaṃvidāṃ mahāmaitryā mahākaruṇāyā aṣṭādaśānām āveṇikānāṃ buddhadharmāṇām. tat kiṃ manyase? ānandāpariṇāmitaṃ dānaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dānapāramitā bhavati.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the forerunner and guide — namely, of the five perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), of all the emptinesses (<s>śūnyatā</s>), of the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa dharma</s>), of the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), of the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), of the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), of the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), of the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), of the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), of the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, of the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), of the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), of the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), of the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, of the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), of great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and of the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>). What do you think, <s>Ānanda</s> — does giving not dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) become the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>)?

body.text: āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan.
body.translated_text: He said: No indeed, Blessed One.

body.text: bhagavān āha: tat kim apariṇāmitaṃ śīlaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ śīlapāramitā bhavati?
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: And does morality not dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects become the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>)?

body.text: āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan.
body.translated_text: He said: No indeed, Blessed One.

body.text: bhagavān āha: tat kim apariṇāmitaṃ kṣāntiṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitā bhavati?
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: And does patience not dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects become the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>)?

body.text: āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan.
body.translated_text: He said: No indeed, Blessed One.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: And does vigor not dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects become the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>)?

body.text: āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan.
body.translated_text: He said: No indeed, Blessed One.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: And does meditation not dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects become the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>)?

body.translated_text: He said: No indeed, Blessed One.

body.text: bhagavān āha: tat kim apariṇāmitaṃ prajñāṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ prajñāpāramitā bhavati?
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: And does wisdom not dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects become the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>)?

body.text: āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan. api tu khalu punaḥ kathaṃ bhagavan dānapāramitāṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dānapāramitā bhavati? kathaṃ bhagavan śīlapāramitāṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ śīlapāramitā bhavati? kathaṃ bhagavan kṣāntipāramitāṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitā bhavati? kathaṃ bhagavan vīryapāramitāṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ vīryapāramitā bhavati? kathaṃ bhagavan dhyānapāramitāṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dhyānapāramitā bhavati? kathaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ prajñāpāramitā bhavati?
body.translated_text: He said: No indeed, Blessed One. But then, Blessed One, how does the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) become the perfection of giving in relation to the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>)? How, Blessed One, does the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) become the perfection of morality in relation to the knowledge of all aspects? How, Blessed One, does the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) become the perfection of patience in relation to the knowledge of all aspects? How, Blessed One, does the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) become the perfection of vigor in relation to the knowledge of all aspects? How, Blessed One, does the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) become the perfection of meditation in relation to the knowledge of all aspects? How, Blessed One, does the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) become the perfection of wisdom in relation to the knowledge of all aspects?

body.text: bhagavān āha: advayayogenānanda pariṇāmitaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dānapāramitā bhavaty anutpādayogenānupalambhayogena pariṇāmitaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dānapāramitā bhavati, advayayogena pariṇāmitaṃ śīlaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ śīlapāramitā bhavaty anutpādayogenānupalambhayogena pariṇāmitaṃ śīlaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ śīlapāramitā bhavati, advayayogena pariṇāmitaṃ kṣāntiḥ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitā bhavaty anutpādayogenānupalambhayogena pariṇāmitā kṣāntiḥ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitā bhavati, advayayogena pariṇāmitaṃ vīryaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ vīryapāramitā bhavati, anutpādayogenānupalambhayogena pariṇāmitaṃ vīryaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ vīryapāramitā bhavati, advayayogena pariṇāmitaṃ dhyānaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dhyānapāramitā bhavaty anutpādayogenānupalambhayogena pariṇāmitaṃ dhyānaṃ sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dhyānapāramitā bhavati, advayayogena pariṇāmitā prajñā sarvākārajñatāyāṃ prajñāpāramitā bhavaty anutpādayogenānupalambhayogena pariṇāmitā prajñā sarvākārajñatāyāṃ prajñāpāramitā bhavati.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: <s>Ānanda</s>, giving dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects through the yoga of non-duality (<s>advayayoga</s>) becomes the perfection of giving; dedicated through the yoga of non-arising (<s>anutpādayoga</s>) and the yoga of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>), it becomes the perfection of giving in relation to the knowledge of all aspects. Morality dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of morality; dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension, morality becomes the perfection of morality in relation to the knowledge of all aspects. Patience dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of patience; dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension, patience becomes the perfection of patience in relation to the knowledge of all aspects. Vigor dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of vigor; dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension, vigor becomes the perfection of vigor in relation to the knowledge of all aspects. Meditation dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of meditation; dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension, meditation becomes the perfection of meditation in relation to the knowledge of all aspects. Wisdom dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of wisdom; dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension, wisdom becomes the perfection of wisdom in relation to the knowledge of all aspects.

Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: Not all the qualities of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Blessed One, have been proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One — those qualities which I have grasped, retained, and recited from the presence of the Blessed One. Whatever son or daughter of good family will embrace this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, grasping it, retaining it, reciting it, mastering it, and wisely attending to it — the qualities which I have grasped, mastered, retained, recited, and set in motion from the presence of the Blessed One regarding this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — Blessed One, when the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been grasped, retained, recited, mastered, set in motion, and wisely attended to, there is the manifestation in the world of the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśa kuśala karmapatha</s>) (

body.translated_text: Blessed One, when the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been grasped, retained, recited, mastered, set in motion, and wisely attended to, stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) become known in the world, once-returners (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) become known in the world, non-returners (<s>anāgāmin</s>) become known in the world, <s>arhat</s>s become known in the world, <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s become known in the world, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s become known in the world. body.text: bhagavān āha: na punaḥ kauśika yena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā udgrahītā bhaviṣyati dhāritā bhaviṣyati vācitā bhaviṣyati paryavāptā bhaviṣyati yoniśaś ca manasikṛtā bhaviṣyati tasyemām eva guṇān vadāmi. tat kasya hetoḥ?
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, it is not only these qualities that I declare for the son of good family or daughter of good family by whom this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will have been taken up, retained, recited, mastered, and wisely attended to. For what reason?

body.text: apramāṇena te kauśika śīlaskandhena samanvāgatā, kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā bhaviṣyanti, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhītā bhaviṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyanti, sarvākārajñatācittena cāvirahitā bhaviṣyati,
