body.text: śakra āha: aham api bhagavan tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā satatasamitaṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyāmi, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyanti, avirahitaś ca bhaviṣyanti sarvākārajñatācittena imāṃ ca prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā satkariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati, puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: I too, Blessed One, will constantly provide protection, guarding, and defense for that son of good family or daughter of good family who will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it, while remaining inseparable from the mind directed toward the knowledge of all aspects, and who, having written down this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will honor it, esteem it, and worship it with flowers, garlands, incense, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments.

body.text: bhagavān āha: tasya punaḥ kauśika kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ svadhyāyamānasya, bahūni devaputrasahasrāṇi manasidharmaśravaṇāyopasaṃkramiṣyanti. tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā prajñāpāramitā pratisaṃyuktaṃ dharmaṃ deśayatas te devaputrāḥ pratibhānam upasaṃhartavyaṃ maṃsyate, yad api te dharmabhānakānam atrāpi tu kāmā bhavanti, tat tenaiva dharmagauravena devaputrāḥ pratibhānam upasaṃhartavyaṃ maṃsyante, imam api sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikaguṇaṃ parigrahīṣyati, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyaty enāṃ ca likhitvā satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati, puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair (

children.translated_text: ) banners, streamers, and various musical instruments.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, when that son of good family or daughter of good family is reciting this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, many thousands of divine sons will approach in order to hear the Dharma. And when that son of good family or daughter of good family is teaching the Dharma connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, those divine sons will think that eloquence should be bestowed upon the Dharma preacher — and even though they may have desires of their own, out of that very reverence for the Dharma, those divine sons will think that eloquence should be bestowed. This too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is a quality visible in the present life that the son of good family or daughter of good family will obtain — one who takes up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retains it, recites it, masters it, and wisely attends to it, and who, having written it down, honors it, reveres it, esteems it, and worships it with flowers, garlands, incense, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments (

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāṣyamānasya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ purato 'nācalayatā bhaviṣyati, kaścit mām anuyokṣyati copalapsyate ca. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyati. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sarvadharmā abhinnā laukikā lokottaraś ca sāsravāś cānāsravāś ca sādhāraṇāś ca kuśalāś cākusalāś ca saṃskṛtāś cāsaṃskṛtāś ca śrāvakadharmāś ca pratyekabuddhadharmāś ca bodhisattvadharmāś ca buddhadharmāś ca. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy eṣā sarvaṃ kuśaladharmāṇāṃ nidhiḥ, sa ca kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā,
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, when that son of good family or daughter of good family is expounding this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> before the four assemblies, there will be fearlessness — 'Someone will question me and find fault.' For what reason? For indeed, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will provide protection, guarding, and defense for that son of good family or daughter of good family. For what reason? For indeed, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all dharmas are undivided — whether worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, shared or unshared, wholesome or unwholesome, conditioned or unconditioned, dharmas of <s>śrāvaka</s>s, dharmas of <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, dharmas of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, or dharmas of <s>Buddha</s>s. For what reason? For indeed, this is the treasury of all wholesome dharmas. And that son of good family or daughter of good family,

body.translated_text: established in internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), established in external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), established in internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), established in great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), established in ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), established in natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), established in the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) — that one, established in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> through non-apprehension, does not perceive that which might be reproached, nor does one perceive in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> the one who reproaches, nor does one perceive in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> the one who reproaches. Thus indeed, that son of good family or daughter of good family who has taken up the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will not be reproached by anyone.

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhṇato dhārayato vācayataḥ paryavāpnuvato yoniśaś ca manasikurvataś cittaṃ nācaleṣyate notrasiṣyati na saṃtrasiṣyati na saṃtrāsam āpatsyate. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā vastu na samanupaśyati, yo 'valīyeta vā saṃlīyeta vā uttrasyed vā saṃtrasyed vā saṃtrāsam āpadyed vā, imāṃ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān parigṛhīṣyanti, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, tāñ ca likhitvā satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati, puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, the mind of that son of good family or daughter of good family who is taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, and wisely attending to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will not waver, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, will not fall into terror. For what reason? For indeed, that son of good family or daughter of good family does not perceive any basis upon which one might shrink back, cower, be frightened, be terrified, or fall into terror. This too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is a quality visible in the present life that sons of good family or daughters of good family will obtain — those who take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it, and who, having written it down, honor it, revere it, esteem it, and worship it with flowers, garlands, incense, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments.

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika yo hi kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ udgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati, tāñ ca likhitvā satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati, pūjayiṣyati, puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ. sa priyo bhaviṣyati mātāpitṝṇāṃ mitrāmātyajñātisālohitānāṃ rājñāṃ rājamahāmātrāṇāṃ śravaṇabrāhmaṇānāṃ ye 'pi te daśasu dikṣu lokadhātuṣu buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvāḥ pratyekabuddhāś cārhantaś cānāgāminaś ca sakṛdāgāminaś ca srotaāpannāś ca teṣām api sa priyo bhaviṣyati, manāpaś ca sadevasya lokasya sabrahmakasya saśravaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ priyo bhaviṣyati, manāpaś ca anācchedya pratibhānaś ca bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, and wisely attend to it, and having written it down, will honor it, revere it, esteem it, and worship it with flowers, garlands, incense, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments — that person will be dear to parents, friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen, to kings and chief royal ministers, and to ascetics and brahmins. And to those <s>Buddha</s>s and Blessed Ones, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s, <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, <s>arhat</s>s, non-returners (<s>anāgāmin</s>), once-returners (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), and stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) who abide in the world-systems of the ten directions — to them too that person will be dear and agreeable. That person will be dear and agreeable to the world with its gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, and its ascetics and brahmins, to the populace including gods, humans, and <s>asura</s>s, and will possess uninterrupted eloquence.

body.text: anacchedyā dānapāramitā bhaviṣyati, anācchedyā śīlapāramitā bhaviṣyati, anācchedyā kṣāntipāramitā bhaviṣyati, anācchedyā vīryapāramitā bhaviṣyati, anācchedyā dhyānapāramitā bhaviṣyati, anācchedyā prajñāpāramitā bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: The perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) will be uninterrupted, the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) will be uninterrupted, the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) will be uninterrupted, the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) will be uninterrupted, the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) will be uninterrupted, the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) will be uninterrupted.

body.translated_text: His cultivation of internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable, his cultivation of the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) will be unbreakable.

body.text: anācchedyā cāsya sattvaparipāko bhaviṣyaty anācchedyā buddhakṣetrapariśuddhir bhaviṣyaty anācchedyā cāsya sarvākārajñatā bhaviṣyati pratibalaś ca bhaviṣyati purataḥ utpannotpannānāṃ pratyanuyogānāṃ sahadharmeṇa niḥśaraṇe imān api sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān parigṛhiṣyati ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś manasikariṣyaty avirahitaś ca bhaviṣyati sarvākārajñatācittena tāṃś ca likhitvā satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ.
body.translated_text: His ripening of beings will be unbreakable, his purification of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (buddha-field) will be unbreakable, and his knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) will be unbreakable. He will be capable of responding to questions that arise before him in accordance with the Dharma. That son or daughter of good family who will grasp this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, wisely attend to it, and will not be separated from the mind directed toward the knowledge of all aspects, and having written it will honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music — that person too will acquire these benefits visible in this very life.

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika yo hi kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā dhārayiṣyati, tatra kauśika ye trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau cāturmahārājakāyikā devaputrā anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye saṃprasthitās trāyastriṃśā yāmās tuṣitā nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikā devā brahmapurohitā devā brahmapārṣadyā mahābrahmāṇa ābhāḥ parīttābhā apramāṇābhā ābhāsvarāḥ śubhāḥ parīttaśubhā apramāṇaśubbāḥ śubhakṛtsnāḥ, bṛhāḥ parīttabṛhā apramāṇabṛhā bṛhatphalā anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye saṃprasthitāḥ, te tatrāgatyemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ vācitvodgṛhya paryavāpya vanditvā namaskṛtya punar api prakramitavyaṃ maṃsyante, ye 'pi te śuddhāvāsakāyikā devā abṛhā atapāḥ sudṛśāḥ sudarśanā akaniṣṭhāḥ, te 'pi tatrāgamyemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ vācitvodgṛhya paryavāpya vanditvā namaskṛtya punar api prakramitavyaṃ maṃsyante.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son or daughter of good family will hold this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in the form of a book — therein, <s>Kauśika</s>, those divine sons of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven in the trichiliocosm who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Ābhā</s>, <s>Parīttābhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇābhā</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Śubha</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Bṛhā</s>, <s>Parīttabṛhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇabṛhā</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening — those will come there, and having recited and grasped and mastered and paid homage and obeisance to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will think it proper to depart again. And those gods dwelling in the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) — the <s>Abṛhā</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśā</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — they too will come there, and having recited and grasped and mastered and paid homage and obeisance to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will think it proper to depart again.

body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, those divine sons of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven in the world-systems of the ten directions who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Ābhā</s>, <s>Parīttābhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇābhā</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Śubha</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Bṛhā</s>, <s>Parīttabṛhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇabṛhā</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening, and those gods dwelling in the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> — the <s>Abṛhā</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśā</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> — and also other greatly powerful gods, <s>nāga</s>s, <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>gandharva</s>s, <s>asura</s>s, <s>garuḍa</s>s, <s>kiṃnara</s>s, and <s>mahoraga</s>s — they too will come there, and having recited and grasped and mastered and paid homage and obeisance to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they will think it proper to depart again.

This too, <s>Kauśika</s>, is a benefit visible in this very life that that son or daughter of good family will acquire: that divine sons who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening will think it proper to come there for the worship of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and for the protection, guarding, and defense of that son or daughter of good family. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, those sons of good family who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening stand ready for the benefit and welfare and happiness of all beings.

body.translated_text: Therein, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son or daughter of good family should generate this thought: 'Those divine sons of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven in the world-systems of the ten directions, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Ābhā</s>, <s>Parīttābhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇābhā</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Śubha</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Bṛhā</s>, <s>Parīttabṛhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇabṛhā</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods who have set out for unsurpassed perfect awakening, and those gods dwelling in the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> — the <s>Abṛhā</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśā</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> — and also other greatly powerful gods, <s>nāga</s>s, <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>gandharva</s>s, <s>asura</s>s, <s>garuḍa</s>s, <s>kiṃnara</s>s, and <s>mahoraga</s>s who have come here to recite, grasp, master, pay homage, and worship this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — may this gift of Dharma (<s>dharmadāna</s>) be given to them. Having recited, grasped, mastered, worshipped, paid homage, and obeisance to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they depart again.' Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, for that son or daughter of good family, those divine sons of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven in the trichiliocosm, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Ābhā</s>, <s>Parīttābhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇābhā</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Śubha</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Bṛhā</s>, <s>Parīttabṛhā</s>, <s>Apramāṇabṛhā</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛhā</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśā</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and those divine sons of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven in the world-systems of the ten directions, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: <s>Kauśika</s>, if that son or daughter of good family perceives a great radiance (<s>avabhāsa</s>) in the place where this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been placed, the conclusion (

Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family is one of pure conduct, then by virtue of that pure conduct, the deities, having come, will recite this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, take it up, master it, honor it, revere it, respect it, worship it, and will become joyful. And the deities of lesser power who inhabit that region will think they should approach. Being unable to endure the splendor, glory, and majesty of those great and mighty deities, to the degree that the great and mighty, greatly powerful, and greatly majestic deities think they should approach, to that degree that son of good family or daughter of good family will be one of lofty aspiration. And impure conduct should not be practiced in the vicinity of that place. That son of good family or daughter of good family should, for the worship-ceremony of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, sprinkle that spot of ground with scented water, strew it with flowers and fragrances, fumigate it with incense-balls, drape it with silken garlands and fabric canopies, and adorn that spot of ground to be pleasing to the eye.

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika sacet kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā caukṣasamācāro bhavati tasya tayā caukṣasamācāratayā devatā āgamyemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ vācayitvodgṛhya paryavāpya satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvā āttamanaskā bhaviṣyati, yāś ca tatra pradeśo alpaśākhyadevatā adhyuṣitā bhaviṣyanti tās tatropasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyate. tāsāṃ maheśākhyānāṃ devātānāṃ tejaś ca śriyaṃ ca gauravaṃ cāsahamānā, yathā yathā maheśākhyamaheśākhyā maharddhikā mahānubhāvā devatā upasaṃkramitavyā maṃsyate, tathā tathā sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā udārādhimuktiko bhaviṣyati. tasya ca sthānasya samantād acaukṣasamudācāratā na pracārayitavyā, tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā asyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pūjākarmaṇe gandhodakāvasiktaḥ sa pṛthivīpradeśaḥ kartavyaḥ puṣpagandhāvakīrṇagandhaghaṭikānidhūpitaḥ, avasaktapaṭṭadāmācailavitānavitato netrapracāraṃ ca tat sa pṛthivīpradeśo 'laṃkartavyaḥ.

na punaḥ kauśika kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā kāyaklamatho bhaviṣyati kāyasukhatāṃ ca kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saṃjñāsyate. kāyalaghutāṃ ca kāyakathanīyataṃ ca cittasukhatāṃ ca sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saṃjñāsyate cittalaghutāṃ ca cittakam athanīyatāṃ ca tataḥ sa rātrau śayyāṃ kalpayantīmām eva prajñāpāramitām aśayeṇādhimuñcan na pāpakān svapnān drakṣati sa paśyaṃs tathāgatam evārhantan samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ drakṣyati dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvagatam aśītyanuvyañjanaiḥ samalaṃkṛtasuvarṇavarṇena kāyena bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtaṃ bodhisattvagaṇapuraskṛtaṃ dharmaṃ deśayataṃ tasya ca tathāgatasyāntikād dharmaṃ śroṣyati, yad uta dānapāramitāṃ śīlapāramitāṃ kṣāntipāramitāṃ vīryapāramitāṃ dhyānapāramitāṃ prajñāpāramitām.
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family will not experience bodily fatigue, and will perceive bodily comfort. That son of good family or daughter of good family will perceive bodily lightness, bodily agreeableness, mental comfort, mental lightness, and mental agreeableness. Then, when lying down to sleep at night, aspiring toward this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with intention, they will not see evil dreams. What they see will be the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One himself — endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being, adorned with the eighty minor characteristics, with a body of golden color, surrounded by the community of monks and attended by an assembly of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, teaching the Dharma. And from that <s>Tathāgata</s> they will hear the Dharma — namely, the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: smṛtyupasthānāni samyakprahāṇāni ṛddhipādā indriyāṇi balāni bodhyaṅgāni āryāṣṭāṅgo mārga āryasatyāni dhyānāni apramāṇāni ārūpyasamāpattayo aṣṭau vimokṣā navānupūrvavihārasamāpattīḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāni, abhijñā samādhīn dhāraṇīmukhāni daśatathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvido mahākaruṇām aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāś ca.
body.translated_text: The foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the powers (<s>bala</s>), the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>).

body.text: tasyāś ca dānapāramitāyā arthaṃ vibhajyamānaṃ śroṣyanti, tasyāś ca śīlapāramitāyā arthaṃ vibhajyamānaṃ śrosyati, tasyāś ca vīryapāramitāyā arthaṃ vibhajyamānaṃ śroṣyati, tasyāś ca kṣāntipāramitāyā arthaṃ vibhajyamānaṃ śroṣyati, tasyāś ca dhyānapāramitāyā arthaṃ vibhajyamānaṃ śroṣyati, tasyāś ca prajñāpāramitāyā arthaṃ vibhajyamānaṃ śroṣyati.

body.translated_text: They will hear the meaning of internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>) being expounded, and will hear the meaning of external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) being expounded, and will hear the meaning of internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>) being expounded, and likewise the meaning of the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) being expounded.

That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, will indeed see these very auspicious dreams of fine forms. He will sleep happily and will awaken happily. His body will become infused with a current (<s>srotaprakṣipta</s>), and he will perceive lightness in his body, not heaviness. He will not have strong craving for food, nor craving for robes, nor craving for medicines and medical requisites for the sick. His perception of food will be gentle, his perception of robes will be gentle, his perception of medicines and medical requisites for the sick will be gentle.

body.text: sa khalu punaḥ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imān eva rūpān bhadrakā svapnān drakṣyati, sa sukham eva śayyāṃ kalpayiṣyati sukhaṃ ca prativibhotsyate srotaprakṣiptaś cāsya kāyo bhhaviṣyati, laghusaṃjñā ca kāye saṃjñāsyate na gurusaṃjñā na cāsya balavatyāhāragṛddhir bhaviṣyati na cīvaragṛddhir bhaviṣyati na glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāragṛdhir bhaviṣyati, mṛddhī cāsyāhārasaṃjñā bhaviṣyati mṛddhīcīvarasaṃjñā bhaviṣyati mṛddhīglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraṃ saṃjñā bhaviṣyati.
tad yathāpi nāma kauśika yogācārasya bhikṣoḥ samādhavyutthitasya manasikārapariṣyandi tena cittena balavatyāhāragṛddhir bhaviṣyati mṛdukā cāsyāhārasaṃjñā bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kauśika</s>, a monk who practices <s>yoga</s> (<s>yogācāra</s>), having emerged from <s>samādhi</s>, with a mind flowing with mental attention (<s>manasikārapariṣyandi</s>) — with that mind he will not have strong craving for food, and his perception of food will be gentle.

body.text: evam eva kauśika tasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā na bakavatyāhāragṛddhir bhaviṣyati. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tasyā mānuṣyāḥ kāye srota upasaṃhariṣyati.
body.translated_text: Just so, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family will not have strong craving for food. For what reason? For indeed, a divine current will be infused into his human body.

body.text: imām api kauśika dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān parigṛhītukāmena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā iyam eva prajñāpāramitāprayatvataḥ srotavyodgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā yoniśaś ca manasikartavyāḥ. sarvākārajñatācittena cāvirahitena bhavitavyāḥ.
body.translated_text: A son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, who wishes to embrace these qualities visible in this very life, should diligently hear, take up, retain, recite, master, and wisely attend to this very perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), and should not be separated from the mind directed toward the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>).

body.text: atha cet sa kauśika kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ nodgṛhīyān na dhārayen na vācayen na paryavāpnuyān na yoniśaś ca manasikuryāt tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitāṃ pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā satkartavyā gurukartavyā mānayitavyā pūjayitavyā puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś cchattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ.
body.translated_text: But if, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family cannot take up, retain, recite, master, or wisely attend to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, then that son of good family or daughter of good family should write this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, make it into a book, and honor, revere, respect, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music.

body.text: evaṃ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahujanahitāya pratipanno bhaviṣyati bahujanasukhāya pratipanno bhaviṣyati, yo hi kaścit kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā puṇyaṃ prasaviṣyati na tve vayaḥ samatād (

body.translated_text: Thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family will have set out for the benefit of many beings, will have set out for the happiness of many beings. For whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, will produce merit — not even equal in measure (

body.text: śatasāhasryāḥ prajñāpāramitāya ekaviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: The twenty-first chapter of the <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: If, <s>Kauśika</s>, you were to obtain this <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> filled to the brim with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, and if this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> were offered to you written as a book — which would you take up?

body.text: atha bhagavāñ chakraṃ devānām indram āmantrayata: sacet tvaṃ kauśikemaṃ jāmbūdvīpaṃ pūrṇaṃ cūḍikāvabaddhaṃ tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ labhethā yac ceyaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakaṃ likhitvopanāmyeta, kiṃ tvaṃ tata udgṛhīyāḥ?

śakra āha: sacen me bhagavann ayaṃ jāmbūdvīpaḥ pūrṇacūḍikāvabaddhas tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ dīpeta yac ceyaṃ prajñāpāramitā pustakaṃ likhitvopanāmyeta imām evāhaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitāṃ gṛhṇīyām. tat kasya hetoḥ? na me bhagavan tatra tathāgataśarīreṣv agauravaṃ nāpratyayaṃ nābahumānatā nāpy ahaṃ bhagavaṃs tathāgataśarīrāṇi, na satkartukāmo na gurukartukāmo na mānayitukāmo na pūjayitukāmaḥ, api tu khalu punar bhagavan prajñāpāramitā niryātāni tāni śarīrāṇi tena tena tathāgataśarīrāṇi satkriyante gurukriyante mānyante pūjayante prajñāpāramitā paribhāvitāni śarīrāṇi tena tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjā labhante, yadāhaṃ bhagavan tathāgataśarīrāṇi satkuryāṃ gurukuryāṃ mānayeyaṃ pūjayeyaṃ divyaiḥ puṣpair divyair mālyair divyair gandhair divyair vilepanair divyaiś cūrṇair divyaiś cīvarair divyaiś chattrair divyair dhvajair divyābhiḥ patākābhir divyaiś ca vādyais tat prajñāpāramitā paribhāvitānīti kṛtvā yac ca tathāgataśarīrāṇi sadevamānuṣāsurena lokena satkrīyante gurukriyante mānyante pūjyante tat prajñāpāramitā paribhāvitānīti kṛtvā.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: If, Blessed One, this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> were heaped full of <s>Tathāgata</s> relics bound up in bundles, and this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> were offered having been written as a book — I, Blessed One, would take this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? It is not, Blessed One, that I have no reverence, no faith, or no esteem for those <s>Tathāgata</s> relics; nor am I, Blessed One, unwilling to honor, respect, esteem, and worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics. But rather, Blessed One, those relics have issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and it is for that reason that the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics are honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped — the relics have been pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and therefore those <s>Tathāgata</s> relics receive worship. When I, Blessed One, honor, respect, esteem, and worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics with divine flowers, divine garlands, divine fragrances, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine pennants, and divine music — that is because they have been pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And that the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics are honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped by the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asura</s>s — that too is because they have been pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha khalv āyuṣmāñ chāradvatīputraḥ śakraṃ devānām indram etad avocat: iyaṃ kauśika prajñāpāramitā agrāhyā arūpiṇī anidarśanā apratighā ekalakṣaṇā yad utālakṣaṇā. tat kathaṃ tvam agrāhyā prajñāpāramitām arūpiṇīm anidarśanām apratighā ekalakṣaṇā yad utālakṣaṇā grahītavyāṃ maṃyase. tat kasya hetoḥ? na hi prajñāpāramitā grahāya notsargāya pratyupasthitā na hānaye na vṛddhaye nācayāya notkṣepāya na saṃkleśāya na vyavadānāya na buddhadharmāṇāṃ dātrī na pṛthagjanadharmāṇāṃ chorayitrī na bodhisattvadharmāṇāṃ dātri na pratyekabuddhadharmāṇāṃ dātrī na śrāvakadharmaṇāṃ dātrī na śaikṣāśaikṣādharmāṇāṃ dātrī na pṛthagjanadharmāṇāṃ chorayitrī nāsaṃskṛtadhātor dātrī na saṃskṛtadhātoś chorayitrī na dānapāramitāyā dātrī na śīlapāramitāyā dātrī na kṣāntipāramitāyā dātrī na vīryapāramitāyā dātrī na dhyānapāramitāyā dātri na prajñāpāramitāyā dātrī.
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: <s>Kauśika</s>, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is ungraspable (<s>agrāhya</s>), formless (<s>arūpin</s>), non-indicative (<s>anidarśana</s>), non-resistant (<s>apratigha</s>), of one characteristic — namely, no characteristic (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>). How then do you think the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — ungraspable, formless, non-indicative, non-resistant, of one characteristic, namely no characteristic — is to be grasped? For what reason? For indeed, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not present for grasping nor for releasing, not for diminishing nor for increasing, not for accumulating nor for dispersing, not for defilement nor for purification; it is not a giver of the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, not a remover of the qualities of an ordinary being, not a giver of the qualities of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, not a giver of the qualities of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, not a giver of the qualities of a <s>śrāvaka</s>, not a giver of the qualities of those in training and beyond training, not a remover of the qualities of an ordinary being, not a giver of the unconditioned element, not a remover of the conditioned element; not a giver of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), not a giver of the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), not a giver of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), not a giver of the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), not a giver of the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), not a giver of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: śakra āha: evam etad bhadanta śāradvatīputraivam etad yo bhadanta śāradvatīputraivaṃ jānāti, na prajñāpāramitā buddhadharmāṇāṃ dātri na pṛthagjanadharmaṇāṃ chorayitrī na bodhisattvadharmāṇāṃ dātrī na pratyekabuddhadharmāṇāṃ dātrī na śrāvakadharmāṇāṃ dātrī na śaikṣāśaikṣadharmāṇāṃ dātrī na pṛthagjanadharmāṇāṃś chorayitrī nāsaṃskṛtadhātor dātri na saṃskṛtadhātor chorayitrī.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: So it is, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, so it is. Whoever, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, knows thus — that the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not a giver of the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, not a remover of the qualities of an ordinary being, not a giver of the qualities of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, not a giver of the qualities of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, not a giver of the qualities of a <s>śrāvaka</s>, not a giver of the qualities of those in training and beyond training, not a remover of the qualities of an ordinary being, not a giver of the unconditioned element, not a remover of the conditioned element —

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: This <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Blessed One, is to be worshipped by the world including its gods, humans, and <s>asura</s>s — this through training in which <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. Just as, Blessed One, when I am seated on my own throne in the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall of the gods, the divine sons come to attend upon me and honor me; and when I do not go there, those divine sons, having come to that assembly and having bowed to that throne and circumambulated it, then depart — here, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, seated, teaches the Dharma to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. Just so, Blessed One, wherever this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will be retained in writing and recited, and will be explained in detail to others, there the gods, <s>nāga</s>s, <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>gandharva</s>s, <s>asura</s>s, <s>garuḍa</s>s, <s>kiṃnara</s>s, and <s>mahoraga</s>s of the world-systems in the ten directions (

For indeed, the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones have issued forth from this; and all <s>śrāvaka</s>s and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s have issued forth from this; and all provisions for the happiness of beings have issued forth from this. And the worship that <s>Tathāgata</s> relics receive — that too is received because of being pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Blessed One, is the foundation, the condition, the cause, and the sustainer of the knowledge of the omniscient (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>) for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct. Therefore, Blessed One, between these two objects of reverence, I would take up this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. When, Blessed One, I take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and, having taken it up, recite it, with a mind absorbed in the Dharma, I do not perceive even a sign at that time — neither of fear nor of rigidity. For what reason?

If, Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) had a sign, were not signless, then the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One would not have, having known all dharmas as signless, without marks, inexpressible, and unutterable, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and would not teach beings the Dharma that is signless, without marks, inexpressible, and unutterable. But since, Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is signless, without marks, inexpressible, and unutterable, therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having known all dharmas as without marks, inexpressible, and unutterable, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, teaches beings the Dharma that is signless, without marks, inexpressible, and unutterable. Therefore, Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) should be honored, revered, respected, and worshipped by the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asura</s>s, with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music. And having been written, it should be honored, revered, respected, and worshipped with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music.

body.translated_text: for that person, rebirth in the hells is not to be expected, nor in the animal realm, nor in the world of <s>Yama</s>; nor is the level of a <s>śrāvaka</s> or the level of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> to be expected — rather, he will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). He will be inseparable from the sight of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and as one who matures beings, he will travel from <s>Buddha</s>-field to <s>Buddha</s>-field, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music.

body.text: punar bhagavan saced ayaṃ trisāhasro lokadhātuś cūḍikāvabaddhaḥ syāt tathāgataśarīraiḥ pūrṇo yac ceyaṃ prajñāpāramitā likhitvopanāmyate. anayor ahaṃ bhagavan dvayor bhāgayor imām eva prajñāpāramitāṃ gṛhṇīyām. tat kasya hetoḥ? ato niryātā hi bhagavans tathāgatās tāni ca tathāgataśarīrāṇi tena tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi satkriyante gurukriyante mānyante pūjyante yāni kulaputrāś ca kuladuhitaraś ca satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvā na durgatiṃ vinipātaṃ gacchanti. divyamānuṣīḥ saṃpattīr anubhūya yathā praṇidhānaṃ parinirvāti. yadi vā śrāvakayānena yadi vā pratyekabuddhayānena yadi vā samyaksaṃbuddhayānena, api tu khalu punar bhagavan yac ca tathāgatadarśanaṃ yac ca prajñāpāramitāyā darśanaṃ tulyam etat. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan prajñāpāramitā ca tathāgataś cādvayam etad advaidhīkāram.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, Blessed One, even if this trichiliocosm were filled to the brim with relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, and if this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> were offered written as a book — of these two, Blessed One, I would take up this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? For indeed, Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>s and those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body have issued forth from this. Therefore those relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are honored, revered, respected, and worshipped; and sons and daughters of good family, having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped them, do not go to an unfortunate destiny or downfall. Having enjoyed divine and human excellences, they attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> according to their vow — whether through the vehicle of <s>śrāvaka</s>s, the vehicle of <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, or the vehicle of perfect <s>Buddha</s>s. Moreover, Blessed One, seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s> and seeing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> are equivalent. For what reason? For indeed, Blessed One, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and the <s>Tathāgata</s> are non-dual (<s>advaya</s>), without division.

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhagavan yac ca tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas triṣu prātihāryeṣu sthitvā dharmadeśayet sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ gāthodānanidānetyuktakajātakavaipulyādbhutadharmāvadānopadeśāt, yac ca kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhya paryavāpya parasmai deśayet tulyam etat. tat kasya hetoḥ? ito niryātā hi bhagavan tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā iti niryātāni trīṇi prātihāryāṇi. ito niryātaṃ sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ gāthodānanidānetyuktakajātakavaipulyadbhutadharmāvadānopadeśāḥ.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, Blessed One, if the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, established in the three miraculous displays (<s>prātihārya</s>), were to teach the Dharma — <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>nidāna</s>, <s>ityuktaka</s>, <s>jātaka</s>, <s>vaipulya</s>, <s>adbhutadharma</s>, <s>avadāna</s>, and <s>upadeśa</s> — and if a son or daughter of good family, having taken up and mastered this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, were to teach it to others, these are equivalent. For what reason? For indeed, Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones have issued forth from this; from this have issued forth the three miraculous displays; from this have issued forth <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>nidāna</s>, <s>ityuktaka</s>, <s>jātaka</s>, <s>vaipulya</s>, <s>adbhutadharma</s>, <s>avadāna</s>, and <s>upadeśa</s>.

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhagavan yac ca te daśasu dikṣv ekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ satkriyeran gurukriyeran mānayeran pūjayeran puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ. yaś ca prajñāpāramitā pustakaṃ likhitvā satkriyeta gurukriyeta mānyeta pūjyeta puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyais tulyam etat. tat kasya hetoḥ? ito niryātā hi tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, Blessed One, if the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones in each of the ten directions, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were honored, revered, respected, and worshipped with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music — and if one were to write this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as a book and honor, revere, respect, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music — these are equivalent. For what reason? For indeed, the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones have issued forth from this.

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati tasya narakagatiḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyā na tiryagyonir na yamalokagatiḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyā na śrāvakabhūmir na pratyekabuddhabhūmiḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā sthito 'vaivartyabhūmau veditavyaḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi sa imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvodgṛhṇāti dhārayati vācayati paryavāpnoti yoniśaś ca manasikaroti tāṃ ca likhitvā satkaroti gurukaroti mānayati pūjayati puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyais tathā hi bhagavan sarvabhayapraśamani sarvaroganirghātanīyaṃ prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, Blessed One, whatever son or daughter of good family will take up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, retain it, recite it, master it, wisely attend to it, and explain it to others in detail — for that person, rebirth in the hells is not to be expected, nor in the animal realm, nor in the world of <s>Yama</s>; nor is the level of a <s>śrāvaka</s> or the level of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> to be expected. For what reason? For indeed, that son or daughter of good family should be known as one who stands on the stage of non-regression (<s>avaivartya bhūmi</s>). For what reason? For indeed, that person takes up this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having written it, retains it, recites it, masters it, wisely attends to it, and having written it, honors, reveres, respects, and worships it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music. For indeed, Blessed One, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the pacifier of all fears and the destroyer of all diseases.

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhagavan yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvodgṛhīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati tāṃ ca satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyais tasya na kutaścid bhayaṃ pratikāṅkṣitavyā, tad yathāpi nāma (

children.text: ) bhagavan dhanikabhayabhītaḥ puruṣo rājānaṃ seveta rājānam upatiṣṭheta sa rājānaṃ sevamāno rājānam upatiṣṭhamāno yata evāsya bhayaṃ bhavati ta evaivaṃ sevante na ca sa tebhyo bibheti. tat kasya hetoḥ? evam etad bhagavan bhavati yo rājaniḥśrito bhavati balavatiniśrito bhavati.
children.translated_text: ) Blessed One, a man afraid of danger from creditors would attend upon a king and wait upon a king. Attending upon and waiting upon the king, those very ones from whom his fear arose likewise attend upon the king, and he does not fear them. For what reason? So it is, Blessed One: one who relies on the king relies on one who is powerful.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, Blessed One, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family will write this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, take it up, retain it, recite it, and master it, and will honor, respect, esteem, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, pennants, and various kinds of music — that person need not apprehend fear from any quarter. Just as, for example (

body.text: evam eva bhagavan prajñāpāramitā paribhāvitāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhate. yad api bhagavan sarvākārajñatājñānaṃ tad api prajñāpāramitāparibhāvitaṃ draṣṭavyam, tasmād ahaṃ bhagavann anayor dvayoḥ pratyaṅgayor imām eva prajñāpāramitāṃ gṛhṇīyāt. tat kasya hetoḥ? ito niryātāni hi bhagavan tathāgataśarīrāṇy ato niryātāni dvātriṃśan mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāny ato niryātāni tathāgatasya daśatathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvido 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmāḥ, ato niryātā mahāmaitrī mahākaruṇā ato niryātā bhagavan pañcapāramitā pāramitānāmadheyaṃ labhate, yāvad ato niryātā tathāgatasya sarvākārajñatā yatra bhagavan grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu yatra ca trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātāv iyaṃ prajñāpāramitodgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyate vācayiṣyate paryavāpsyate tāṃ ca likhitvā satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyate pūjayiṣyate, tena tatra manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vāvatāraprekṣy avatāragaveṣy avatāraṃ lapsyate. sarve ca te anupūrveṇa parinirvānadharmāṇo bhaviṣyanti, trayāṇāṃ yānānāṃ manyat amānyat anena yānena. evaṃ mahārthikā bhagavann iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā, atra hi nāma bhagavaṃs trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvānāṃ buddhasatyena pratyupasthitā buddhotpādo bhagavaṃs tatra lokadhātau pratikāṅkṣitavyā, yatra lokadhātāv iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā pracariṣyate, tad yathāpi nāma bhagavann anargho 'yaṃ mahāmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet, tac ca mahāmaṇiratnam ebhir evaṃrūpair guṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ bhavet,
body.translated_text: Just so, Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics that have been pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> receive worship. Even the knowledge of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatājñāna</s>), Blessed One, is to be regarded as pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Therefore, Blessed One, between these two objects of reverence, I would take this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? For from this have issued forth the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics; from this have issued forth the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>dvātriṃśat mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>); from this have issued forth the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s ten powers (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), and eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>); from this have issued forth great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>); from this, Blessed One, have issued forth the five perfections that receive the designation '<s>pāramitā</s>'; and from this has issued forth the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). Wherever, Blessed One — in villages, cities, market towns, districts, kingdoms, or royal capitals, and wherever in the trichiliocosm — this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will be taken up, retained, recited, and mastered, and written down and honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped — there no human or non-human seeking an opportunity, looking for an opening, will find an opening. And all of them will progressively become ones destined for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, through whichever of the three vehicles they may follow. So greatly beneficial, Blessed One, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For indeed, Blessed One, in whatever world-system of this trichiliocosm the truth of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhasatya</s>) is present for beings — in that world-system, Blessed One, the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is to be expected, wherever this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will circulate. Just as, Blessed One, there might be a priceless great jewel (<s>mahāmaṇiratna</s>), and that great jewel would be endowed with such qualities as these:

body.text: yatra yatra tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ sthāpyet, tatra tatrāmanuṣyā avatāraṃ na labheran, yatrāmanuṣyagṛhītā stri vā puruṣo vā bhavet, tatra tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ praveśet, tataḥ so 'manuṣyas tasya mahāmaṇiratnasya tejo sahamānaḥ kṣipram evāprakrāman nāvatiṣṭheta pittena vā dahyamānasya tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ śarīre sthāpyeta tad api pittam atigṛhṇīyāt pātābhibhūte vā śarīre tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ sthāpyet tad api vā taṃ atigṛhṇīyāt.
body.translated_text: wherever that great jewel is placed, there non-human beings would not find an opening. Wherever a woman or man is possessed by a non-human being, if that great jewel is brought there, then that non-human being, unable to endure the power of the great jewel, would quickly depart and not remain. If one whose body is burning with bile has that great jewel placed on their body, it would overcome that bile. If it is placed on a body afflicted by an imbalance of humors, it would overcome that too.

children.translated_text: ) increase. At night it would produce illumination. And when the hot season is present, wherever that great jewel is placed, it would make that place cool. When the cold season is present, wherever that great jewel is placed, it would make that place warm. Wherever on the earth that great jewel is placed, on that spot of earth it would make it neither too hot nor too cold, endowed with softness. Wherever on the earth that great jewel is placed, on that spot of earth no venomous serpent would approach.

body.translated_text: If that great jewel is placed on a body stiffened by phlegm, it would pacify that phlegm. If there were a disease caused by the conjunction of the three humors (<s>sāṃnipātika</s>), and that great jewel were placed on the body, it would pacify that disease of the three humors and it would not (

body.text: tad anye 'pi ca vṛścikādayaḥ sarīsṛpāḥ prāṇino na tatropacaret. yā kācid bhagavan strī vā puruṣo vā āśīviṣeṇa daṣṭho bhavet, tasya tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ darśet tasya sahadarśanena tad viṣaṃ vigacchet.
body.translated_text: Nor would other scorpions, creeping creatures, or living beings approach there. Blessed One, whatever woman or man has been bitten by a venomous serpent — if that great jewel is shown to them, at the very sight of it, that poison would dissipate.

body.text: ebhir bhagavann evaṃrūpair guṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet, yāsām api bhagavan strīṇāṃ vā puruṣāṇāṃ vā arbudaṃ vā timiraṃ vā ajakaṃ vā akṣirogo vā srotarogo vā ghrāṇarogo vā jihvārogo vā kaṇṭharogo vā kāyarogo vā bhavet teṣāṃ tan māhamaṇiratnaṃ kāye sthāpyet, teṣāṃ tad arbudaṃ vā vā timiraṃ vā ajakaṃ vā akṣirogo vā srotrarogo vā ghrāṇarogo vā jihvārogo vā kaṇṭharogo vā kāyarogo vā upaśāmyet.
body.translated_text: That great jewel, Blessed One, would be endowed with such qualities. And whatever women or men, Blessed One, have a tumor, or a cataract, or a goiter, or an eye disease, or an ear disease, or a nose disease, or a tongue disease, or a throat disease, or a bodily disease — if that great jewel is placed on their body, their tumor, or cataract, or goiter, or eye disease, or ear disease, or nose disease, or tongue disease, or throat disease, or bodily disease would be pacified.

body.text: ebhir bhagavann evaṃrūpair guṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ bhavet, yatrāpi bhagavann udake tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ prakṣipet, tad eva tad udakam aṣṭāṅgopetam ekavarṇaṃ bhavet.
body.translated_text: That great jewel, Blessed One, would be endowed with such qualities. If, Blessed One, that great jewel were cast into water, that very water would become endowed with eight qualities and of one color.

body.text: sacet bhagavan nīlakena cīvareṇa tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ baddhvodake prakṣipyet, tat svabhāvam eva tad udakaṃ bhavet, sacet pītakena cīvareṇa tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ baddhvodake prakṣipyet, tat svabhāvam eva tad udakaṃ bhavet, sacet lohitakena cīvareṇa tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ baddhvodake prakṣipyet, tat svabhāvam eva tad udakaṃ bhavet, saced avadānakena cīvareṇa tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ baddhvodake prakṣipyet, tat svabhāvam eva tad udakaṃ bhavet, sacet māñjiṣṭhāvarṇena cīvareṇa tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ baddhvodake prakṣipyet, tat svabhāvam eva tad udakaṃ bhavet, sacet sphaṭikavarṇena cīvareṇa tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ baddhvodake prakṣipyet, tat svabhāvam eva tad udakaṃ bhavet, ebhiś ca nānāprakāraiś cīvarais tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ baddhvodake prakṣipyeta tat svabhāvam eva tad udakaṃ bhavet, yad api bhagavaṃs tatrodake kāluṣyante tan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ prasādayet, ebhir bhagavann evaṃrūpair guṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ (

children.translated_text: ) and many others as well. Just so, Blessed One, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is like a divine jewel — the source of all qualities, the liberator from all evil.

body.translated_text: If, Blessed One, that great jewel were wrapped in a blue cloth and cast into water, that water would remain in its natural state. If wrapped in a yellow cloth and cast into water, that water would remain in its natural state. If wrapped in a red cloth and cast into water, that water would remain in its natural state. If wrapped in a white cloth and cast into water, that water would remain in its natural state. If wrapped in a madder-colored cloth and cast into water, that water would remain in its natural state. If wrapped in a crystal-colored cloth and cast into water, that water would remain in its natural state. If that great jewel were wrapped in various kinds of cloths and cast into water, that water would remain in its natural state. And if, Blessed One, the water there becomes turbid, that great jewel would purify it. That great jewel, Blessed One, would be endowed with such qualities (

Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s> — is that great jewel a divine one, or does it exist among the human beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?

body.text: atha khalv āyuṣmān ānandaḥ śakraṃ devānām indram etad avocat: tat kiṃ manyase? kauśika divyam etan maṇiratnam utāho svij jāṃbudvīpakanāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ maṇiratnam asti.
śakra āha: divyam etad bhadanta maṇiratnam.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: It is a divine jewel, venerable sir.

body.text: api tu khalu punar bhadantānanda yāni jāṃbūdvīpakānāṃ mānuṣyāṇāṃ mahāmaṇiratnāny asti tāni parīttāni gurūṇi ca, yāni divyāni tāni mahānti laghūni ca tair aṅgais tāvat suparipūrṇāni jāṃbūdvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ maṇiratnāni yathā divyāni tāni punar jāṃbūdvīpakāni ratnāni teṣāṃ divyānāṃ maṇiratnānāṃ saṃkhyāṃ vā kalāṃ vā gaṇanāṃ vā upamāṃ vā upaniśāṃ vā nopayānti.
body.translated_text: However, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the great jewels that exist among the human beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are small and heavy, whereas the divine ones are large and light, and so well-endowed with their qualities. The jewels of the human beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> do not approach even a fraction, a hundredth, a calculation, an analogy, or an approximation of those divine jewels.

body.text: punar api śakro devānām indro bhagavantam etad avocat: tat khalu punar bhagavan mahāmaṇiratnaṃ yasmin karaṇḍake prakṣiptaṃ bhavet yadā kṣiptaṃ bhavet yadā kṣipataṃ ca tataḥ karaṇḍakāt spṛhaṇīyam eva tat karaṇḍakaṃ bhavet tair maṇiratnaguṇaiḥ paro 'pi tatra karaṇḍake spṛhom utpādayet, evam eva bhagavan yatreyaṃ prajñāpāramitā pracariṣyati, tatra teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ vā kuladuhitṝṇāṃ vā kāyikāś cetasikā vā duḥkhopadravā manuṣyakṛtā vā amanuṣyakṛtā vā na bhaviṣyati, mahāmaṇiratnam iti bhagavan prajñāpāramitām etad adhivacanaṃ sarvākārajñatājñānasyaitad adhivacanam.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: Indeed, Blessed One, that great jewel — in whatever casket it has been placed, once placed, that casket itself becomes desirable on account of the qualities of the jewel, and others too would generate desire for that casket. Just so, Blessed One, wherever this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will circulate, there those sons of good family or daughters of good family will not experience bodily or mental suffering or affliction, whether caused by humans or non-humans. 'Great jewel' — Blessed One, this is a designation for the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; this is a designation for the knowledge of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatājñāna</s>).

body.text: kiyanto bhagavañ chakyaṃ prajñāpāramitāyā guṇāḥ parikīrtayitum aprameyā hi prajñāpāramitāyā guṇāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāś ca tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi bhajanaṃ, kiyanto bhagavañ chakyaṃ dhyānapāramitāyā guṇāḥ parikīrtayitum aprameyā hi dhyānapāramitāyā guṇā dhyānapāramitāyāś ca tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi bhājanaṃ, kiyanto bhagavañ chakyaṃ vīryapāramitāyā guṇāḥ parikīrtayitum aprameyā hi vīryapāramitāyā guṇā vīryapāramitāyāś ca tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi bhājanaṃ, kiyanto bhagavañ chakyaṃ kṣāntipāramitāyā guṇāḥ parikīrtayitum aprameyā hi kṣāntipāramitāyā guṇāḥ kṣāntipāramitāyāś ca tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi bhajanaṃ, kiyanto bhagavañ chakyaṃ śīlapāramitāyā guṇāḥ parikīrtayitum aprameyā hi śīlapāramitāyā (

How much, Blessed One, is one able to proclaim the qualities of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>)? For the qualities of the perfection of giving are immeasurable, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics are the vessel of the perfection of giving.

For the qualities of the perfection of meditation are immeasurable, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics are the vessel of the perfection of meditation. children.translated_text: ) <s>Tathāgata</s> relics are vessels of the immeasurables. Blessed One, those <s>Tathāgata</s> bodily remains are the vessel of the perfection of non-casting-up and non-casting-down (<s>anutkṣepāprakṣepapāramitā</s>), and therefore those <s>Tathāgata</s> bodily remains receive worship. Blessed One, those <s>Tathāgata</s> bodily remains are the vessel of the perfection of neither coming, going, nor abiding (<s>anāgatyagatyasthitipāramitā</s>), and therefore those <s>Tathāgata</s> bodily remains receive worship.
