Furthermore, Blessed One, set aside the trichiliocosm bound up with bundles of <s>Tathāgata</s> bodily remains. If, Blessed One, the world-systems in the ten directions, equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were filled with bundles of <s>Tathāgata</s> bodily remains, and this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> written as a book were offered — between these two objects, Blessed One, I would take this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? For indeed, Blessed One, those <s>Tathāgata</s> bodily remains of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One have issued forth from this and are worshipped; those <s>Tathāgata</s> bodily remains pervaded by the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Blessed One, receive worship.

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhagavan tiṣṭhantu trisāhasramahāsāḥsro lokadhātus tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ pūrṇacūḍikāvabaddhāḥ, sacet bhagavan daśasu dikṣuḥ gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavas tathāgataśarīrāṇāṃ pūrṇacūḍikāvabaddhā bhaveyur yac ca prajñāpāramitāpustakaṃ likhitvopanāmyetaḥ, anayor ahaṃ bhagavan dvayoḥ pratyaṅgayor imām eva prajñāpāramitāṃ gṛhīyām. tat kasya hetoḥ? ato niryātāni hi bhagavan tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjyaṃte prajñāpāramitā paribhāvitani bhagavaṃs tāni tathāgataśarīrāṇi pūjāṃ labhante.

yaḥ punar bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgataśarīrāṇi satkuryād gurukuryād mānayet pūjayet sa tasya kuśalamūlasya paryantam adhigamya devamanuṣyasaṃpattīr anubhūya kṣatriyamahāśālakuleṣu brāhmaṇamahāśālakuleṣu gṛhapatimahāśālakuleṣu cāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu deveṣu yāmeṣu deveṣu tuṣiteṣu deveṣu nirmāṇaratiṣu deveṣu paranirmitavaśavartiṣu deveṣu sukham anubhūya tenaiva kuśalamūlena duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati, etāvat tathāgataśarīrapūjāyāḥ phalam imāṃ punaḥ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhan dhārayan vācayan paryavāpnuvan yoniśaś ca manasikurvan samādhipāramitāṃ ca paripūrayiṣyanti, vīryapāramitāṃ ca paripūrayiṣyanti, kṣāntipāramitāṃ ca paripūrayiṣyanti, śīlapāramitāṃ ca paripūrayiṣyanti, dānapāramitāṃ ca paripūrayiṣyanti.
body.translated_text: Moreover, Blessed One, whoever — a son or daughter of good family — were to honor, respect, esteem, and worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics, that person, reaching the limit of that root of merit, having experienced the prosperities of gods and humans — in the families of great <s>kṣatriya</s> households, in the families of great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> households, in the families of great householder households, among the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods — having experienced happiness, by that very root of merit will make an end of suffering. This is the fruit of worship of <s>Tathāgata</s> relics. But one who grasps, retains, recites, masters, and wisely attends to this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will fulfill the perfection of concentration (<s>samādhipāramitā</s>), will fulfill the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), will fulfill the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), will fulfill the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), and will fulfill the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>).

body.text: adhyātmaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, bahirdhāśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, śūnyatāśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, mahāśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, paramārthaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, saṃskṛtaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, asaṃskṛtaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, (

children.text: ) atyantaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, anavarāgraśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, anavakāraśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, prakṛtiśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, sarvadharmaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, svalakṣaṇaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, anupalambhaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, abhāvaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, svabhāvaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāṃ paripūrayiṣyati.
children.translated_text: ) will fulfill the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>).

body.translated_text: One will fulfill internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), will fulfill the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>) (

body.text: catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni paripūrayiṣyati, catvāri samyakprahāṇāni paripūrayiṣyati, catura ṛddhipādān paripūrayiṣyati, pañcendriyāṇi paripūrayiṣyati, pañca balāni paripūrayiṣyati, sapta bodhyaṅgāni paripūrayiṣyati, āryāṣṭāṅgamārgaṃ paripūrayiṣyati. catvāry āryasatyāni paripūrayiṣyati, catvāri dhyānāni paripūrayiṣyati, catvāry apramāṇāni paripūrayiṣyati, catasra ārūpyasamāpattiḥ paripūrayiṣyati, aṣṭau vimokṣān paripūrayiṣyati, navānupūrvavihārasamāpattīḥ paripūrayiṣyati, śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāni paripūrayiṣyati, pañcābhijñāḥ paripūrayiṣyati, samādhīn paripūrayiṣyati, dhāraṇīmukhāni paripūrayiṣyati, daśa tathāgatabalāni paripūrayiṣyati, catvāri vaiśāradyāni paripūrayiṣyati, catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ paripūrayiṣyati, mahāmaitrīṃ paripūrayiṣyati, mahākaruṇāṃ paripūrayiṣyati, aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmān paripūrayiṣyati.
body.translated_text: One will fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), will fulfill the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), will fulfill the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), will fulfill the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), will fulfill the five powers (<s>bala</s>), will fulfill the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), will fulfill the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), will fulfill the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), will fulfill the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), will fulfill the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), will fulfill the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), will fulfill the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), will fulfill the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), will fulfill the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), will fulfill the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), will fulfill the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), will fulfill the gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), will fulfill the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), will fulfill the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), will fulfill the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), will fulfill great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), will fulfill great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and will fulfill the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>).

body.text: śrāvakabhūmiṃ ca pratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ cātikramya bodhisattvaniyāmam avakramiṣyati, bodhisattvaniyāmam avakramya bodhisattvābhijñāḥ pratilapsyate, bodhisattvābhijñā pratilabhya buddhakṣetrād buddhakṣetraṃ saṃkramiṣyati, sa saṃcintyātmabhāvaṃ parigṛhīṣyati, yair ātmabhāvaḥ sattvaparipāko bhaviṣyati, yadi vā cakravartāśrayaṃ yadi vā kṣatriyamahāśālakuleṣu yadi vā brāhmaṇamahāśālakuleṣu yadi vā gṛhapatimahāśālakuleṣu yadi vā śakrarūpeṇa yadi vā brāhmaṇarūpeṇa yadi vā vaiśramaṇarūpeṇa sa tair ātmabhāvaiḥ sattvān paripācayiṣyati, tasmāt tarhi bhagavan na mama tathāgataśarīreṣv agauravaṃ nāpy apratyayā nāpy apūjayitukāmatā nāpy agrahītukāmatā.
body.translated_text: Having surpassed the level of a <s>śrāvaka</s> and the level of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, one will enter the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s certainty of attainment (<s>bodhisattvaniyāma</s>). Having entered the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s certainty of attainment, one will obtain the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s superknowledges (<s>bodhisattvābhijñā</s>). Having obtained the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s superknowledges, one will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field. One will intentionally take on forms of existence — whichever forms of existence will serve for the ripening of beings: whether the status of a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>), or in the families of great <s>kṣatriya</s> households, or in the families of great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> households, or in the families of great householder households, or in the form of <s>Śakra</s>, or in the form of <s>Brahmā</s>, or in the form of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. With those forms of existence, one will ripen beings. Therefore, Blessed One, it is not that I have no reverence for the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics, nor lack of faith, nor unwillingness to worship, nor unwillingness to take them up.

body.text: api tu khalu punar bhagavan kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ satkurvatā gurukurvatā mānayatā pūjayata sarvabuddhadharmāṇāṃ hetur upacito bhavati sarvasaṃpattayaś ca parigṛhītā bhavanti, tathāgataśarīrāṇi satkṛtā bhavanti gurukṛtāni bhavanti yāni tāni bhavanti pūjitāni bhavanti.
body.translated_text: But rather, Blessed One, a son or daughter of good family who honors, respects, esteems, and worships this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — by that the cause for all qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> is accumulated and all prosperities are embraced; the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics are honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped.

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhagavan ye daśasu dikṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā (

children.text: ) aprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhanti dhriyate yāpayanti dharmaṃ deśayanti tān dhharmakāyena ca jñānakāyena ca draṣṭukāmena pūjayitukāmena iyaṃ prajñāpāramitodgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pūjayitavyā parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyā yoniśaś ca manasikartavyā, sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu dikṣv aprameyāsakhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tāṃ tathāgatān arhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāṃ drakṣyati. evaṃ khalu tena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ ca tāṃ buddhān anusmṛtibhāvayitavyā dharmatayā.
children.translated_text: ) abide, endure, and dwell in innumerable and incalculable world-systems in the ten directions, teaching the Dharma — a son or daughter of good family who wishes to see and worship those <s>Tathāgata</s>s through their <s>dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body) and <s>jñānakāya</s> (knowledge-body) should take up, retain, recite, master, and worship this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and should explain it in detail to others and wisely attend to it. That son or daughter of good family will see those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones in the innumerable and incalculable world-systems of the ten directions. Thus indeed, that son or daughter of good family should cultivate the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>) through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and through the nature of dharmas (<s>dharmatā</s>).

body.translated_text: Furthermore, Blessed One, whatever <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones (

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhagavaṃs tāṃ tathāgatān arhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān saṃdraṣṭukāmena, kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā iyaṃ prajñāpāramitodgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā pravartayitavyā pūjayitavyā parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitavyā yoniśaś ca manasikartavyā, dharmatāyā dve ime bhagavan dharmatā.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, Blessed One, a son or daughter of good family who wishes to directly see those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones should take up, retain, recite, master, set in motion, and worship this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and should explain it in detail to others and wisely attend to it. Through the nature of dharmas (<s>dharmatā</s>) — Blessed One, there are two kinds of <s>dharmatā</s>.

body.text: katame dve saṃskṛtā ca dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā asaṃskṛtā ca dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā asaṃskṛtā ca dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā?
body.translated_text: What are the two? The conditioned nature of dharmas (<s>saṃskṛtā dharmatā</s>) and the unconditioned nature of dharmas (<s>asaṃskṛtā dharmatā</s>).

body.text: tatra bhagavan katamā saṃskṛtānāṃ dharmatā? yad adhyātmaśūnyatāyaṃ jñānaṃ yad bahirdhāśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatayāṃ jñānaṃ yad śūnyatāśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad mahāśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad paramārthaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad saṃskṛtaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad asaṃskṛtaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad atyantaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad anavarāgraśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad anavakāraśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad prakṛtiśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad sarvadharmaśūnyatayāṃ jñānaṃ yad svalakṣaṇaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad anupalambhaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad abhāvaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad svabhāvaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānaṃ yad abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāyāṃ jñānam.
body.translated_text: Therein, Blessed One, what is the nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of conditioned dharmas? The knowledge pertaining to internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), the knowledge pertaining to external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>),

body.text: yac caturṣu smṛtyupasthānāneṣu jñānaṃ, yac caturṣu samyakprahāṇāneṣu jñānaṃ, yac caturṣv ṛddhipādeṣu jñānaṃ, yat pañcasv indriyeṣu jñānaṃ, yat pañcasu baleṣu jñānaṃ, yat saptasu bodhyaṅgeṣu jñānaṃ, yad āryāṣṭāṅge marge jñānaṃ, yac caturṣv āryasatyeṣu jñānaṃ, yac caturṣu dhyāneṣu jñānaṃ, yac caturṣv apramāṇeṣu jñānaṃ, yac catasṛṣv ārūpyasamāpattiṣu jñānaṃ, yad aṣṭāsu vimokṣeṣu jñānaṃ, yan navānupūrvavihārasamāpattiṣu jñānaṃ, yañ chūnyatānimittāpraṇihiteṣu vimokṣamukheṣu jñānaṃ, yat pañcasv abhijñāsu jñānaṃ, yat sarvasamādhiṣu jñānaṃ, yat sarvadhāraṇīmukheṣu jñānaṃ, yad daśasu tathāgatabaleṣu jñānaṃ, yac (

children.text: ) caturṣu vaiśāradyeṣu jñānaṃ, yac catasṛṣu pratisaṃvitsu jñānaṃ, yan mahāmaitryāṃ jñānaṃ, yan mahākaruṇāyāṃ jñānaṃ, yad aṣṭādaśasv āveṇikeṣu buddhadharmeṣu jñānaṃ, yat kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu jñānaṃ, yad akuśaleṣu dharmeṣu jñānaṃ, yat sāśraveṣu dharmeṣu jñānaṃ, yad anāśraveṣu dharmeṣu jñānaṃ, yal laukikeṣu dharmeṣu jñānaṃ, yal lokottareṣu dharmeṣu jñānaṃ, iyam ucyate saṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā.
children.translated_text: ) the knowledge pertaining to the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the knowledge pertaining to the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the knowledge pertaining to great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), the knowledge pertaining to great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>),

body.translated_text: the knowledge pertaining to the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the knowledge pertaining to the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the knowledge pertaining to the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>),

body.text: tatra katamā asaṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā? yasyā notpādo na nirodho na sthānaṃ na sthito nānyathātvaṃ na saṃkleśo na vyavadānaṃ na hānir na vṛddhir yā sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvatā,
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the nature of unconditioned dharmas? That of which there is no arising, no cessation, no abiding, no standing, and no alteration —

body.text: katamā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvatā? abhāvasvabhāvā hi sarvadharmā iyam ucyate, asaṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā.
body.translated_text: And what is the inherent-nature-ness (<s>svabhāvatā</s>) of all dharmas? All dharmas are devoid of inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāva</s>) — this is called the nature of unconditioned dharmas.

body.text: bhagavān āha: evam etat kauśikaivam etat, ye 'pi te 'bhūvann atīte 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās te 'pīmām eva prajñāpāramitāṃ āgamyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhāḥ, ye 'pi te bhaviṣyanty anāgate 'dhvani tathāgatārhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās te 'pīmām eva prajñāpāramitām āgamyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante, ye 'pi te etarhi daśadig lokadhātuṣv aprameyeṣv asaṃkhyeyeṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās tiṣṭhanti dhhriyante yāpayanti dharmaṃ deśayanti, te 'pīmām eva prajñāpāramitāyām āgamyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyante, ye 'pi te 'bhūvann atītānāṃ tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ śrāvakāḥ, ye 'pi te bhaviṣyanty anāgatānāṃ tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ śrāvakāḥ, ye 'py etarhi pratyutpannānāṃ tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ śrāvakāḥ, te 'pīmām eva prajñāpāramitām āgamya srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpsyanti prāpnuvanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpsyanti prāpnuvanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpsyanti prāpnuvanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpsyanti prāpnuvanti ca, ye 'pi te 'bhūvann atite 'dhvani pratyekabuddhāḥ, ye 'pi te bhaviṣyanty anāgate 'dhvani pratyekabuddhā, ye 'pi te etarhi aprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu pratyekabuddhās tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti tair apīmām eva prajñāpāramitām āgamya pratyekabodhiḥ prāptāḥ prāpsyate prāpyate ca. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra prajñāpāramitāyā sarvāṇi trīṇi yānāni vistareṇopadiṣṭāni, tāni punar animittayogenānupalambhayogenānutpādayogenānirodhayogenāsasaṃkleśayogenāvyavadānayogenānabhisaṃskārayogenānāyūhayogenāniryuhayogenānukṣepayogenāprakṣepayogenānugrahayogenānutsargayogena (

children.text: ) tat punar lokavyavahāreṇa na paramārthena. tat kasya hetoḥ? na hi prajñāpāramitā āramitā na pāramitā na hi prajñāpāramitā apāro na pāraḥ, na sthalaṃ na nimnaṃ na samaṃ na viṣamaṃ na nimittaṃ nānimittaṃ na laukikī na lokottarā na saṃskṛtā nāsaṃskṛtā na kuśalā nākuśalā nātītā nānāgatā na pratyutpannā, na hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā buddhadharmānāṃ dātrī, na hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā srotaāpattidharmāṇāṃ dātrī, na hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā sakṛdāgāmidharmāṇāṃ dātrī, na hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā anāgāmidharmāṇāṃ dātrī, na hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā arhaddharmāṇāṃ dātrī na hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā pratyekabuddhadharmāṇāṃ dātrī, na hi kauśika prajñāpāramitā pṛthagjanadharmāṇāṃ dātrī.
children.translated_text: ) yet that is by way of worldly convention, not in the ultimate sense. For what reason? For indeed, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is neither a perfection nor a non-perfection.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. Those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones who existed in the past,
<s>Śakra</s> said: This is a great perfection (<s>mahāpāramitā</s>), Blessed One — namely, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: śakra āha: mahāpāramiteyaṃ bhagavan yad uta prajñāpāramitā, atra bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carantaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ cittacaritāni prajānanti na sattvam upalabhate na sattvaprajñaptim upalabhate nātmanam upalabhate na sattvam upalabhate na jīvam upalabhate na jantum upalabhate na poṣam upalabhate na puruṣam upalabhate na pudgalam upalabhate na manujam upalabhate na mānavam upalabhate na kārakam upalabhate na vedakam upalabhate na jānakam upalabhate na paśyakam upalabhate.
na rūpam upalabhate, na vedanām upalabhate, na saṃjñām upalabhate, na saṃskārām upalabhate, na vijñānam upalabhate.

body.text: na hi prajñāpāramitopalambhayogena pratyupasthitā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hi tasyāḥ svabhāvo na saṃvidyate yenopalabhet yad vopapalabhet yatra vopalabhet.
body.translated_text: For indeed, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not established through the method of apprehension (<s>upalambhayoga</s>). For what reason? For indeed, her own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is not found — neither by whom one might apprehend, nor what one might apprehend, nor where one might apprehend.

The Blessed One said: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. For indeed, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> through the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>) for a long time, does not even apprehend awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — how much less a <s>Buddha</s>, how much less the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: bhagavān āha: evam etat kauśikaivam etat, yathā hi tad dīrgharātrau bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nupalambhayogena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ sa bodhim api nopalabhhate prāg eva buddhaṃ prāg eva buddhadharmān.
śakra āha: punar bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati na tadanyāsu pāramitāsu.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: Furthermore, Blessed One, does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practice only in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and not in the other perfections?

body.text: bhagavān āha: sarvāsu kauśika ṣaḍpāramitāsu bodhisattvo mahāsattvaś carati tac cānupalambhayogena. sa dānam api nopalabhate dāyakam api nopalabhate pratigrāhakam api nopalabhate, śīlam api nopalabhate śīlavantam api nopalabhate dauḥśīlam api nopalabhate, kṣāntim api nopalabhate kṣamīnam api nopalabhate vyāpādam api nopalabhate, vīryam api nopalabhate vīryavantam api nopalabhate kauśīdyam api nopalabhate, dhyānam api nopalabhate dhyāyinam api nopalabhate vikṣepam api nopalabhate, prajñām api nopalabhate prajñāvantam api nopalabhate dauṣprajñam api nopalabhate.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, practices in all six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), and that through the method of non-apprehension. He does not apprehend giving, nor the giver, nor the recipient; he does not apprehend morality, nor the moral person, nor the immoral person; he does not apprehend patience, nor the patient person, nor ill-will; he does not apprehend vigor, nor the vigorous person, nor laziness; he does not apprehend meditation, nor the meditator, nor distraction; he does not apprehend wisdom, nor the wise person, nor poor wisdom.

Just so, <s>Kauśika</s>, when the five (

body.text: śakra āha: mahāguṇasamanvāgatā bhagavan prajñāpāramitā, sarvaguṇaparipūrikā, aprameyaguṇasamanvāgatā bhagavan prajñāpāramitā apramāṇaguṇasamanvāgatā aparyantaguṇasamanvagatā bhagavan prajñāpāramitā aparyavasānaguṇasamanvāgatayā tayā hi kaścid bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitvā pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā dhārayet tāś ca satkuryād gurukuryād mānayet pūjayet puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyair uttare ca yathopadiṣṭāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ yoniśo manasikuryād yo 'pi kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā parasmai dadyāt kataras tayor bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet?
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: The perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), Blessed One, is endowed with great qualities, is the fulfiller of all qualities, is endowed with immeasurable qualities, is endowed with measureless qualities, is endowed with boundless qualities, is endowed with unlimited qualities. Blessed One, if some son or daughter of good family, having written this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and made it into a book, were to retain it and honor, revere, respect, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music, and moreover were to wisely attend to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as instructed — and if another son or daughter of good family, having made this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> into a book, were to give it to another — which of those two would produce more merit?

body.text: bhagavān āha: tena hi kauśika tvām evātra paripakṣyāmi, yathā te kṣamate tathā vyākuru. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgataśarīrāṇi satkuryād gurukuryād mānayet pūjayet puṣpair mālyaiar gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vadyaiḥ, yaś ca kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā sarṣapaphalamātraṃ tathāgataśarīraṃ parasmai dadyāt saṃvibhāgaṃ kuryāt so 'pi kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā, tat sarṣapaphalamātraṃ tathāgataśarīraṃ gṛhītvā satkuyād gurukruyāt mānayet pūjayet puṣpair mālyaiar gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ, kataras tayor bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Well then, <s>Kauśika</s>, I shall question you about this very matter; answer as it seems right to you. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? If a son or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, respect, and worship the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music — and if another son or daughter of good family were to give to another even a mustard-seed-sized relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body and share it — and that other son or daughter of good family, having received that mustard-seed-sized relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, were to honor, revere, respect, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music — which of those two would produce more merit?

body.text: śakra āha: yathāhaṃ bhagavan bhagavatā bhāṣitasvārtham ājānāmi, yo yaṃ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgataśarīrāṇi satkuryād gurukuryād mānayet pūjayet puṣpair mālyaiar gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhavajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ, yo 'pi parasmai sarṣapaphalamātraṃ tathāgataśarīraṃ dadyād ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, imam eva bhagavann arthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyat, tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena vajropamaṃ samādhiḥ samāpadyaḥ vajropamam ātmabhāvaṃ bhittvā tathāgataśarīrāṇy adhiṣṭhitāni mahākaruṇāṃ saṃjanayya sattvakāye tathāgatadhātuvainayikānāṃ sattvānām. tat kasya hetoḥ? ye hi kecid bhagavan tathagatasyāntasaḥ sarṣapaphalamātraṃ dhātuṃ pūjayiṣyanti vividhābhiḥ pūjābhiḥ sarve te tasya kuśalamūlasya paryantam (

children.translated_text: ) will make an end of suffering.

body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: As I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has said, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, esteem, and worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments — if one were to give even a mustard-seed-sized <s>Tathāgata</s> relic to another, that person would produce even more merit. Seeing this very purpose, Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, having entered the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s> (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>) and having broken open the diamond-like physical body, blessed the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics, generating great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) for the body of beings — for those beings who are to be disciplined through <s>Tathāgata</s> relics. For what reason? For indeed, Blessed One, whoever will worship even a mustard-seed-sized relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s> with various forms of worship — all of them, having reached the end of that wholesome root (

body.text: bhagavān āha: evam etat kauśikaivam etat, yo hi kaścit kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā satkuryād gurukruyād mānayet pūjayet puṣpair mālyaiar gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyair yaś cemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ parasmai likhitvā dadyād dharmaprītyā ayaṃ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: So it is, <s>Kauśika</s>, so it is. For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, having made this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> into a book, were to honor, revere, esteem, and worship it with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments, and were to write this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and give it to another out of love for the Dharma — that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce even more merit.

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ yathopadiṣṭā parebhyo gatvā ācakṣīt deśayet saṃprakāśayet vicaret vibhajet uttānīkuryād ayaṃ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā teṣāṃ pūrvakānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāñ cāntikād bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, śāstaiva saṃpratikāṅkṣitavyānyatarānyatarīyā gurusthānīyā vijñāḥ sabrahmacārī. tat kasya hetoḥ? eṣa evātra kauśika śāstā yad uta prajñāpāramitā na hy anyaḥ śāstānyā prajñāpāramitā prajñāpāramitaiva śāstā śāstaiḥ prajñāpāramitā. tat kasya hetoḥ? atra hi prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣamāṇair atītānāgatapratyutpannais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbudhyate 'bhisaṃbhotsyate ca, ye 'pi te vijñāḥ sabrahmacāriṇas te 'pi nānye anyatrāvaivartikabodhisattvebhyo yatra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyate 'bhisaṃbhotsyate ca. atra hi kauśika prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śrāvakayānikā api śikṣitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikā api śikṣitvā pratyekabodhin abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃvuddhyate abhisaṃbhotsyate ca, bodhisattvā api mahāsattvāḥ śikṣitvā bodhisattvaniyamam avakrāntā avakrāmanti avakrāmiṣyanti ca, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbuddhānte abhisaṃbhotsyante ca.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family were to explain this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as instructed to others, were to teach it, illuminate it, practice it, analyze it, and make it clear — that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce even more merit than those earlier sons of good family or daughters of good family. That person is to be regarded as equivalent to the Teacher himself, or as one or another of those who stand in the place of a teacher — wise fellow practitioners of the holy life. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, the Teacher here is none other than the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; there is no other teacher apart from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself is the Teacher, and the Teacher is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? For indeed, training here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past, present, and future have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. And those wise fellow practitioners of the holy life are none other than irreversible <s>bodhisattva</s>s (<s>avaivartika</s>), who, having trained in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, training here in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, even those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), have attained, do attain, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhattva</s>). And even those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, having trained, have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>). And <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s too, having trained, have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s> (<s>bodhisattvaniyāma</s>), and have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening.

children.text: ) mālyaiar gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyair imaṃ cārthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasyaitad abhūt, katamad ahaṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśrāya vihareyaṃ so 'haṃ kauśika sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake saśravaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ sadevamānuṣāsurāyām ātmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ cādhikaṃ vā na samanupaśyāmi, tasya mamaitad abhūd, ya nv eva mayā dharmābhisaṃbuddhaḥ śāntaḥ praṇītas tam eva dharmaṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśrāya vihareyaṃ katamaś cāsau kauśika dharmā yad uta saiva prajñāpāramitā aham eva tāvat kauśikemāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ satkaromi gurukaromi mānayāmi pūjayāmi satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśrāya viharāmi, kim aṅga punaḥ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbodhukāmeneyaṃ prajñāpāramitā na satkartavyā na gurukartavyā na mānayitavyā na pūjayitavyā puṣpair mālyaiar gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ, śrāvakayānikair vā kauśika kulaputrair vā kuladuhitṛbhir vā pratyekabudhayānikair api kulaputrair vā kuladuhitṛbhir vā iyam eva prajñāpāramitā satkartavyā gurukartavyā mānayitavyā pūjayitavyā puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhavajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? prajñāpāramitā niryātā hi bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bodhisattvaniryātāś ca tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tathāgataniryātāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhās tasmāt tarhi kauśika bodhisattvayānikaiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhir vā śrāvakayānikaiś ca pratyekabuddhayanikaiś ca kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhir vā iyam eva prajñāpāramitā satkartavyā gurukartavyā mānayitavyā pūjayitavyā puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhavajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ. yatra śikṣitvā kulaputrā kuladuhitaraś cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbuddhyante 'bhisaṃbhotsyante ca śrāvakayānikāś cārhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca pratyekabuddhayānīkāś ca pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca.
children.translated_text: ) garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments. And seeing this purpose, having fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening, this thought arose: 'Whom shall I honor, revere, esteem, worship, and rely upon to dwell?' And I, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the world with its gods, <s>Māra</s>s, <s>Brahmā</s>s, among the populace with its ascetics and brahmins, and among gods, humans, and <s>asura</s>s, do not see anyone equal to or surpassing myself. This thought then arose in me: 'I should honor, revere, esteem, worship, and rely upon the very Dharma to which I have fully awakened — peaceful and sublime.' And what is that Dharma, <s>Kauśika</s>? It is none other than the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself. I myself, <s>Kauśika</s>, honor, revere, esteem, and worship this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped it, rely upon it to dwell. How then, <s>Kauśika</s>, should a son of good family or daughter of good family who wishes to fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening not honor, revere, esteem, and worship this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments? And, <s>Kauśika</s>, even by sons of good family or daughters of good family of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, and by sons of good family or daughters of good family of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments. For what reason? For <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have issued forth from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones have issued forth from <s>bodhisattva</s>s, and <s>śrāvaka</s>s and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s have issued forth from <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, by sons of good family and daughters of good family of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle, by those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, and by those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, streamers, and various musical instruments — this in which, having trained, sons of good family and daughters of good family have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening; and those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship; and those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>).

body.text: śatasāhasryāḥ prajñāpāramitayā dvāviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: The twenty-second chapter of the <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavāñ chakraṃ devānām indram āmantrayeta: sacet kauśika jāmbūdvīpakān sattvān kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānāṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: If, <s>Kauśika</s>, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśa kuśala karmapatha</s>), what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s> — would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on account of that?

body.text: śakra āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>.

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ parasmai dadyāt paṭhanāya vā likhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? atra hi prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭā yatra śikṣitvā kulaputrā kuladuhitaraś ca samyaktvanyāmam avakrāntāś cāvakramanti ca avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāś ca prāpnuvanti ca prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāś ca prāpnuvanti ca prāpsyanti ca, anagāmiphalaṃ prāptāś ca prāpnuvanti ca prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāś ca prāpnuvanti ca prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāś ca prāpnuvanti ca prāpsyanti ca, anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiṃ saṃprasthitā samyaktvanyāmam avakrāntāś cāvakramanti cāvakramiṣyanti ca, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante 'bhisaṃbhotsyante.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: More than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would the son of good family or daughter of good family produce merit who gives a book of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to another for reading, writing, or recitation. For what reason? For indeed, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the outflow-free dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) are taught in detail — training in which, sons of good family and daughters of good family have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the correct (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhattva</s>); those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); those who have set out for unsurpassed perfect complete awakening have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the correct; and have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening.

body.text: katame ca te kauśika sāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭāḥ? yad uta catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni catvāri samyakprahāṇāni catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ pañcendriyāṇi pañca balāni sapta bodhyaṅgāni āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaś catvāry āryasatyāni.
body.translated_text: And what are those outflow-free dharmas taught in detail, <s>Kauśika</s>? Namely: the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), and the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>).

body.text: adhyātmaśūnyatā, bahirdhāśūnyatā, adhyatmabahirdhāśūnyatā, śūnyatāśūnyatā, mahāśūnyatā, paramārthaśūnyatā, saṃskṛtaśūnyatā, asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā, atyantaśūnyatā, anavarāgraśūnyatā, anavakāraśūnyatā, prakṛtiśūnyatā, sarvadharmaśūnyatā, svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā, anupalambhaśūnyatā, abhāvaśūnyatā, svabhāvaśūnyatā, abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: aṣṭau vimokṣā navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayo daśatathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvido mahākaruṇā aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmaḥ,
body.translated_text: The eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>).

body.text: ime te kauśika anāsravā dharmā ye prajñāpāramitayā nirdiṣṭā yatra śikṣitvā kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhāś cābhisaṃbudhyante cābhisaṃbhotsyante ca, evaṃ kauśikaikaṃ sattvaṃ srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpya kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā (

children.text: ) bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, na tv eva jāmbūdvīpakān sattvān daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpya. tat kasya hetoḥ? daśasu kauśika kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ sattvā aparimuktā evaṃ narakatiryagyoner yamalokān srotaāpattiphale kauśika sattvaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ parimukto narakatiryagyoner yamalokān, kaḥ punar vādaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphale anāgāmiphale 'rhattve pratiṣṭhāpayet, yaś ca punaḥ kauśika sarvajāmbūdvīpakān sattvān srotaāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayed anāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayed arhattve pratiṣṭhāpayet, yaś caikaṃ sattvaṃ pratyekabodhau pratiṣṭhāpayed ayam eva bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, yo vā kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā sarvajāmbūdvīpakān pratyekabodhau pratiṣṭhāpayed yaś ca kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā ekam api sattvam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayed ayam eva bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. tat kasya hetoḥ? buddhanetryāḥ so vyavacchedāya pratipanno bhavati, ya ekasattvam apy anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pratiṣṭhāpayati. tat kasya hetoḥ? bodhisattvanirjātā hi kauśika srotaāpannāḥ sakṛdāgāmino 'nāgāmino 'rhantaḥ pratyekabuddhā bodhisattvaniryātā hi kauśika tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhās tad anena kauśika paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam. bodhisattvo 'pi pūjayitavyo mānayitavyaḥ satkartavyo gurukartavyaḥ puṣpair dhūpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyaiḥ, sa devakena lokena samārakena saśravaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajñāyāḥ, yo hi kaścit kauśika kulaputro vā kuladhitā vā jāmbūdvīpakān sattvān daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.
children.translated_text: ) would produce more merit — but not by establishing the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the ten wholesome courses of action. For what reason? <s>Kauśika</s>, beings established in the ten wholesome courses of action are not freed from the hells, animal births, or the world of <s>Yama</s>. But a being established in the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), <s>Kauśika</s>, is freed from the hells, animal births, and the world of <s>Yama</s> — how much more so one established in the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), or <s>arhat</s>ship. And further, <s>Kauśika</s>, if someone were to establish all the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the fruit of stream-entry, in the fruit of once-returning, in the fruit of non-returning, and in <s>arhat</s>ship — yet one who establishes even a single being in solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>) would produce more merit. And if any son or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in solitary awakening — yet any son or daughter of good family who establishes even a single being in unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) would produce more merit. For what reason? That one who establishes even a single being in unsurpassed perfect awakening is one who has set out for the non-interruption of the lineage of <s>Buddha</s>s (<s>buddhanetrī</s>). For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, <s>arhat</s>s, and <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s have arisen from <s>bodhisattva</s>s; <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Arhat</s>s, Perfectly Awakened Ones have arisen from <s>bodhisattva</s>s. Therefore, <s>Kauśika</s>, by this method it should be understood: a <s>bodhisattva</s> too is to be worshipped, honored, respected, and revered with flowers, incense, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, pennants, and various kinds of music — by the world with its gods, <s>Māra</s>s, and <s>Brahmā</s>s, and the generation of ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s. Now, <s>Kauśika</s>, if any son or daughter of good family were to establish the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the ten wholesome courses of action — what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account?

body.translated_text: These, <s>Kauśika</s>, are the outflow-free dharmas taught in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — training in which, sons of good family and daughters of good family have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening. body.text: katame ca te kauśikānāsravā dharmās tad yathā dānapāramitā śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramita dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: And what, <s>Kauśika</s>, are those undefiled dharmas? body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ parasmai dadyāt, paṭhanāya vā Iekhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭā yatra kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś caśikṣitvā samyaktvanyāmam avakrānto avakramanty avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvā bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyate abhisaṃbhotsyate ca.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: More merit than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family produce who would give to another a copy of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — for reading, for writing, or for reciting. For what reason? For indeed, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the undefiled dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) are taught in detail, and sons and daughters of good family, having trained therein, have descended, do descend, and will descend into the certainty of the correct path (<s>samyaktvanyāma</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship; those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); and <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have descended, do descend, and will descend into the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s certainty of attainment (<s>bodhisattvaniyāma</s>); and have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.translated_text: He said: A great deal, Blessed One! A great deal, <s>Sugata</s>!

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ parasmai dadyāt, paṭhanāya vā lekhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭā yatra kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca śikṣitvā samyaktvanyāmam avakrāntā, avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvā bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyate abhisaṃbhotsyate ca.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: That son or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce a far greater heap of merit who gives this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as a book to another for reading, writing, or recitation. For what reason? For indeed, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the undefiled dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) have been taught in detail, wherein sons and daughters of good family, having trained, have entered, are entering, and will enter the certainty of the right way (<s>samyaktvanyāma</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship; those inclined toward the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, are attaining, and will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); and <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have entered, are entering, and will enter the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s certainty of attainment (<s>bodhisattvaniyāma</s>); have awakened, are awakening, and will awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.translated_text: What are those undefiled dharmas, <s>Kauśika</s>? Namely: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>), and other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> have been taught in detail. By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, it should be understood thus: whatever son or daughter of good family were to give the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having written it as a book, to others for reading, writing, or recitation — that one would produce a far greater heap of merit. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all dharmas have been taught in detail — through which great <s>kṣatriya</s> families become known, great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families become known, and great householder families become known.

However many beings there are in the middle dichiliocosm, <s>Kauśika</s> — if all those beings were each to construct <s>stūpa</s>s of the seven precious substances for the <s>Tathāgata</s> after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and worship them for as long as they live with divine flowers, divine garlands, divine fragrances, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine flags, and divine music — what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Set aside the beings in the middle dichiliocosm, <s>Kauśika</s>. However many beings there are in the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>), <s>Kauśika</s> — if all those beings were each to construct <s>stūpa</s>s of the seven precious substances for the <s>Tathāgata</s> after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and worship them — what do you think? Would they produce much merit from that?

body.text: tiṣṭhantu kauśika dvisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvās tān kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.

<s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son or daughter of good family were to establish in the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>kuśala karmapatha</s>) all the beings in the world-systems of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in each direction. What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son or daughter of good family produce much merit from that?

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: That son or daughter of good family would produce even more merit who gives the book of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to another — whether for reading, for copying, or for reciting. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> the undefiled dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) have been taught in detail, and sons and daughters of good family, having trained in them, have entered, are entering, and will enter the certainty of the right course (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhattva</s>); those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, are attaining, and will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have entered, are entering, and will enter the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s> course (

body.translated_text: And what are those undefiled dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>), <s>Kauśika</s>? They are as follows: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni, catvāri samyakprahāṇāni, catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ, pañcendriyāṇi, pañca balāni, sapta bodhyaṅgāny āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaś catvāry āryasatyāny aṣṭau vimokṣā navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāni pañcābhijñāḥ sarvasamādhayaḥ sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni daśatathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvido 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ, mahāmaitrī mahākaruṇā mahāmuditā mahopekṣā anye cāparimāṇā buddhadharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭāḥ. tad anenāpi te kauśika paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyaṃ, yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā parebhyo dadyāt paṭhanāyāpi lekhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi, ayam eva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vistareṇa sarvadharmā upadiṣṭā yaiḥ kṣatriyamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, brāhmaṇamahāśalakulāni prajñāyante, gṛhapatimahāśalakulāni prajñāyante.
body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>), and other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> have been taught in detail. By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, it should be understood that a son or daughter of good family who, having written the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as a book, gives it to others — whether for reading, for copying, or for reciting — that person would produce far more merit. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> all dharmas have been taught in detail, through which the great families of the <s>kṣatriya</s>s are known, the great families of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s are known, and the great families of the householders are known.

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ parasmai dadyāt, paṭhanāya vā lekhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭā yatra kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca śikṣitvā samyaktvanyāmam avakrānto avakramanty avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvā bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyate abhisaṃbhotsyate ca.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: More than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would the son of good family or daughter of good family produce merit who gives a book of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to another for reading, writing, or recitation. For what reason? For indeed, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the outflow-free dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) are taught in detail — training in which, sons of good family and daughters of good family have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the correct (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhattva</s>); those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); and <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; and have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening.

body.text: katame ca te kauśikānāsravā dharmās tad yathā dānapāramitā, śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: And what are those outflow-free dharmas, <s>Kauśika</s>? body.text: tiṣṭhantu kauśika cāturmahādvīpake lokadhātau sattvāḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika sāhasre lokadhātau sattvās tān kaścid eva kulaputro yā kuladuhitā vā caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec caturṣv apramāṇeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec catasṛṣv ārūpyasamāpttiṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet pañcasv abhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: Setting aside the beings in a world-system of four great continents, <s>Kauśika</s> — as many beings as there are in a thousandfold world-system, if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish them in the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), establish them in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), establish them in the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and establish them in the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) — what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account?

body.text: āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata.
body.translated_text: He said: Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>.

Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the beings of the thousand-fold world-system. <s>Kauśika</s>, if some son or daughter of good family were to establish all the beings in the two-thousand-fold world-system (<s>dvisāhasra lokadhātu</s>) in the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), in the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and in the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) — what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account?

body.text: tiṣṭhantu kauśika sāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ yāvantaḥ kauśika dvisāhasre lokadhātau sattvās tān kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladtihitā vā caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec caturḥv apramāṇeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec catasṛṣv ārūpyasamāpttiṣu pratiṣṭhapayet pañcasv abhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.
āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata.
body.translated_text: He said: Much, Blessed One! Much, <s>Sugata</s>!

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ likhitvā parebhyo dadyāt, paṭhanāya vā lekhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭāḥ, yatra kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca śikṣitvā samyaktvanyāmam avakrāntā, avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvā bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante abhisaṃbhotsyante ca.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: More merit than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son or daughter of good family produce who would write a copy of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and give it to others — for reading, for writing, or for reciting. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> the undefiled dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) are taught in detail, and sons and daughters of good family, having trained therein, have descended, do descend, and will descend into the certainty of the correct path (<s>samyaktvanyāma</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship; those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); and <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have descended, do descend, and will descend into the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s certainty of attainment (<s>bodhisattvaniyāma</s>); and have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: katame te kauśikānāsravā dharmās tad yathā dānapāramitā, śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyanapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: And what, <s>Kauśika</s>, are those undefiled dharmas? They are: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

Set aside the dichiliocosm, <s>Kauśika</s>. However many beings there are in the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>), <s>Kauśika</s> — if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish them in the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), establish them in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), establish them in the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and establish them in the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) — what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit from that?

body.text: tiṣṭhantu kauśika dvisāhasre lokadhātau sattvā yāvantaḥ kauśika trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvās tān kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec caturṣv apramāṇeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec catasṛṣv ārūpyasamāpttiṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet pañcasv abhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.
āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata.
body.translated_text: He said: Much, Blessed One! Much, <s>Sugata</s>!

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ parasmai dadyāt, paṭhanāya vā lekhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭāḥ, yatra kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca śikṣitvā samyaktvanyāmam avakrāntā, avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca. sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, (

children.text: ) anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvā bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante abhisaṃbhotsyante ca.
children.translated_text: have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship; those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, are attaining, and will attain <s>pratyekabodhi</s>; and <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have entered, are entering, and will enter the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s> (<s>bodhisattvanyāma</s>); have fully awakened, are fully awakening, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce even more merit — one who would give a book of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to another for reading, writing, or recitation. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> the uncontaminated dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) have been taught in detail, wherein sons of good family and daughters of good family, having trained, have entered, are entering, and will enter the certainty of the correct way (<s>samyaktvanyāma</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>);

body.text: katame ca te kauśikānāsravā dharmās tad yathā dānapāramitā, śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: And what are those uncontaminated dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>), <s>Kauśika</s>? Namely: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.translated_text: Internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), internal-and-external emptiness (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the beginningless and endless (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of all dharmas (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and the emptiness of non-existence and inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni, catvāri samyakprahāṇāni, catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ, pañcendriyāṇi, pañca balāni, sapta bodhyaṅgāny āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaś catvāry āryasatyāny aṣṭau vimokṣā navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāni sarvasamādhayaḥ sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni daśatathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvido 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmāḥ, mahāmaitrī mahākaruṇā mahāmuditā mahopekṣāḥ, anye cāparimāṇā buddhadharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭāḥ. tad anenāpi te kauśika paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam. yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prajñāpāramitāṃ likhitāṃ kṛtvā parebhyo dadyāt paṭhanāyāpi lekhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi, ayam eva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vistareṇa sarvadharmā upadiṣṭā yaiḥ kṣatriyamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, brāhmaṇamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, gṛhapatimahāśālakulāni prajñāyante.
body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>), and other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> have been taught in detail. By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, it should be understood thus: whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, having written the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as a book, were to give it to others for reading, writing, or recitation — that one would produce even more merit. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> all dharmas have been taught in detail, through which great <s>kṣatriya</s> families become known, great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families become known, and great householder families become known.

body.text: yāvantaḥ kauśika pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvās tān kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec caturṣv apramāṇeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec catasṛṣv ārūpyasamāpttiṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet pañcasv abhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: However many beings there are in the eastern direction, <s>Kauśika</s>, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> — if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish them in the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), establish them in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), establish them in the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and establish them in the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) — what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit from that?

body.text: āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata.
body.translated_text: He said: Much, Blessed One! Much, <s>Sugata</s>!

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ likhitāṃ kṛtvā parasmai dadyāt, paṭhanāya vā lekhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭā yatra kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca śikṣitvā samyaktvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvā bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante abhisaṃbhotsyante ca.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce even more merit — one who, having written this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as a book, would give it to another for reading, writing, or recitation. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> the uncontaminated dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) have been taught in detail, wherein sons of good family and daughters of good family, having trained, have entered, are entering, and will enter the certainty of the correct way (<s>samyaktvanyāma</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, are attaining, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship; those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, are attaining, and will attain <s>pratyekabodhi</s>; and <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have entered, are entering, and will enter the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s> (<s>bodhisattvanyāma</s>); have fully awakened, are fully awakening, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: katame ca te kauśikānāsravā dharmās tad yathā dānapāramitā, śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: And what are those uncontaminated dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>), <s>Kauśika</s>? Namely: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

children.text: ) vā prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā parebhyo dadyāt paṭhanāyāpi lekhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi, ayam eva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vistareṇa sarvadharmā upadiṣṭā yaiḥ kṣatriyamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, brāhmaṇamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, gṛhapatimahāśālakulāṅi prajñāyante.

body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>), and other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> have been taught in detail. body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce even more merit — one who would give a book of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to another for reading, writing, or recitation. For what reason?
