body.text: catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni, catvāri samyakprahāṇāni, catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ, pañcendriyāṇi, pañca balāni, sapta bodhyaṅgāny āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaś catvāry āryasatyāny aṣṭau vimokṣā navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukhāni ṣaḍ abhijñāḥ sarvasamādhayaḥ sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni daśatathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catasraḥ pratisaṃvido 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ, mahāmaitri mahākaruṇā mahāmuditā mahopekṣā anye cāparimāṇā buddhadharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭāḥ. tad anenāpi te kauśika paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyaṃ, yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prajñāpāramitāṃ pustakalikhitāṃ kṛtvā parebhyo dadyāt paṭhanāyāpi lekhanāyāpi vācanāyāpi, ayam eva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vistareṇa sarvadharmā upadiṣṭā yaiḥ kṣatriyamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, brāhmaṇamahāśālakulāni prajñāyante, gṛhapatimahāśālakulāni prajñāyante.
body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>), and other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> have been taught in detail. By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, it should be understood thus: whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, having written the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as a book, were to give it to others for reading, writing, or recitation — that very one would produce even more merit. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> all dharmas have been taught in detail, through which great <s>kṣatriya</s> families become known, great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families become known, and great householder families become known.

body.text: ) dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec caturṣv apramāṇeṣu catasṛṣv ārūpyasamāpattiṣu pañcasv abhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: ) meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), establish them in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) — what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account?

body.text: āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata.
body.translated_text: He said: Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>.

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ parasmai dadyāt, paṭhanāya vā lekhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭā yatra kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca śikṣitvā samyaktvanyāmam avakrāntā, avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvā bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante abhisaṃbhotsyante ca.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: More than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would the son of good family or daughter of good family produce merit who gives a book of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to another for reading, writing, or recitation. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> the outflow-free dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>) are taught in detail — training in which, sons of good family and daughters of good family have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the correct (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); have attained, do attain, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship (<s>arhattva</s>); those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); and <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; and have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening.

body.text: katame te kauśikānāsravā dharmās tad yathā dānapāramitā, śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: What are those outflow-free dharmas, <s>Kauśika</s>? Namely: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: yāvantaḥ kauśika dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvās tān kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayec caturṣv apramāṇeṣu catasṛṣv ārūpyasamāpattiṣu pañcasv abhijñāsu pratiṣṭhapayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: As many beings as there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the southwestern direction — if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish them in the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), establish them in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) — what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>, would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account?

body.text: āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata.
body.translated_text: He said: Much, Blessed One; much, <s>Sugata</s>.

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. yo 'syāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ pustakaṃ parasmai dadyāt, paṭhanāya vā lekhanāya vā vācanāya vā. tat kasya hetoḥ? tathā hy atra kauśika prajñāpāramitāyām anāsravā dharmā vistareṇopadiṣṭā yatra kulaputraḥ kuladuhitaraś ca śikṣitvā samyaktvanyāmam avakrāntā, avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti ca, srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, arhattvaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, pratyekabuddhayānikāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanti prāpsyanti ca, bodhisattvāś ca mahāsattvā bodhisattvanyāmam avakrāntā avakrāmanty avakramiṣyanti, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante abhisaṃbhotsyante ca.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: More than that, <s>Kauśika</s>, would the son of good family or daughter of good family produce merit who gives a book of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to another for reading, writing, or recitation. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> the outflow-free dharmas are taught in detail — training in which, sons of good family and daughters of good family have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the correct; have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry; have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of once-returning; have attained, do attain, and will attain the fruit of non-returning; have attained, do attain, and will attain <s>arhat</s>ship; those of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle have attained, do attain, and will attain solitary awakening; and <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>s have entered, do enter, and will enter the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; and have fully awakened, do fully awaken, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening.

body.text: katame te kauśikānāsravā dharmās tad yathā dānapāramitā, śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā.
body.translated_text: What are those outflow-free dharmas, <s>Kauśika</s>? Namely: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>), and other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> are taught in detail. By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, it should be understood thus: whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, having written the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as a book, would give it to others for reading, writing, or recitation — that very one would produce more merit. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> all dharmas are taught in detail, through which great <s>Kṣatriya</s> families become known, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> families become known, great householder families become known.

However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in the world-systems in the northwestern direction, as numerous as the grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> — if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish them in the four meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), what do you think, <s>Kauśika</s> — would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on account of that?

āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata.

body.translated_text: And what are those uncontaminated dharmas (<s>anāsrava dharma</s>), <s>Kauśika</s>? body.translated_text: The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gateways of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), all concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), all gateways of retention (<s>dhāraṇīmukha</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the eighteen exclusive qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), great sympathetic joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>), great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>), and other immeasurable qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> have been taught in detail. By this method too, <s>Kauśika</s>, it should be understood thus: whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, having written the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as a book, were to give it to others for reading, writing, or recitation — that one would produce even more merit. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> all dharmas have been taught in detail, through which great <s>kṣatriya</s> families become known, great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families become known, and great householder families become known.

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika yo hi kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anena paryāyeṇa prajñāpāramitāṃ parebhyo vistareṇākhyāsyati deśayiṣyati prakāśayiṣyati prabhāvayiṣyati vivariṣyati vibhajiṣyaty uttarīkariṣyati, saṃprakāśayiṣyaty arthaṃ cāsya upadekṣyati, tatrāyaṃ kauśika prajñāpāramitāyā arthaḥ, na prajñāpāramitādvayeṇa draṣṭavyā na dvayena na nimittato nāyuhato nāniryūhataḥ, notkṣepato na prakṣepataḥ, na saṃkreśato na vyavadānato notpādato na nirodhataḥ, na grahato nāgrahato nodgrahato notsargato na sthānato nāsthānato na bhūtato nābhūtataḥ, na yogato nāyogato na śleṣmato nāśleṣmato na pratyayato nāpratyayato na dharmato nādharmataḥ, na tathāgatato nātathāgatato na bhūtakoṭīto nābhūtakoṭītaḥ. ayam eva sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family would, by this method, explain the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to others in detail, teach it, illuminate it, make it shine forth, open it up, analyze it, make it clear, fully illuminate it, and point out its meaning — herein, <s>Kauśika</s>, this is the meaning of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not be seen through non-duality, nor through duality, nor from the standpoint of signs, nor from the standpoint of reasoning, nor from the standpoint of analysis, nor from the standpoint of casting up nor casting down, nor from the standpoint of defilement nor purification, nor from the standpoint of arising nor cessation, nor from the standpoint of grasping nor non-grasping, nor of taking up nor letting go, nor of abiding nor non-abiding, nor of the real nor the unreal, nor of conjunction nor non-conjunction, nor of adhesion nor non-adhesion, nor of conditions nor non-conditions, nor of dharma nor non-dharma, nor from the standpoint of the <s>Tathāgata</s> nor the non-<s>Tathāgata</s>, nor from the standpoint of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) nor the non-limit of reality. That very son of good family or daughter of good family would produce even more merit.

body.text: ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ parebhyo vistareṇākhyāsyati deśayiṣyati prakāśayiṣyati vicariṣyati bhajiṣyati, utttānīkariṣyati saṃprakāśayiṣyati, eyaṃ cāsya upadekṣyati, na tv eva ya ātmanaikopagṛhīyāt paryavāpnuyād ādhārayed dhārayed vācayed yoniśaś ca manasikuryāt.
body.translated_text: One who would explain this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to others in detail, teach it, illuminate it, practice it, and cultivate it, make it clear and fully illuminate it, and point out its meaning — but not one who would merely take it up for oneself alone, master it, hold it, retain it, recite it, and attend to it wisely.

Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family would personally take up the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, master it, and attend to it wisely, and would also explain it to others in detail, teach it, illuminate it, make it known, establish it, practice it, cultivate it, make it clear, and fully illuminate it, and would point out its meaning — that very son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, would produce even more merit.

body.text: punar aparaṃ kauśika yaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā svayaṃ prajñāpāramitām udgṛhīṣyati paryavāpsyati yoniśaś ca manasikariṣyati tāṃ ca parasmai vistareṇākhyāsyati deśayiṣyati prakāśayiṣyati prajñāpayiṣyati sthāpayiṣyati vicariṣyati bhajiṣyati, utttanīkariṣyati saṃprakāśayiṣyati. arthaṃ cāsya upadekṣyaty ayam eva sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasaviṣyati.
śakra āha: evaṃ khalu bhagavan kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā prajñāpāramitopadiṣṭavyā, sārthā savyañjanā.
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: Indeed so, Blessed One! The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be taught by a son of good family or daughter of good family — with its meaning and with its letter.

body.text: bhagavān āha: evaṃ khlu kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā parebhyaḥ prajñāpāramitopadeṣṭavyā sārthā savyañjanā. evam upadiśan punaḥ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāparimāmānena puṇyaskandhena samanvāgato bhaviṣyati.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Indeed so, <s>Kauśika</s>! The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be taught by a son of good family or daughter of good family to others — with its meaning and with its letter. Teaching thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family will be endowed with an immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless heap of merit.

body.text: sacet kauśika kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pūrvasyāṃ diśy aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāṃ tathāgatān arhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān yāvaj jīvaṃ sarvasukhopadhānena satkuryān mānayet pūjayet puṣpair mālyair gandhair vilepanaiś cūrṇaiś cīvaraiś chattrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhir vividhaiś ca vādyair yaś ca khalu punaḥ kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vemāṃ prajñāpāramitām anekaparyāyeṇa parasmai vistareṇa sārthaṃ savyañjanam ācakṣīd deśayet prakāśayed vicared vibhajed uttānīkuryāt prakāśayed ayam eva sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet. tat kasya hetoḥ? atra hi prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitvā atītānāgatapratyutpannais tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhair anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbuddhyate 'bhisaṃbhotsyante ca.
body.translated_text: If, <s>Kauśika</s>, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, respect, and worship immeasurable and incalculable <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>arhat</s>s, perfectly and fully awakened ones in the eastern direction for as long as they live, with the provision of every comfort, with flowers, garlands, fragrances, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of music — and if, on the other hand, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family were to explain this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to another in detail by many methods, with meaning and with letter, teaching, illuminating, practicing, analyzing, making clear, and fully illuminating it — that very son of good family or daughter of good family would produce even more merit. For what reason? For by training in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>arhat</s>s, perfectly and fully awakened ones of the past, future, and present have fully awakened, are fully awakening, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect complete awakening.

body.text: evaṃ khalu kauśikopalambhacaritasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā na dānapāramitā paripūryate na śīlapāramitā paripūryate na kṣāntipāramitā paripūryate na vīryapāramitā paripūryate na dhyānapāramitā paripūryate na prajñāpāramitā paripūryate.
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, <s>Kauśika</s>, for a son of good family or daughter of good family who practices through apprehension, the perfection of giving is not fulfilled, the perfection of morality is not fulfilled, the perfection of patience is not fulfilled, the perfection of vigor is not fulfilled, the perfection of meditation is not fulfilled, the perfection of wisdom is not fulfilled.

body.text: śakra āha: kathaṃ carato bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dānapāramitā paripūryate? kathaṃ carato bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya śīlapāramitā paripūryate? kathaṃ carato bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kṣāntipāramitā paripūryate? kathaṃ carato bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya vīryapāramitā paripūryate? kathaṃ carato bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dhyānapāramitā paripūryate? kathaṃ carato bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitā paripūryate?
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: How, Blessed One, does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s perfection of giving become fulfilled through practice? How does the perfection of morality become fulfilled? How does the perfection of patience become fulfilled? How does the perfection of vigor become fulfilled? How does the perfection of meditation become fulfilled? How does the perfection of wisdom become fulfilled?

body.text: bhagavān āha: iha kauśika bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dānaṃ dadat na dāyakam upalabhate na dānaṃ pratigrāhakam upalabhate, na śīlaṃ rakṣan na śīlaṃ na śīlasamādānam upalabhate, na kṣāntiṃ bhāvayan na kṣāntiṃ rakṣanti bhāvanām upalabhate, na vīryam ārabhamāṇe na vīryāraṃbham upalabhate, na dhyānāni na dhyānabhāvanām upalabhate, na prajñāṃ na prajmbhāvanām upalabhate, evaṃ carataḥ kauśika bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya dānapāramitā paripūryate śīlapāramitā paripūryate kṣāntipāramitā paripūryate vīryapāramitā paripūryate dhyānapāramitā paripūryate prajñāpāramitā paripūryate.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Here, <s>Kauśika</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while giving a gift, does not apprehend a giver, does not apprehend the gift, and does not apprehend a recipient. While guarding morality, he does not apprehend morality, nor the undertaking of morality. While cultivating patience, he does not apprehend patience, nor the cultivation of patience. While exerting vigor, he does not apprehend the exertion of vigor. He does not apprehend the meditative absorptions, nor the cultivation of meditation. He does not apprehend wisdom, nor the cultivation of wisdom. For one who practices in this way, <s>Kauśika</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s perfection of giving is fulfilled, the perfection of morality is fulfilled, the perfection of patience is fulfilled, the perfection of vigor is fulfilled, the perfection of meditation is fulfilled, the perfection of wisdom is fulfilled.

body.text: evaṃ khalu kauśika kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā abudhyamānasya prajñāpāramitā sārthā savyañjanām upadeṣṭavyā, evam abudhyamānasya dhyānapāramitā sārthā savyañjanam upadeṣṭavyā, evam abudhyamānasya vīryapāramitā sārthā savyañjanam upadeṣṭavyā, evam abudhyamānasya kṣāntipāramitā sārthā savyañjanam upadeṣṭavyā, evam abudhyamānasya śīlapāramitā sārthā savyañjanam upadeṣṭavyā, evam abudhyamānasya (

<s>Śakra</s> said: What, Blessed One, is the counterfeit (<s>prativarṇikā</s>) of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?

body.text: śakra āha: katamā bhagavan prajñāpāramitā prativarṇikā?
bhagavān āha: iha kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prajñāpāramitām upadekṣyāma iti, te prativarṇikā upadekṣyati.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Here, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family, thinking 'I shall teach the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' will teach a counterfeit.

body.text: śakra āha: kathaṃ bhagavaṃs te kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaro yā prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikām upadekṣyanti?
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: How, Blessed One, will those sons of good family and daughters of good family teach a counterfeit of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?

body.text: bhagavān āha: iha kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prajñāpāramitām upadiśantaḥ, prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikām upadekṣyanti, tatra yā prajñāpāramitāyāḥ prativarṇikā, yad uta rūpam anityam ity upadekṣyanti, rūpaṃ duḥkham ity upadekṣyanti, rūpam anātmety upadekṣyanti, rūpam aśubham ity upadekṣyanti.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Here, <s>Kauśika</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family, while teaching the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will teach a counterfeit of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. That which is a counterfeit of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is this: they will teach that form (<s>rūpa</s>) is impermanent, they will teach that form is suffering, they will teach that form is without self, they will teach that form is impure.

body.text: evaṃ ca vakṣyanti ya evaṃ carati sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratīti yeṣāṃ copadekṣyanti, te rūpam anityam iti gaveṣiṣyante, rūpaṃ duḥkham iti gaveṣiṣyante, rūpam anātmeti gaveṣiṣyante, rūpam aśubham iti gaveṣiṣyante, te rūpam anityam iti gaveṣamāṇāḥ, rūpaṃ duḥkham iti gaveṣamāṇāḥ, rūpam anātmeti gaveṣamāṇāḥ, rūpam aśubham iti gaveṣamāṇāḥ prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikāyāṃ cariṣyanti,
body.translated_text: And they will say thus: 'Whoever practices in this way practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, those sons and daughters of good family instruct those sons and daughters of good family who follow the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> thus: 'Come, son of good family, cultivate the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Being, cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, you will enter the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s certainty of attainment (<s>bodhisattvanyāma</s>), you will attain patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (<s>anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣānti</s>). Being, having attained patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas and established in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), you will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones.' Those who do not instruct thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, those sons and daughters of good family will not be teaching a counterfeit of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (<s>prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā</s>).

body.text: śakra āha: katham upadiśanto bhagavaṃs te kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca teṣāṃ bodhisattvayānikānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ vā na prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikām upadekṣyanti?
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said: 'How, Blessed One, should those sons and daughters of good family instruct those sons and daughters of good family who follow the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle so that they will not be teaching a counterfeit of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (<s>prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā</s>)?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: iha kauśika kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca teṣāṃ bodhisattvayānikānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ caivaṃ prajñāpāramitām upadekṣyanti. ehi tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvaya mā ca rūpam anityam iti samanupaśyaḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ? rūpaṃ svabhāvaśūnyaṃ yo rūpasya svabhāvaḥ so 'bhūvaḥ sā prajñāpāramitāyā prajñāpāramitā na tatra rūpaṃ nitya iti vā anityam iti copalabhyate, rūpam eva na saṃvidyate nopalabhate. kutaḥ punar nityaṃ vā anityaṃ vā bbaviṣyanti, evam upadiśantaḥ kauśika te kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaro vā na prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikām upadekṣyanti.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Kauśika</s>, sons and daughters of good family will instruct those sons and daughters of good family who follow the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> thus: Come, son of good family, cultivate the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, but do not regard form (<s>rūpa</s>) as impermanent. For what reason? Form is empty of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnya</s>). That which is the inherent nature of form — that is non-existence. That is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. In the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, form is apprehended neither as permanent nor as impermanent. Form itself is not found, is not apprehended. How then could it be permanent or impermanent? Those who instruct thus, <s>Kauśika</s>, those sons or daughters of good family, will not be teaching a counterfeit of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (<s>prajñāpāramitāprativarṇikā</s>).'

body.text: tiṣṭhantu kauśika trisāhasre mahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ pratyekabodhau pratiṣṭhāpitā yāvantaḥ kauśika daśasu dikṣv ekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvās tān kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā pratyekabodhau pratiṣṭhāpayet. tat kiṃ manyase? kauśikāpi nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahupuṇyaṃ prasavet.
body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the beings in the threefold-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system established in <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>. Would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit on that account?

body.text: bhagavān āha: ataḥ sa kauśika kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet, ya imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ sārthāṃ savyañjanāṃ parebhyo vistareṇācakṣīt deśayet prakāśayed vicared vibhajed uttānīkuryāt saṃprakāśayet, evaṃ ca vaded, ehi tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitām udgṛhāṇa paryavāpnuhy ādhāraya dhāraya vācaya yoniśaś ca manasikuru yathopadiṣṭāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pratipadyasva. yadā tvaṃ kulaputra yathopadiṣṭāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pratipatsyase. tadā tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāṃ śikṣiṣyase, yadā tvaṃ kulaputra prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣiṣyase, tadā tvaṃ sarvadharmān pratilapsyase, yadā tvaṃ sarvadharmān pratilapsyase, tadā te prajñāpāramitā bhūyasyā mātrayā bhāvanāparipūriṃ gamiṣyati, yadā te prajñāpāramitā bhūyasyā mātrayā bhāvanāparipuriṃ gamiṣyati tadā tvam anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyase. tat kasya hetoḥ? ato niryātā hi kauśika prathamacittotpādikā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ.
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'That son or daughter of good family, <s>Kauśika</s>, would generate even more merit — the one who would explain this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with its meaning and letter to others in detail, would teach, illuminate, expound, analyze, elucidate, and make it clear, and would say thus: Come, son of good family, take up the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, master it, retain it, bear it in mind, recite it, attend to it wisely, and practice in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as it has been taught. When you, son of good family, practice in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as it has been taught, then you, son of good family, will be training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. When you, son of good family, train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, then you will attain all dharmas. When you attain all dharmas, then your <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will reach the fullness of cultivation to an even greater degree. When your <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> reaches the fullness of cultivation to an even greater degree, then you will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect and complete awakening.' For what reason? For from this, <s>Kauśika</s>, have come forth the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who first generate the thought of awakening.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kauśika</s>, suppose some son or daughter of good family were to establish as many beings as there are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> on the stage of non-regression (<s>avaivartyabhūmi</s>). What do you think, <s>Kauśika</s>? Would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit on that account?

And suppose one among those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> were to say thus: 'Come, quickly fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening!' — yet that son or daughter of good family who would fully instruct him in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with its meaning and letter in detail, that very son or daughter of good family would generate even greater merit.

body.text: tiṣṭhantu kauśika trisāhasre mahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvā avaivartikā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, yāvantaḥ kauśika daśasu dikṣv ekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvās te sarva avaivartikā bhaveyur anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau tebhyo bodhisattvebhyo mahāsattvebhyaḥ, kaścid eva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ punyaṃ prasavet. tat kasya hetoḥ? avaivartikebhyo hi bodhisattvebhyo nānyārthaṃ dharmam upadeṣṭavyo niyatā hi te saṃbodhi parāyaṇānate bhuyo vivartittite anuttarāyā samyaksaṃbodher ayam abhū kaścic citaḥ saṃsārāt mahākaruṇāsaṃpīḍitaś ca.
body.translated_text: Set aside, <s>Kauśika</s>, the beings of the three-thousand great-thousand-fold world-system who are irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening. However many beings there are, <s>Kauśika</s>, in each of the ten directions, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> — suppose all of them were irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening — that son or daughter of good family who would instruct those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> [in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] would generate even greater merit. For what reason? Because for irreversible <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, no other teaching need be given; they are certainly destined for awakening, yet they will never turn back from unsurpassed perfect awakening — this was something once considered — and they are impelled by great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>).

Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: In proportion as, Blessed One, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> draws near to unsurpassed perfect awakening, so should that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> be admonished and instructed in the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>); so should he be admonished and instructed in the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>); so should he be admonished and instructed in the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>); so should he be admonished and instructed in the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>); so should he be admonished and instructed in the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>); so should he be admonished and instructed in the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: tasmād bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisambudhyate, anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaiḥ sarvalokadhātuṣu naraka ucchidyante tiryagyoni ucchidyante yamaloka ucchidyante, āsurāś ca kāyā parihīyante divyāṃs ca kāyā abhivartante, kṣatriyamahāśālakulānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, brāhmaṇamahāśālakulānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati, gṛhapatimahāśālakulānāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati.
body.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect and full awakening. When one has fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect and full awakening, in all world-systems the hells (<s>naraka</s>) are cut off, the animal realm (<s>tiryagyoni</s>) is cut off, the world of <s>Yama</s> is cut off, the bodies of <s>Asuras</s> diminish, and the divine bodies (<s>divyakāya</s>) increase. There arises in the world the appearance of great <s>Kṣatriya</s> families, there arises in the world the appearance of great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> families, and there arises in the world the appearance of great householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>) families.

body.translated_text: There arises in the world the appearance of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the powers (<s>bala</s>), the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>), the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>), the gates of liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s>), the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), the gates of <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>). There arises in the world the appearance of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle).
